本文由中国工程院院士刘吉臻撰写，围绕《新型电力系统建设“十五五”规划》核心要求，系统阐述了我国电源结构绿色低碳转型的总体方向与实施路径。文章指出，“十五五”是我国实现碳达峰的关键期，须统筹发展与安全，坚持多能并举、协同转型。核心任务包括：加快构建以非化石能源为主体的电力供给格局，推动其在装机与发电量上均成为“双主体”；分类推进风电、光伏等新能源多场景开发与消纳，强化跨区外送与就地利用协同；科学开发水电、积极安全有序发展核电、因地制宜发展光热、生物质等多元清洁能源；同步推进煤电结构优化与节能降碳改造，兼顾兜底保障与深度减排，并探索煤电与新能源融合、零碳燃料掺烧及CCUS等前沿技术路径，全面支撑绿色低碳电力供给体系加快形成。（199字）
云南楚雄罗海营光伏发电项目近日实现全容量并网发电，正式投产运营。该项目位于禄丰市碧城镇，是楚雄百万千瓦级“风光储一体化”新能源基地的重点工程，装机容量35兆瓦（安装容量43.9兆瓦），配套新建35千伏开关站，占地约730亩。由中国电建昆明院牵头EPC总承包、水电十五局施工。项目年均发电量约5996万千瓦时，每年可节约标准煤1.76万吨、减排二氧化碳4.62万吨。其清洁电力将增强区域电网供应能力，支撑工业低碳转型与山区乡村振兴。建设过程中，团队克服山地施工复杂等困难，优化方案、强化协同，并同步改善乡村道路、落实水土保持，践行央企社会责任。
杭锦旗110万千瓦风光一体化项目近日实现全容量并网发电，正式投入商业运营。该项目位于内蒙古鄂尔多斯市杭锦旗，是“三北”工程生态能源融合发展的示范工程，总装机110万千瓦（光伏80万千瓦、风电30万千瓦）。项目创新采用“板上发电、板下种植、治沙改土”立体开发模式，依托光伏阵列改善沙地微气候，促进植被恢复与生态治理同步推进。施工中应用光伏组件智能安装机器人，显著提升效率与安全性。投运后，年均发电约24亿千瓦时，可节约标准煤73万吨、减排二氧化碳约200万吨，有力支撑区域能源结构优化、绿色电力外送及国家重要能源基地与北方生态安全屏障建设。
2026年上半年，我国煤电发电量占比历史性降至49.7%，首次低于50%，标志着电力系统结构性转型进入新阶段。同期，可再生能源发电量达近2万亿千瓦时，占总发电量的41.2%，其中风电与太阳能合计超1.2万亿千瓦时；可再生能源装机达24.55亿千瓦，占总装机约60.7%。新能源已从“补充能源”跃升为“电量主体”，而煤电正转向保障性、调节性角色。《可再生能源发展“十五五”规划》明确，到2030年非化石能源发电量占比将超50%，并强调“可靠替代”与系统支撑能力提升。转型带来能源安全增强、产业升级加速和“双碳”目标推进，同时也面临电网稳定性、储能技术及市场机制等挑战。
2025年，德国风电与光伏发电量达225太瓦时（占总发电量44%），首次超过化石燃料发电量（217太瓦时，占43%），标志着其能源转型（Energiewende）的重要里程碑。这一进展源于二十年来风光装机的持续扩张，也与德国坚定推进弃核、逐步退煤政策密切相关。政府设定目标：2030年陆上风电装机达115吉瓦，可再生能源供电占比达80%；2035年建成基本气候中和的电力系统；2045年实现全经济领域净零排放。为支撑转型，2025年新增风光装机创纪录达20.8吉瓦。当前挑战包括煤电退出（最晚2038年，或提前完成）、燃气电厂作为过渡并计划转向绿氢运行，以及德国选择党等政治力量对转型路径的反对。8月即将发布的退煤时间表评估报告，将成为检验政策执行力的关键节点。（199字）
阿曼Nama电力与水务采购公司（Nama PWP）启动编号为OPWP/2026/033的招标，面向全球遴选财务与商业顾问，以支持其开发三个各1GW、总计3GW的公用事业级光伏独立发电厂（IPP）项目。这些项目将接入阿曼主互联系统（MIS），计划于2030年第二季度投入商业运营，是该国推进电力结构多元化、提升清洁能源占比的重要举措。顾问职责涵盖项目前期开发阶段的财务建模、风险评估、商业模式设计，并全程协助组织竞争性招标流程。招标文件发放时间为2026年7月28日至8月6日，投标截止日期为2026年9月10日。此举与Nama PWP此前就技术顾问开展的招标及阿曼电力传输公司（OETC）提出的2030年前新增超5GW光伏装机目标相协同。
自8月1日起，一批新修订和制定的国家标准正式实施，涵盖光伏发电、节能减排、水资源管理、新能源应用、前沿技术及民生服务等多个领域。其中，光伏发电系列标准明确了系统建模、参数测试与并网运行控制的技术要求，为大规模光伏接入电网提供模型支撑和调度依据；煤炭开采与甲醛能耗限额等强制性标准推动高耗能行业节能降耗；黄河流域用水定额标准覆盖工业与服务业，强化区域水资源刚性约束；家用太阳能热水系统标准提升产品能效与质量；脑机接口、数字孪生、北斗应用等新兴领域标准统一架构、数据格式与技术接口，助力产业化发展；绿色产品评价标准从多维度规范钢管等建材的绿色属性；旅游服务标准则聚焦购物场所质量、无障碍设施及老年旅游安全，提升服务可及性与规范性。整体上，这批标准旨在支撑高质量发展、绿色低碳转型与人民生活品质提升。（199字）
余姚宝湾物流中心建成3.84MW屋顶光伏电站，采用尤利卡550W单玻组件，年发绿电370万度，降本260万元、减碳1980吨，成功斩获国家一级绿色仓库认证。项目精准适配姚江高湿工况，轻量耐候、高效稳定，彰显光伏赋能传统物流绿色升级的标杆价值。
中广核宁德200兆瓦海上光伏项目于7月31日实现全容量并网发电，是福建省首批海上光伏项目之一，也是中广核首个“核光同场”示范工程。项目位于福鼎市太姥山镇宁德核电站水区范围内，占地约3020亩，配套20兆瓦/40兆瓦时储能系统及12公里220千伏送出线路（含闽东最高138米跨海输电铁塔）。运行期25年预计年均上网电量3亿千瓦时，可年减标煤约9.13万吨、减排二氧化碳约19.8万吨。建设中攻克近海腐蚀、成本高等难题，自主研发大直径混凝土管桩与轻量化支架体系，降低总体建设成本超10%，形成可复制的近海光伏技术方案。项目探索核电与光伏协同开发路径，助力区域零碳园区建设与国家“双碳”目标实现。
华能满城300MW林光互补项目二标段（装机容量70MW）近日实现首批光伏组件成功并网发电，标志着该项目建设取得关键性进展。项目位于河北保定满城区石井乡山地片区，地形复杂、岩层裸露、高差大、场地分散，且施工范围涉及村落、景区、柿子林及临近高速、南水北调工程等敏感区域，征地协调难、审批流程繁、交叉作业多、运输与施工组织挑战突出。中国安能一局辽宁公司项目部通过科学排产、资源优化、全过程精细化管控和重点工序跟踪，克服山地施工、气象多变、安全风险高等困难，如期完成首批并网目标。项目后续将全力推进剩余工程建设，力争实现全容量并网，助力区域绿色能源转型与生态经济协同发展。（198字）

title: 市场回温！上半年全球光伏企业融资总额同比增长 56%-索比光伏网
content:
Mercom Capital Group 最新报告显示，2026 年上半年全球光伏行业企业融资总额从 2025 年同期的 108 亿美元增长至 169 亿美元，同比涨幅达 56%。
尽管风险投资（VC）金额有所下降，但在强劲的债权融资和资本市场融资活动的推动下，行业整体融资规模仍实现显著增长。
Mercom 报告显示，2026 年上半年全球光伏企业融资总额同比增长 56%，达到 169 亿美元。（图片来源：Mercom Capital Group）
该报告题为《2026 年上半年及第二季度光伏融资与并购报告（1H and Q2 2026 Solar Funding and M&A Report）》，报告期内企业并购（M&A）活动和大型光伏项目收购活动均较去年同期有所增加。这一增长态势与 2025 年上半年形成对比，当时全球光伏企业融资总额曾同比下降 39% 至 108 亿美元。
在各类融资渠道中，债权融资和公开市场融资成为增长的主要驱动力。其中，已披露的债权融资通过 44 笔交易共筹集 132 亿美元，较 2025 年同期的 78 亿美元增长 69%；公开市场融资则通过 17 笔交易募集 22 亿美元，较 2025 年上半年的 4.67 亿美元激增 371%。同时，并购市场也表现活跃，上半年录得 57 笔企业交易，高于去年同期的 50 笔。
风险投资领域在报告期内出现下滑，VC 融资额同比下降 40% 至 15 亿美元，涉及 35 笔交易，而 2025 年同期为 32 笔交易筹集 25 亿美元。尽管总金额下降，但交易笔数有所增加，且光伏下游企业仍是投资重点，22 笔 VC 交易涉及 8.84 亿美元。其中最大的 VC 融资案例包括 Inox Clean Energy（3.43 亿美元）、Nexamp（1.8 亿美元）、Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions（1.65 亿美元）、Amarenco（1.5 亿美元）以及 GREW Solar（1.18 亿美元）。
证券化融资在 2026 年上半年表现低迷，3 笔交易总价值为 5.4 亿美元，较去年同期的 4 笔交易（共 16 亿美元）下降了 66%。

作为弘元绿能高效组件智能制造的重要生产基地，江阴基地始终坚持以数字化、智能化赋能制造升级，持续推进智能工厂建设，围绕研发设计、生产制造、质量管控、设备运维、仓储物流等关键环节，加快构建覆盖全业务流程的数字化运营体系，不断提升制造效率、质量水平和运营能力。
基地深度融合工业互联网、自动化生产装备及数字化管理平台，推动生产计划、工艺控制、设备管理、质量检测等核心业务协同运行，实现产品全生命周期数字化管理。同时，通过智能物流、在线监测、数据分析等数字化应用，持续提升制造能力和供应链协同能力，为高品质产品稳定交付提供坚实保障。
近年来，公司持续推进智能制造场景建设，在智能排产、在线检测、设备运维、能源管理等方面不断探索数字化应用，逐步形成覆盖生产全过程的智能制造体系，为企业数字化转型积累了丰富实践经验，也打造出具有行业示范意义的智能制造新模式。
全流程数字化管控
构建质量可追溯体系
质量是智能制造的核心，也是企业高质量发展的生命线。弘元绿能始终坚持“质量贯穿全生命周期”理念，依托数字化管理平台，构建覆盖原材料入厂、生产制造、在线检测、成品交付等全过程的质量管理体系，实现产品全生命周期质量信息数字化管理。
依托全过程数据采集和信息互联，产品生产过程中的关键工艺参数、检测结果及质量信息均实现数字化记录和全过程留存，建立起完整的产品质量档案，实现产品来源可查、过程可控、质量可溯，不断提升产品一致性和可靠性，为全球客户提供更加稳定、可靠的产品解决方案。
与此同时，公司持续推进标准化、精益化管理，通过数字化手段实现质量持续优化，推动质量管理由事后管控向全过程预防转变，以智能制造持续夯实产品竞争力。
绘就低碳制造新图景
智能制造不仅提升生产效率，也为绿色低碳发展提供重要支撑。弘元绿能始终坚持绿色发展理念，将节能降耗、能源优化和资源高效利用融入生产制造全过程，推动智能制造与绿色制造深度融合。
江阴基地积极推进绿色能源应用，建设35MW屋顶分布式光伏项目，预计年发电量约3500万千瓦时，通过利用清洁能源助力基地绿色生产，进一步提升可再生能源应用水平，推动制造过程向低碳化、绿色化方向升级。
智造成果加速转化
创新产品走向全球
智能制造能力最终要转化为产品竞争力和市场价值。今年，弘元绿能自主研发推出的HT 3.0高效四分片组件在江阴基地正式下线，并快速实现规模化量产。依托先进智能制造体系和全过程质量管控能力，产品实现研发、制造、检测、交付等环节高效协同，在保障产品一致性和可靠性的同时，有效提升了产品交付能力。
目前，HT 3.0高效四分片组件已实现大批量出货，产品陆续发往欧洲、澳新、日本等海外市场，以更优的发电性能、更高的可靠性和更具竞争力的系统价值，持续获得全球客户认可，充分展现了弘元绿能智能制造赋能产品创新和全球化发展的综合实力。
从绿色工厂到先进级智能工厂，从数字化升级到智能制造跃迁，弘元绿能始终坚持创新驱动发展，以智能制造培育新质生产力，以绿色制造引领产业升级。未来，公司将持续深化数字化、智能化、绿色化融合发展，不断提升先进制造能力和全球市场竞争力，为新能源产业高质量发展和全球能源绿色低碳转型贡献更多弘元力量。

科幻航天剧《太阳系公民》在通威光伏基地实景拍摄，首次以工业美学镜头全景展现中国光伏智造硬实力：5G+AI调度、AGV无人车、智能机械臂协同作业的数字化产线。该剧为中宣部“十五五”重点文艺项目、中国航天70周年献礼剧，巧妙串联地面新能源与深空探索，彰显光伏产业支撑国家战略的科技担当。

爱旭“珠海担杆岛零碳示范项目”入选工信部智能光伏典型案例。项目首创“风光储充与柴备一体化”微电网，建成208kW光伏+25kW风电系统，年发绿电超25万度，用电成本从3元/度降至0.6元/度，年减碳105吨，实现海岛24小时清洁稳定供电。

title: 晶科、晋能、晶澳、旭合、TCL中环、东方日升等8家企业入围！潞安太阳能年度集采中标候选人公示-索比光伏网
content:
8月4日，山西潞安太阳能科技有限责任公司光伏组件、组件物资年度招标采购（001标段）中标候选人公示。
根据公示信息，入围候选人名单的企业包括晶科能源、晋能科技、恒曦光副、晶澳科技、旭合科技、三一硅能、TCL中环、东方日升等8家企业。
根据招标公告，本项目招标人为山西潞安太阳能科技有限责任公司，投标人要求提供光伏组件的供货业绩累计不少于500MW，至少有一个合同不少于50MW。

title: 道达尔能源收购壳牌欧洲4GW可再生能源资产-索比光伏网
content:
道达尔能源（TotalEnergies）正以未公开的价格收购壳牌（Shell）在欧洲的陆上可再生能源业务，该业务包括分布在四个欧洲国家的运营资产和数 GW 的项目储备。与此同时，道达尔能源还宣布向 KKR 部分出售已开发的可再生能源资产。
道达尔能源表示，与壳牌及 KKR 达成的两项交易与其综合电力战略高度契合。（图片来源：TotalEnergies）
这家法国能源巨头已签署协议收购壳牌在欧洲的陆上可再生能源业务，同时另行同意向投资公司 KKR 出售一组已开发可再生能源资产组合 50% 的股权。从壳牌收购的资产包括位于意大利、荷兰、西班牙和英国的 500MW 已运营或在建的光伏及风电资产，以及 3.5GW 的光伏、风电和电池储能系统（BESS）项目储备。道达尔能源表示，此次收购将扩大其在这四个欧洲市场的发电业务。交易完成后，道达尔能源在欧洲的可再生能源总装机容量或在建容量将达到近 10GW，另有 27GW 正处于开发阶段。
在开展收购的同时，道达尔能源已同意将一个 1.2GW 陆上光伏和风电组合项目的 50% 股权出售给由 KKR 管理的保险账户。该后期开发阶段资产组合的资产组合企业价值为 18 亿欧元，包括位于德国、西班牙、法国和波兰的资产。道达尔能源将在交易完成后保留剩余 50% 的股份并继续运营这些资产。这两项交易均预计在 2026 年底前完成，但须获得监管部门和惯例批准。
道达尔能源天然气、可再生能源及电力业务总裁 Stéphane Michel 表示，这两项交易符合公司战略，能够优化在可再生能源领域的资本配置，同时继续推进其综合电力战略。该公司的目标是到 2030 年实现 100TWh 的发电量，其中约 70% 来自可再生能源，30% 来自灵活发电。Michel 解释称，壳牌的交易扩大了道达尔能源在欧洲战略性去监管市场的可再生能源组合，而 KKR 的交易则通过成熟资产变现来回收资本，支持其综合电力增长战略。由于道达尔能源目前正专注于该地区的大型风电和光伏资产，该公司近期已出售了其在欧洲的分布式光伏业务。
对于壳牌而言，此次出售反映了其在 2025 年资本市场日宣布的积极管理电力组合的战略，旨在将资本引导至其认为具有更强长期价值的领域。壳牌的目标是每年向其下游、可再生能源和能源解决方案业务投资约 80 亿美元，同时每年为综合天然气和上游部门预留 120 亿至 140 亿美元。壳牌下游、可再生能源和能源解决方案业务总裁 Machteld de Haan 表示，公司正在重新配置资本，并优先考虑具有差异化能力且能随时间创造最大价值的领域，包括通过资产支持的电力交易和以客户为中心的能源解决方案。此前，壳牌曾以 18 亿美元的价格将其在印度 Sprng Energy 的控股公司 Solenergi Power 的全部股份出售给了 Aditya Birla Renewables。

title: 阳光电源：以电力电子技术立身，引领全球清洁能源功率变换-索比光伏网
content:
在全球能源转型加速推进的背景下，光伏、风电、储能等新能源装机规模持续扩大。连接发电侧与电网侧的“核心枢纽”，正是电力电子技术——它将电压、频率不稳定的清洁能源，转换为可并网、可调度的优质电力。可以说，新能源时代“发得出”靠资源，“用得好”靠电力电子。
作为光伏逆变器、风电变流器与储能系统的全球领军企业，阳光电源股份有限公司（Sungrow）自1997年创立以来，始终以电力电子功率变换为核心主业，践行“让人人享用清洁电力”的企业使命，致力于“成为清洁电力转换技术全球引领者”。本文从企业概况、核心技术体系、旗舰产品、核心优势、研发与全球化五个维度，系统呈现这家电力电子技术企业的硬核实力。
电力电子技术（Power Electronics）是利用半导体功率器件对电能进行高效变换与控制的工程技术，典型产品包括光伏逆变器、风电变流器、储能变流器（PCS）等，是风光储系统接入电网的“技术中枢”。据阳光电源公开信息，截至2025年底，其电力电子转换设备全球累计装机量已突破1000吉瓦。在新能源装机持续增长的背景下，高可靠功率变换设备的需求正被不断放大。
一、企业概况：深耕电力电子二十余载
阳光电源股份有限公司成立于1997年，总部位于安徽合肥。公司业务覆盖光伏逆变器、风电变流及传动、储能系统、充电设备、新能源汽车电控及电源系统、氢能装备、AIDC电源等多元场景，形成“光、风、储、电、氢”一体化的清洁能源版图。截至目前，其产品及服务已累计销往全球100多个国家和地区，构建起覆盖全球的研发、制造与服务网络。
在全球能源转型浪潮中，阳光电源并非“偏科选手”——在光伏逆变器、风电变流器、储能系统三大功率变换赛道上同步保持全球领先，是名副其实的“三料冠军”。2024年，光伏逆变器出货量蝉联全球第一；风电变流器全球出货量连续多年位居榜首；储能系统累计装机量同样位列全球第一。
作为一家以技术立身的企业，阳光电源秉持“诚恳务实、严谨开放、创新尊重、成就客户”的品牌价值观，以“灵动创新的清洁能源专家”为品牌主旨，践行“连接绿色使命，共筑持续价值”的价值主张，将使命贯穿于研发、制造与服务的每一个环节。
二、核心技术体系：从功率器件到系统级构网
阳光电源的技术能力贯穿“器件—拓扑—系统—电网”四个层级，构建了完整的技术纵深：
功率变换平台覆盖kW级组串式到MW级集中式产品，全面适配1500V系统，支持多路MPPT独立跟踪，最大化每一块组件的发电收益。
宽禁带器件应用方面，PowerTitan 3.0储能系统首次规模化采用全液冷碳化硅（SiC）功率器件，PCS最大效率达99.3%。碳化硅的高频特性相比传统IGBT可降低开关损耗约30%，在高温工况下效率优势更为显著。
构网型（Grid-forming）技术方面，PowerTitan 3.0搭载下一代“干细胞”构网技术，不仅能提前预判电网波动，在跟踪模式与构网模式间无缝切换，支持吉瓦级电网黑启动，更可在20毫秒内快速响应电网强度变化。阳光电源已完成全球最大构网型储能项目——沙特7.8GWh项目的全容量并网。
系统级创新层面，2026年SNEC展会上，阳光电源重磅发布PowerMatrix™矩阵逆变器，并同步推出以其为核心的矩阵逆变系统。该系统是实现光伏、储能、电网、负荷一体协同控制的全新品类，突破了传统系统架构分散耦合、能量流动路径单一、协同能力弱等局限，依托“多端口一体化、光储原生融合、分层协同控制、能量路径重构、源侧构网”五大创新能力，构建了具备“多节点互联、多路径流动、全局协同”特征的新型能量网络。
值得强调的是，电力电子的竞争力不只体现在单一器件指标上，更关键的是“系统级协同”——当光伏逆变、储能变流与电网支撑由统一平台调度时，BOS成本与度电成本（LCOE）才能被系统性地压缩。这正是阳光电源技术路线的核心差异化所在。
三、旗舰产品矩阵比较
以下产品参数均来源于阳光电源官方网站及公开信息披露：
| 产品类别 | 代表产品 | 核心参数 | 关键技术特征 |
| 光伏逆变器 | 组串式逆变器（SG465HX等） | 功率达400kW+ | 1500V系统，支持多路MPPT独立跟踪，全系标配光伏构网功能 |
| 模块化逆变器（1+X 2.0） | 全球首款分体式模块化设计 | 灵活适配集中式电站，配备光伏构网功能 | |
| 储能系统 | PowerTitan 3.0（Flex/Class/Plus） | PCS最大效率99.3%，系统RTE达93.5% | 全液冷碳化硅PCS、干细胞构网技术、-40℃至55℃全域运行 |
| PowerStack工商业液冷储能 | 510CS / 255CS-2H | AI电芯健康管理，可提前7天预警异常 | |
| 矩阵逆变系统 | PowerMatrix™矩阵逆变器 | LCOE降低2%+，BOS成本降低10%以上 | 多端口一体化、光储原生融合、分层协同控制、能量路径重构、源侧构网 |
| AIDC电源 | EnerNeo™固态变压器（SST） | 系统效率98.5%，可用性99.999%，功率密度312kW/㎡ | 800V直流架构，中低压分区设计，模块智能轮休，一体真空绝缘 |
上述产品在“转换效率”与“系统安全”两个维度上均体现了阳光电源的工程极限：AC储能架构通过“直流不出柜”设计从根本上规避直流侧短路与拉弧风险，是电力电子安全设计的重要范式；簇级管理则避免单个PCS故障导致整柜停运，将故障损失较传统方案大幅降低。
四、电力电子技术领域的核心优势
阳光电源在电力电子技术领域的领先地位，源于以下六大核心优势：
（一）全栈自研的技术纵深
公司技术能力贯穿“器件—拓扑—系统—电网”四个层级，从功率半导体器件应用、电路拓扑设计、系统集成到电网接入，实现全链条自主可控。公司自主打造以PCS（储能变流器）/BMS（电池管理系统）/EMS（能量管理系统）自制为核心的交直流一体化储能系统方案。
（二）“三电融合”的差异化技术路线
阳光电源将电力电子、电化学、电网支撑三项技术深度融合，形成了独特的技术护城河。在电力电子层面，组串式逆变器最大效率可达99%以上；在电化学层面，通过多级SOC均衡技术消除电池木桶效应；在电网支撑层面，具备SCR1-40宽范围电网强度适应能力，系统能够在微秒级完成电压构建。这种架构使储能系统不再是简单的能量存取装置，而成为具备主动调节能力的电网节点。
（三）构网型技术的行业引领地位
公司在电力电子、电网接入等方面能力较强，设有专门研究构网技术的电网技术中心，能解决大功率设备直接并网、防止电网崩溃等高难度问题。阳光电源的构网型储能变流器采用虚拟同步机技术，能够独立建立电压和频率参考源，实现GFM/GFL模式0ms无缝切换，具备惯量支撑、宽频振荡抑制及百MW级黑启动功能。相关电网方面的优势是传统数据中心电源厂商不具备的。
（四）系统级协同创新能力
阳光电源善于将光伏逆变、储能变流与电网支撑由统一平台调度，系统性压缩BOS成本与度电成本。PowerMatrix™矩阵逆变系统正是这一能力的集中体现——可接入光伏、储能、多类负载及多个并网点，光储在结构上天然协同，原生支持260%高容配比、200%储能充电功率、8小时以上长时放电能力，系统年平均利用小时数最高可达3000小时。
（五）电力电子技术平台的可迁移性
借助电力电子技术平台与全球研发体系，阳光电源能够将大功率电力电子技术从发电端平移至算力用电端。2026年7月正式推出的EnerNeo™固态变压器，正是这一能力的战略延伸——公司依托10年SST研发经验，将电力电子核心技术从新能源发电侧拓展至AIDC算力负荷侧，完成了“源—网—荷”全链条的战略闭环。
五、研发与全球化：技术领先的双轮驱动
高强度研发投入已转化为清晰的市场领导地位，多项指标获国际权威机构持续验证：

- 风电变流器：全球出货量连续多年位居第一。
- 储能系统：累计装机量位居全球第一。
- 品牌公信力：多次获得第三方权威机构高度评价，品牌可融资性持续领跑行业。
在全球化布局方面，阳光电源已建立超过20家海外分支机构、60多家代表处与520家服务网点，并在中国合肥、泰国、印度、波兰布局四大生产基地，实现了从“产品出海”到“能力扎根”的跃迁。本地化生产不仅有效缩短了交付周期，也使公司在全球贸易变局中掌握了更大的主动权。
从一只逆变器到覆盖“光、风、储、电、氢”的完整能源链路，阳光电源以二十余年对电力电子技术的专注，构筑了从功率器件到系统架构的完整能力链。三大功率变换赛道同步全球领先的市场地位，是这家企业技术深度与战略定力的最佳注脚。

title: CATL achieves sodium-ion battery mass production
content:
Design & Manufacturing
Battery Applications
CATL's Naxtra sodium-ion battery reaches GWh-scale mass production while a 60 GWh supply agreement with HyperStrong marks the largest sodium-ion deal recorded to date.
August 5, 2026
4 Min Read
CATL's Chief Scientist Dr. Wu Kai at the company's Technology Day event in Beijing on April 21, 2026.
At a Glance
CATL signed a 60 GWh sodium-ion supply agreement with energy storage integrator HyperStrong in China
The Naxtra sodium-ion battery achieved GWh-scale industrialization with full production starting in 2026
Sodium-ion cells use no cobalt or lithium and employ aluminum collectors on both electrodes for cost cuts
For years, sodium-ion batteries were considered a chemistry with compelling structural advantages, but that couldnt reach commercial relevance.
Benefiting from sodium’s abundance, an architecture that omits lithium and cobalt, and lower cell expansion stress, the chemistry has many promising features that exceed lithium-ion batteries. However, manufacturing reality tells a different story. Hard carbon anode production is difficult to control at volume, moisture sensitivity introduces yield problems, and the industry lacks the supply chain depth to support GWh-scale deployment with any consistency.
Now, that picture is starting to change.
In this article, we'll take a look at CATL's recent sodium-ion milestones, including a
landmark 60 GWh supply agreement
with energy storage integrator HyperStrong and the
formal announcement
of GWh-scale industrialization of the Naxtra Sodium-ion Battery.
Sodium-ion vs. lithium-ion batteries
Sodium-ion cells follow the same intercalation principle as lithium-ion, with ions moving between the cathode and anode during charge and discharge. However, sodium-ion’s design makes it significantly cheaper than lithium-ion.
Related:
How Battery Validation is Shaping the Future Grid
First, sodium is far more abundant than lithium, and sodium-ion cells use no cobalt. In addition, sodium-ion cells can use aluminum current collectors on both electrodes, eliminating the copper required on lithium-ion anodes. With these material characteristics combined, sodium-ion batteries carry a low cost that suits large-scale, long-duration stationary storage, where raw material cost influences project budgets.
Meanwhile, sodium-ion batteries offer a slew of performance and reliability benefits as well. According to the
American Physical Society
, sodium-ion cells tolerate wider temperature ranges than conventional lithium-ion chemistries, maintain cycle stability at high ambient temperatures, and generate less heat during operation, reducing the burden on thermal management systems.
Where sodium-ion falls short is energy density and ease of manufacturing. Sodium-ion cells store less energy per kilogram than LFP (lithium iron phosphate), and their hard carbon anodes are more difficult to produce consistently as compared to graphite anodes used in lithium-ion designs. Controlling gas generation in hard carbon production, managing moisture exposure, achieving reliable adhesion of the aluminum current collector, and tuning anode formation protocols are only some of the engineering obstacles that have kept sodium-ion batteries from volume production.
Related:
Startups Pitch Investors to Transform the Battery Industry
CATL and HyperStrong’s 60-GWh sodium-ion agreement
In April of this year, CATL and energy storage integrator HyperStrong
signed a strategic cooperation agreement
in Ningde, China, covering a three-year, 60 GWh sodium-ion battery supply commitment. CATL describes the agreement as the largest sodium-ion battery supply deal in the world to date, and HyperStrong as the company's first strategic partner for sodium-ion energy storage. Their collaboration covers technology research and development, product applications, and project deployment.
CATL and HyperStrong representatives at the signing ceremony. Credit: CATL
CATL and HyperStrong representatives at the signing ceremony. Credit:
The agreement rests on manufacturing capabilities that CATL claims to have developed across the full sodium-ion production process. For example, the company claims notable energy density gains compared to previous commercial sodium-ion attempts, owing to a combination of morphology control and surface modification. On the production side, CATL says it resolved key process challenges by applying angstrom-level pore size regulation, surface molecular water-locking, and adaptive dynamic formation, each aimed at ensuring output consistency at high volumes.
CATL also notes that its sodium-ion cells share a platform-based design with the same form factor as its lithium-ion products. According to the company, that design choice reduces integration costs for operators and shortens the time from product qualification to power station deployment.
Related:
Breaking Down the Limits of Solid-State Battery Performance
CATL’s Naxtra Battery Reaches GWh-Scale Production
Meanwhile, at CATL's Super Technology Day in Beijing this year, the company
announced
that its Naxtra sodium-ion battery has achieved GWh-level industrialization. CATL describes the Naxtra as the result of systematically resolving hundreds of engineering challenges, with particular focus on four bottlenecks it identified as blocking sodium-ion mass production:
Extreme water control
Gas generation in hard carbon production lines
Aluminum foil adhesion
Self-forming anode systems
CATL says full-scale mass production will begin by the end of 2026.
The Naxtra sodium-ion battery marks CATL’s transition from the lab to gigawatt-hour scale manufacturing of sodium-ion technology. Credit: CATL
The Naxtra sodium-ion battery marks CATL’s transition from the lab to gigawatt-hour scale manufacturing of sodium-ion technology. Credit:
Taken together, the HyperStrong agreement and the Naxtra industrialization announcement show CATL’s involvement in two sides of the push for sodium-ion adoption. One demonstrates the chemistry’s commercial demand at scale, while the other shows that they can deliver the manufacturing capacity to meet it.
The open question now is whether hard carbon anode supply chains can develop at the pace that matches CATL’s commitments and timelines. The answer to that question will dictate the scale to which CATL and other battery manufacturers can produce sodium-ion cells.

He holds an M.S. and B.S. in EE and has designed electronics for top brands, including MakerBot, UltiMaker, Hyundai, and AT&T. title: EQONIC Advances Aluminum Battery Technology for Sustainability
content:
Battery Manufacturing
Materials
Design & Manufacturing
Industry Outlook
EQONIC introduces aluminum battery technology focused on affordability, sustainability, and scalability, addressing key challenges in energy storage solutions.
August 5, 2026
3 Min Read
Eqonic confirmed its proprietary, lithium-free composite has aluminum as its core material.
Eqonic Group.
EQONIC Group—a UK-based battery technology startup—has announced aluminum as the core material in its new lithium-free, sodium-free, and rare-earth-free battery technology. This development marks a great step toward a cost-effective and sustainable alternative to traditional battery chemistries such as
lithium-ion batteries
. The company is now moving to the next step, industrial validation, a critical phase in preparing the technology for commercial deployment.
Driving cost efficiency
According to the company, its aluminum-based battery technology has the potential to significantly reduce costs.
has set a target manufactured cost of £50/kWh at scale, which is approximately half the industry average for lithium-ion batteries. This cost reduction could make battery energy storage systems (BESS) and electric vehicles (EVs) more affordable, potentially accelerating the adoption of renewable energy technologies.
Related:
Driving Innovation in Europe Battery Manufacturing with CATL
“Aluminum-based chemistry gives us everything we set out to achieve – material abundance, high levels of safety, and low cost – without the trade-offs that lithium, sodium, and rare earth materials carry,” stated Jas Kandola, Founder and CEO of EQONIC Group. By focusing on affordability, EQONIC aims to address one of the key barriers to widespread adoption of energy storage solutions.
Sustainability through abundant materials
Aluminum, one of the most abundant elements on Earth, offers a sustainable and widely available alternative to materials like
lithium and other critical minerals
, which are often associated with supply chain challenges and environmental concerns. EQONIC’s choice of aluminum aligns with its goal of creating a more sustainable battery technology while ensuring a stable and cost-effective supply chain.
The company’s decision to avoid sodium, another emerging chemistry in battery technology, is notable. According to
, while sodium-ion battery adoption is growing, especially in BESS applications, these batteries still face challenges with scalability and supply chain efficiency. By focusing on aluminum, EQONIC aims to bypass these challenges entirely, leveraging a material that is not only abundant but also supported by well-established, responsibly managed supply chains. This focus on sustainability could make EQONIC’s technology an attractive option for industries seeking to reduce their environmental impact while maintaining cost efficiency.
EQONIC confirms aluminum as the chemistry behind its breakthrough battery technology. Courtesy of Eqonic.
Progressing toward industrial validation
EQONIC is now advancing its aluminum-based technology toward industrial validation, a critical step in transitioning from laboratory research to commercial readiness. This phase will involve rigorous testing to assess the manufacturability, performance, and reliability of the technology at scale.
Related:
Building the Future of Battery Technology in Upstate New York
“Confirming the chemistry is one part of the story; progressing towards industrial validation is the part that matters most, and that’s exactly where our focus is now,” Kandola stated. Industrial validation is essential for ensuring that the technology can meet the demands of real-world applications and achieve the reliability required for widespread adoption.
The next steps in EQONIC’s journey will be critical. Industrial validation will play a pivotal role in demonstrating the technology’s performance and reliability, ensuring it is ready for commercial deployment. As the company continues to progress, its focus on cost efficiency and sustainability positions it as a noteworthy player in the evolving energy storage landscape. The use of abundant materials like aluminum, combined with third-party validation, will be essential in building trust and ensuring the long-term viability of this new lithium-free battery technology.

title: EV Fires Behave Like Conventional Car Fires
content:
Battery News
Automotive & Mobility
Testing & Safety
New research from UL finds electric vehicle fires behave much like conventional car fires, contrary to widespread assumptions about intensity.
August 5, 2026
4 Min Read
Carmakers can give firefighters a better chance to extinguish EV battery fires with possible adjustments to battery pack design.
Witthay Prasongsin via Getty Images
At a Glance
Battery access for firefighters remains a key challenge despite similar fire behavior.
Thermal runaway timing varies widely between EV models, affecting fire growth rates.
Standardizing emergency features across EV brands could improve responder safety.
EV battery fires
are an issue that looms large in the popular imagination, but they are poorly understood and documented. Indeed, a 2025
U.S. Fire Administration report on EV fires
says in its introduction, “There are substantial gaps in the science available to inform safe and effective approaches for identifying, confining, and extinguishing EV fires.
The report identified these three current challenges:
Limited science-based guidance for fire departments, EMS, law enforcement, towing operators, and the automotive recovery industry.
Significant differences in battery types, chemistry, location, and size across different EV brands, models, and years.
Existing tactics, tools, and procedures for addressing EV fires are not always based on scientific evidence.
With this in mind,
UL Research Institutes’ Fire Safety Research Institute
undertook a
project to document the nature of EV fires
and came to the somewhat surprising conclusion that EVs burn similarly to combustion-powered vehicles. Conventional wisdom has been that, while EVs catch fire less frequently than ICE cars, their fires burn with greater intensity.
UL Research Institutes initiated battery fires in EVs and found that “fire dynamics and associated chemical hazard in both EVs and ICEVs are primarily driven by the fire in the passenger compartment materials, and thus were similar between powertrain types.”
That means that the technical details of both kinds of fires are more similar than was expected. “The time to burnout, peak heat release rate, and total energy release were similar between EVs and ICEVs,” the report states. “Though anecdotally there have been concerns about major differences in EV fire behavior, no evidence was found that EVs burn hotter, or last longer than their conventional counterparts.”
The EVs in the test showed more variability in the fire growth rate than the ICE vehicles, with some growing faster and others more slowly than the conventional vehicles that were set on fire. Video analysis of the fires revealed that this is because of the time between the first recognition of a thermal runaway in the battery pack and the time needed for visible flames to emerge that then set the rest of the car alight.
"This research provides the fire service with evidence-based tactics they can implement immediately to improve firefighter safety and operations during EV fire incidents,” said
Adam Barowy
, Principal Research Engineer, UL Research Institutes, Fire Safety Research Institute. “By understanding fire behavior, exposure hazards, and the effectiveness of standard suppression strategies, fire departments can make informed tactical decisions that protect their teams and the communities they serve."
While the research was intended for firefighters, carmakers can also benefit as they consider design options when developing future EVs. “Overcoming the challenges associated with EV fire suppression will likely require continued advances in battery and vehicle safety engineering alongside improvements in firefighting tools and tactics,” the report acknowledged.
One of the toughest challenges that firefighters faced when battling the EV fires was getting enough cooling water to the battery cells that were undergoing thermal runaway. Carmakers go to great lengths to protect the battery cells from outside intrusion in the event of a crash, but this complicates firefighting. “Designs which facilitate better firefighter access to the battery during rare but severe fire events may warrant further consideration,” the report found.
Researchers cited the example of the Renault Zoe, a car that includes a firefighter access port in the battery case that allows water to be sprayed inside the battery enclosure. They acknowledge the potential for unintended side effects of such a feature, such as the potential for it to become a pathway for battery effluent to enter the passenger compartment, increasing the risk of explosion.
The UL researchers also point to the value of standardization of emergency responder-facing features, such as high-voltage disconnects, vent locations, and safety markings. This would simplify emergency operations for responders who wouldn’t have to consider as much variety among manufacturers.
The discontinued Renault Zoe EV's battery pack featured a port for firefighters to introduce water in case of a fire. RENAULT
Carmakers endeavor to ensure sufficient cooling for the cells in a pack to preserve their longevity and performance, and also to reduce the potential for thermal runaway. But, once runaway starts, variations in battery pack construction appear to make no difference in its propagation, according to the UL team.
However, researchers don’t rule out the potential for continued progress in this area. “Advances in battery cells, chemistries, and pack designs that improve resistance to thermal runaway propagation, while balancing the many competing objectives of vehicle design, could reduce the resources required for fire suppression and improve responder safety,” the report states, perhaps optimistically. “Ongoing collaboration and open communication between vehicle manufacturers, battery developers, researchers, and the fire service will likely be important in achieving these goals.”
Certainly, this seems like a worthy objective and ample motivation for all four groups to pursue improvements in this area.

title: Do We Really Need Mega Next-Gen Data Center Campuses?
content:
Over the past three decades, data centers have expanded in size and scope like heated gas – rapid and relentless. What began as modest server rooms, or a large air-conditioned hall with a mainframe supporting enterprise applications, has evolved into sprawling hyperscale campuses with hundreds of thousands of servers spread across multiple buildings.
Facilities once measured in square feet are now measured in acres. The largest under development in the US includes
Meta’s 3,650-acre Hyperion campus
in Richland Parish, Louisiana. And an even bigger concept has been floated: investor and “Shark Tank” co-host Kevin O'Leary has discussed a
40,000-acre site
in Utah, later pared back to 20,000 acres after
significant public blowback
. Mind you, 20,000 acres is roughly the size of Manhattan.
Not all of that land is built up. Within each facility, a portion of the constructed area is IT “white space,” the data halls that house compute and storage, while “gray space” supports mechanical and electrical systems such as power distribution, UPS, switchgear, and cooling. At the campus scale, additional acreage is dedicated to substations, utility corridors, roads, yards, and setbacks. The result – a built environment so extensive that you need a car to get around it – prompts the question: Do operators truly need campuses so large?
Related:
Power Bottlenecks Push Data Centers Beyond Traditional Hubs
Peter Skae, managing director of technical services at data center construction firm JLL, said the driver behind these giant facilities is straightforward: workloads have simply outgrown the capacity of a single building.
“Hyperscale data centers have grown massive because of cloud computing, AI, and digital services that all require enormous computational power and storage capacity that's most efficiently delivered at scale,” Skae said. “Consolidating into larger facilities achieves significant cost advantages through economies of scale while enabling the advanced power, cooling, and redundancy infrastructure needed for mission-critical operations.”
Modular Design at Campus Scale
Rather than betting everything on a single monolithic structure, developers are building campuses composed of multiple, reasonably sized buildings. Skae noted that this model brings capacity to market faster, is easier to manage,
improves redundancy
, spreads risk across multiple assets, and supports multi-tenant demand. There is, however, a practical limit. “Of course, you can only build so many buildings at a time, and trade labor isn’t exactly plentiful,” he said.
Analysts agree that these massive campuses start small and are positioned to grow. They rarely open at full size, and there is no guarantee they will ever reach maximum capacity.
Related:
AI Data Center Boom Strains Global Construction Capacity
Alan Howard, senior analyst for facilities at Omdia, pointed out that these sites are really collections of buildings – typically 150,000 to 400,000 square feet each – developed over time. “Some campus builds can take 10 years or more,” he said, adding that the surge in AI demand – and the capital chasing it – has accelerated timelines on select projects as service providers move quickly to capture market opportunity.
This shift from a single building to a multi-building campus somewhat mirrors what is happening inside server CPUs. Instead of a big monolithic design, chipmakers are embracing
chiplets
– separate pieces tied together with high-speed interconnects. Likewise, these new data center campuses function as interconnected modules.
Alex Cordovil, research director at Dell'Oro Group, echoed the module theme, noting that many AI deployments are being built as cluster building blocks of 10-50 MW. Plenty of operators are content to run only a few of those. “The headline-grabbing giants are one end of a much wider spectrum, not the whole story,” he said.
When Scale Pays for Itself
Why are some developers chasing 1 GW-plus total campus capacity? Cordovil said the constraint on
site selection
has changed. For many advanced AI workloads, the time a frontier model takes to compute an answer dwarfs network latency. Users already wait seconds for a model to respond, so whether results arrive in five milliseconds or a hundred is rarely noticeable.
Related:
How Data Centers Can Be Better Neighbors: Building Community Trust
“That breaks the old rule that compute had to sit close to the user, and it frees developers to build in remote, isolated locations where the usual siting constraints all but disappear,” Cordovil said. “Once you remove those constraints, scale becomes the lever you pull.”
At that scale, the economics compound. If a developer is effectively building its own power – through
on-site generation
, dedicated substations, high-voltage interconnects, or long-term offtake arrangements – the undertaking is enormous and complex, Cordovil explained. A larger footprint helps amortize those investments. The same logic applies to permitting: securing approval for one very large campus and then building it out in phases over several years can de-risk the project more than pursuing many smaller, separate approvals.
Operating the Megacampus
Operating at this scale is less about heroics and more about discipline. According to Skae, it’s achievable through systematic processes, proven technology, and specialized expertise. JLL relies on integrated technology platforms that provide real-time visibility across massive footprints; designs for longevity and future-proofing over 50-year asset lifecycles; collaboration across the delivery team; and a zoned approach that breaks large facilities into manageable areas with dedicated teams responsible for each zone.
Howard emphasized resource planning from day one. “Power and water planning for multi-GW scale campuses is critical at the very earliest stages,” he said. “Each campus is different, but on-site generation and backup are likely even with a grid connection. For cooler climates like Utah and Wyoming, the use of water is likely to be minimized by using air-cooled chillers. To the extent direct-to-chip cooling is used, the closed-loop system will have little water demand,” he said.
In short, the industry’s pull toward ever-larger campuses isn’t mere spectacle. It’s a response to outsized computational demand, shifting constraints, and the economics of building and operating mission-critical infrastructure at scale – even if it means a data center now requires a map and, occasionally, a set of car keys.

title: Power Bottlenecks Push Data Centers Beyond Traditional Hubs
content:
Power availability is overtaking customer demand as the decisive factor shaping global data center development, pushing more projects beyond established hubs and into secondary markets, new research reveals.
According to a
Ashburn, Virginia, led the Americas ranking; Johor, Malaysia, topped Asia-Pacific; and London ranked first in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa.
“Power availability has become the primary factor determining both where data centers are built and whether announced projects proceed on schedule,” Alexandra Desseyn, Americas research manager at DCByte, told
Data Center Knowledge.
Established Hubs Face Delivery Limits
Major data center hubs retain key advantages, including connectivity, cloud availability zones, and mature customer ecosystems. However, the report highlights that
grid queues
, land scarcity, and regulatory pressure are increasingly hindering the conversion of demand into operational capacity.
Related:
Emerging Data Center Markets: Key Locations to Watch in 2026
Ashburn remains the center of the world’s largest data center market, with 5.6 GW of live capacity and another 15 GW in its pipeline as of the first quarter. Yet grid connections can take between five and seven years, while development is spreading into Prince William,
Culpeper
, and Spotsylvania counties.
Similar pressures are emerging elsewhere internationally, with Tokyo facing power connection timelines of up to a decade, while Dublin and Amsterdam have been classified as constrained core markets. In those locations, demand remains strong, but power, regulation, and community resistance limit delivery.
“In many primary markets, grid-connection timeframes now extend several years, meaning suitable land without a credible route to power has limited development value,” Desseyn said.
Secondary Markets Gain Ground
DCByte’s future growth rankings show investment shifting toward markets with more flexible development conditions. Pittsburgh, Charlotte, and Austin led the Americas list, while Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, and Jakarta topped the APAC list. Zaragoza, Milan, and Berlin headed the EMEA ranking.
Johor exemplifies how rapidly this shift can occur, with the
Malaysian market
growing from less than 10 MW five years ago to approximately 1 GW within four years, transforming from a Singapore spillover location into APAC’s leading emerging growth market.
Related:
New Data Center Developments: August 2026
Desseyn noted that Tennessee, West Texas, and locations beyond Northern Virginia’s established clusters are attracting greater attention in North America.
Portugal, Spain, and Nordic locations offer opportunities in Europe, while Johor, Batam, and secondary Japanese markets are positioned for further growth in APAC.
Power Means More Than Supply
The report indicated developers must look beyond a market’s total electricity generation. Transmission capacity, substation availability, interconnection queues, and staged energization all determine whether power can reach a site within a commercially viable timeframe.
“Operators are favoring jurisdictions with clear planning frameworks, supportive local governments and an established process for accommodating large energy users,” Desseyn said.
She noted where policies remain unsettled, or community opposition is strong, projects are more likely to be redesigned, delayed or redirected to another market.
Long lead times for transformers, switchgear, and gas turbines add further delivery risks. Operators must also consider fiber diversity, water, construction labor and whether facilities can support liquid cooling and AI rack densities approaching or exceeding 100 kW.
Related:
Virginia Report Finds Groundwater Running Dry for New Data Centers
Meanwhile, planning and community acceptance are becoming equally important as authorities scrutinize resource consumption, incentives, environmental effects and permanent job creation.
Ultimately, Desseyn said, the next investment cycle will favor markets that can demonstrate delivery certainty.
“The winning regions will not necessarily be those offering the cheapest land or electricity, but those able to provide a credible and coordinated path through power procurement, planning, construction and community approval,” she explained.

title: CATL-backed CNTE brings Czech Republic’s largest battery online - Energy Storage
content: The Czech Republic’s largest completed BESS project is now online, serving the European frequency regulation market. Located on a former mining wasteland, the 37.95 MW/41.7 MWh Modlany BESS features 11 liquid-cooled, 20-foot energy storage containers supplied by CNTE. CNTE is invested by Chinese battery giant CATL, and its STAR T-285 containers supplied to the Modlany project use CATL’s lithium-ion phosphate cells. Each container is rated at 3.45 MW/3.793 MWh and supports 1P charging and discharging and is suitable for one-to-four-hour systems, according to CNTE. The Modlany project, which also includes 42.7 MW of solar, is connected to a high-voltage substation and provides grid balancing and fast-response frequency regulation services. The battery can store excess solar power and can rapidly charge or discharge depending on grid requirements, helping to balance electricity demand and fluctuations in solar generation throughout the Czech electricity system as it adds more renewables. Modlany’s owners Katemo Group state on their website that the planned storage capacity is “up to 130 MWh”. The Czech engineering company is working with CATL and CNTE to bring BESS to the Czech and Slovak markets and it has kitted its Modlany battery out with its own energy management software designed to optimize performance and adhere to cybersecurity standards. The future of the Czech Republic’s energy storage market will be driven by utility-scale investments and favorable regulations, according to analysis by Aurora Energy Research from November 2025. The agency forecasted the country’s total battery storage capacity to hit 6 GWh by the end of the decade. In March 2025, the European Union approved an aid package for 1.5 GWh of storage capacity in the Czech Republic. Other battery players besides CNTE are watching the growing market closely. China’s AlphaESS signed agreements in December 2025 to deliver a combined 320 MWh of BESS across two sites in the Czech Republic, which when completed will eclipse Modlany’s capacity. Headquartered in Fujian Province, China, CNTE is active in the C&I and residential segments as well as smart electric vehicle charging. In the utility-scale market, it has projects in Germany, the Netherlands, Switzerland, Austria, and China. It is also present in South Africa, Uganda and other European markets through its C&I activities. title: Electrovaya unveils 7 MW containerized battery system targeting AI data centers - Energy Storage
content: Lithium-ion technology company Electrovaya has launched the ElvaPulse 1500, a high-power stationary battery energy storage system designed for data centers, artificial intelligence infrastructure, and mission-critical power applications. The launch marks the debut product under Electrovaya’s new ElvaPulse stationary storage portfolio, engineered specifically to handle high-surge, rapid-discharge power requirements driven by volatile AI compute workloads. Housed in a standard 20-foot modular container, the 1,500 VDC architecture delivers up to 2.88 MWh of nominal energy capacity and can supply approximately 7 MW of continuous power. The unit is built around the company’s proprietary ceramic separator technology that underpins its Infinity Battery line. The battery unit operates at a discharge duration of under 30 minutes, representing a C-rate greater than 2C. Electrovaya states this high power density allows facilities to reduce physical site footprints and cut balance-of-system costs compared to standard 2- to 4-hour utility-scale storage profiles. The platform targets microgrids, peak-demand management, industrial power quality, and renewable energy firming in addition to hyperscale data centers. Electrovaya Chief Executive Officer Raj DasGupta said the platform was purpose-built to meet pushing energy demands by offering high power density alongside proven battery longevity and configuration flexibility. Initial commercial deliveries are targeted for the second quarter of 2027 out of Electrovaya’s manufacturing facility in Jamestown, New York. Certification processes for UL 1973 and UL 9540 are currently underway with completion targeted for the first quarter of 2027, and the company is currently accepting production reservations while engaging in active discussions with hyperscale and energy developers. title: Growatt brings MINA to all-in-one home storage - Energy Storage
content: Growatt has launched MINA, a single-phase all-in-one residential energy storage system combining a hybrid inverter, modular battery storage, backup power and intelligent energy management. The company is targeting rooftop solar markets in Europe and Australia, where time-of-use tariffs, lower solar export payments and rising electricity prices are increasing demand for household self-consumption and energy resilience. MINA is available with inverter output ranging from 3 kW to 10 kW. Its battery can be configured with one to six 5 kWh modules, providing total usable storage capacity of between 5 kWh and 30 kWh. The system supports three maximum power point trackers, with one string connected to each tracker, and a maximum DC-to-AC ratio of 2.0. Maximum input current is 18 A per tracker, allowing the inverter to accommodate newer high-current PV modules. Growatt said its battery optimizer technology manages each module independently. This is designed to reduce the effect of differences in state of charge, operating history or ageing between battery modules. It also allows homeowners to add new modules to an existing system as household demand increases. Potential expansion scenarios include the addition of electric vehicles, heat pumps, home offices or higher backup requirements. The architecture enables customers to install a smaller system initially rather than paying for the maximum capacity at the time of commissioning. MINA provides a 63 A backup connection and can supply selected household loads during grid outages. A preliminary European datasheet lists a transfer time of less than 10 milliseconds, intended to maintain operation of lighting, refrigeration, communications and other essential equipment with minimal interruption. The system incorporates self-aligning connectors and a wire-free stacked battery architecture. Growatt claims the hardware can be stacked in around 10 minutes, with system setup and diagnostics completed in a similar period. It can be installed on the floor or mounted against a wall. Other features include Type II surge protection on both the AC and DC sides, arc-fault protection, natural cooling and remote monitoring. Users and installers can view PV generation, battery status, household consumption and operating performance through Growatt’s monitoring platform. The system is also virtual-power-plant ready. Growatt lists a 25-kW bidirectional DC charging function for future vehicle-to-grid applications, although this feature is not yet commercially available. Growatt has already presented MINA in Australia. The latest announcement broadens its commercial positioning across Germany, the Netherlands, Italy, Spain, the United Kingdom, Australia and other residential storage markets. title: Ola Electric, Axis Energy plan to deploy up to 20 GWh of battery storage by 2032 - Energy Storage
content: Ola Electric has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with renewable energy developer Axis Energy to deploy as much as 5 GWh of BESS per year from 2028. The MoU runs until 2032 with a cumulative target of 20 GWh over the five-year period, providing Indian EV manufacturer Ola Electric with a significant pipeline for its new manufacturing platform – Ola Mahashakti . Scheduled to launch on August 15, Ola Mahashakti is being billed as an energy storage platform for commercial, industrial and utility-scale applications. Ola said its Mahashakti battery energy storage systems (BESS) are being developed in India on a vertically integrated manufacturing platform spanning cell technology, manufacturing, and system engineering. The deal with Axis Energy sees Ola partner with a developer building one of India’s largest pipelines of storage-backed renewable projects. Axis Energy has secured grid approvals for over 3.75 GW projects in Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan and has another 3.5 GW capacity in pipeline. These projects, spanning firm and dispatchable renewable energy (FDRE), hybrid, and other non-solar configurations, will require large-scale BESS to improve renewable energy integration, enhance grid reliability, and deliver firm, round-the-clock clean energy. The national opportunity for BESS is even greater. The Central Electricity Authority has said India’s energy transition will require 400+ GWh storage deployment by 2032. Reddy Kataru, chairman and managing director of Axis Energy Ventures, described the MoU with Ola as an “important step” toward evaluating domestic BESS solutions. Bhavish Aggarwal, chairman and managing director of Ola Electric, said that the company’s vertically integrated cell-to-system platform will enable it to deliver a strong proposition across safety, performance and total cost of ownership. “Axis Energy is our first large-scale partner and an important early validation of Mahashakti’s potential. We are witnessing a strong interest from potential partners in the industry, and this MoU further strengthens our momentum in building long-term partnerships,” Aggarwal said. Headquartered in Hyderabad, Axis Energy Ventures has more than 15 years of experience in developing and delivering renewable energy projects across India. The company has more than 1.5 GW of commissioned capacity and a development pipeline of over 8.5 GW. Axis Energy Ventures has a strategic partnership with Brookfield Renewable through Evren, a 51:49 joint venture backed by Brookfield’s $20 billion Global Transition Fund II. Ola Electric Mobility’s Ola Future factory in Tamil Nadu produces electric vehicles and components. It is supported by Ola’s Bengaluru-based Battery Innovation Centre (BIC), dedicated to advancing cell and battery technology. title: Serentica Renewables commissions first phase of 1 GWh Bikaner battery project - Energy Storage
content: Serentica Renewables has commissioned the first phase of its 1 GWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in Bikaner, Rajasthan. The project represents the first time the renewable energy arm of Vedanta Group has delivered a large-scale BESS for the commercial and industrial segment. The first phase of the project comprises a 50 MW/200 MWh BESS. The Bikaner BESS has been developed with a modular architecture to provide operational flexibility, scalability and rapid response capabilities. Serentica Renewables said its Bikaner project powers one of the world’s first time-block round-the-clock (RTC) renewable power arrangements for industrial consumers, demonstrating how battery storage can transform intermittent renewable energy into dependable, 24/7 clean power. “Battery energy storage systems will play a defining role in the next phase of India’s clean energy transition by making renewable energy available whenever it is needed,” said Akshay Hiranandani, CEO, Serentica Renewables. “The commissioning of phase 1 of our 1 GWh BESS is a significant milestone in our journey to deliver reliable, round the clock renewable energy for India’s industrial sector. By integrating advanced storage with renewable generation, we are creating a future ready energy ecosystem that combines sustainability, reliability and flexibility for our customers.” Established in 2022, Serentica Renewables is an independent power producer (IPP) with 3.2 GW of renewable energy capacity. The IPP has ongoing projects across multiple states, leveraging a mix of solar, wind, energy storage, and advanced balancing solutions. title: US grants $490 million loan for 220 MW of battery capacity in Puerto Rico - Energy Storage
content: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) has closed a $489.4 million loan with Dawn Puerto Rico, a subsidiary of Pattern Energy, to fund 220 MW of battery energy storage systems in Puerto Rico. The facility will be located in Arecibo and Santa Isabel and will use battery technology made in the United States, according to the DOE’s Energy Domain Financing Office. The agency did not specify the energy capacity of the systems, expressed in MWh, or their duration of discharge. The DOE estimates that batteries will be able to provide backup electricity to more than 100,000 customers during periods of supply shortages. It also estimates that it will prevent approximately 13 million cumulative hours of service interruptions, taking as a reference the network operational data for 2025. The loan would reduce the electricity costs of Puerto Rican households and businesses by about $312.5 million over the next 25 years, according to US government projections. The funding was restructured following a review by the current US administration. In addition to the two battery projects, the agreement provides for a way for the possible future development of dispatchable electricity generation powered by natural gas. The DOE did not report the power, location or timetable of that eventual infrastructure. The closed operation changes the scope of the conditional commitment announced by the DOE in January 2025. That proposal included three independent BESS systems with a joint power of 180 MW and a capacity of 720 MWh, in addition to a 70 MWac photovoltaic plant with integrated storage. The new announcement raises total storage power to 220 MW, but no longer includes photovoltaic installations. Nor does it detail how the power is distributed between the projects of Arecibo and Santa Isabel. Since 2025, the DOE has issued several emergency orders under section 202(c) of the Federal Energy Act to authorize generation and other actions aimed at maintaining Puerto Rico’s electricity supply during periods of high demand and during hurricane season. title: Ørsted turns on 500 MWh battery project with co-located solar in Texas - Energy Storage
content: The 250 MW/ 500MWh  Old 300 Storage project in Needville, Texas, has reached commercial operations according Ørsted, co-located with a 430 MW solar project. Old 300 Storage is fully integrated into the ERCOT grid and will be operated independently from the Old 300 Solar installation, which has been generating since 2024. Energy storage for the project comprises Tesla Megapacks manufactured at the company’s Lathrop, California facility. Ørsted said the developer and Tesla have been working in collaboration with the Needville Fire Department to provide “comprehensive education” on the energy storage technology and safety response protocols. Melissa Peterson, president of Ørsted Americas Onshore noted that BESS has been playing a larger role on the ERCOT grid, providing power at times of tight supply and demand margins. “Achieving commercial operations at our Old 300 Storage project will have tangible benefits, such as strengthening grid reliability by providing additional resources to Texas grid operators and allowing for more diverse and localized energy options as electricity demand continues to grow.” Old 300 Storage is part of a growing onshore portfolio developed by Ørsted in the United States. Major projects include a 300MW/1200MWh BESS located developed with Salt River Project and located alongside the Eleven Mile Solar Center in Pinal County, Arizona. The project was commissioned in 2024 and represented an approximate $1 billion investment by Ørsted in clean energy for Arizona Following the Old 300 BESS entering commercial operations, Ørsted now has a 6 GW of operational onshore US energy projects. The international developer, which has its global headquarters in Denmark, estimates the Old 300 solar and storage projects combined will inject approximately $110 million in property tax revenue for the local area. BMW is hurrying to ramp up production of the
after opening orders early due to stronger-than-expected demand.
BMW i3 enters production as demand surges

title: Juiced doubles down with 120-mile range e-bike on dual-battery Scrambler Hardtail
content:
Micah Toll
| Aug 6 2026 - 4:56 am PT
When Juiced Bikes
unveiled its new generation
of Scrambler models earlier this summer, the company hinted that an even longer-range version was on the way. Now it’s here.
Juiced has officially launched the dual-battery version of its Scrambler Hardtail, giving riders a claimed range of up to 120 miles (200 km) while keeping the same moped-style design that has made the Scrambler one of the company’s signature models – and the first model to relaunch the brand’s second act.
The new setup essentially doubles down on what many riders already liked about the 52V bike. A second battery mounted beneath the frame boosts total battery capacity to 38.4 Ah, helping push the claimed maximum range to 120 miles (200 km) under ideal riding conditions. That should make range anxiety all but disappear for commuters, weekend explorers, or anyone who just likes taking the scenic route home.
Of course, very few riders are actually going to pedal for 120 miles in a single outing. That number is based on ideal conditions with conservative riding. But the bigger takeaway isn’t necessarily the headline range figure – it’s the freedom that comes with having enough battery capacity that you can stop worrying about it altogether.
And even for riders who don’t intend to keep the bike in its lowest power mode to eke out that full 120 miles of range, the 1,996 Wh of capacity from those two batteries is going to provide plenty of high-power throttle riding, too.
Dual batteries offer twice the range
The bike still uses the same 1,764W peak rear hub motor found on the standard Hardtail Scrambler and meets the same legal requirements for Class 2 or Class 3 operation, meaning riders aren’t getting extra speed, but they are getting a lot more time in the saddle before needing to recharge.
Juiced is currently offering the dual-battery Hardtail Scrambler
for $1,999
, a $245 discount from its listed MSRP. The company is also throwing in a handful of accessories, including fenders, a handlebar bag, bar pad, headplate, custom nameplate, and stickers.
I recently had the chance
to spend time riding and reviewing the new Scrambler lineup
, and one of the things that stood out most was how well these bikes blend classic minibike styling with genuinely useful everyday performance. The Hardtail version skips rear suspension in favor of a simpler, lighter frame, though the large 20×4-inch tires still do a respectable job of soaking up rough pavement. And since its geometry has been carried over from the full-suspension version, it still rides like a well thought out, powerful e-bike – not a random Amazon frame with a motor strapped on.
With a second battery, you’ll never let your girl see your range anxiety
For riders who regularly rack up serious mileage or simply hate charging, the dual-battery Scrambler looks like a compelling new option.
At under $2,000
, it also undercuts many other long-range e-bikes while bringing a unique moto-inspired style that has become something of a Juiced trademark.

title: Tesla starts Megapack 3 production with 28% more energy per unit
content:
Tesla Megapack
Fred Lambert
| Aug 6 2026 - 5:52 am PT
Tesla has started building its next-generation Megapack 3 grid battery, with the first units rolling off the line at the company’s new Megafactory in Brookshire, Texas.
The plant went from groundbreaking to production in 16 months and is designed to build 50 GWh of Megapack 3 a year. That’s the version Tesla says packs roughly 28% more energy into the same footprint as the Megapack it replaces.
Tesla confirmed the production start on Wednesday through its Megapack account, noting the Brookshire facility has “a designed capacity of 50 GWh/year dedicated to Megapack 3.” It’s the physical follow-through on the
Megapack 3 and Megablock reveal
Megapack 3 is officially rolling off the line at our newest Megafactory in Brookshire, Texas!
The factory went from groundbreaking to operation in just 16 months & has a designed capacity of 50 GWh/year dedicated to Megapack 3
So here’s what actually changed between Megapack 3 and the versions before it.
What’s different about Megapack 3
A single Megapack 3 holds about 5 MWh, up from 3.9 MWh on the Megapack 2 XL. That’s roughly 28% more storage in a box that takes up the same ground.
Tesla gets there mainly by using bigger cells. Megapack 3 moves to a larger 2.8-liter cell format, which lets Tesla cram more capacity into each cabinet without growing the enclosure.
The other big change is plumbing. Tesla says Megapack 3 cuts thermal-system connection points by 78% versus the previous generation. Fewer connections means fewer places for a liquid-cooled battery to leak or fail, and less labor to assemble and service. Not glamorous. But at grid scale, reliability and install time are the whole game.
For context, the Megapack has been climbing this curve for years. It launched in 2019 at around 3 MWh, then Tesla
squeezed it up to 3.9 MWh
with the 2 XL in 2022. Megapack 3 is the biggest single jump yet.
The real shift is the Megablock
A Megablock bundles up to four Megapack 3 units (about 20 MWh) with the transformer and switchgear already integrated at the factory. On older Megapacks, a lot of that medium-voltage wiring happened in the field, one of the slowest and most expensive parts of building a battery farm.
Tesla just signed a
$5 billion, 25 GWh Megapack deal with NatPower
in Europe, and data-center operators are buying storage as fast as Tesla can build it. A denser unit that goes up faster is exactly what those customers are asking for.
Why the new factory matters
Brookshire is Tesla’s answer to a supply problem. The company’s Lathrop, California Megafactory and its Shanghai plant have been running flat out, and Tesla
announced this third Megafactory
specifically to add capacity as competition from CATL, Fluence, and BYD heats up.
At 50 GWh a year dedicated to Megapack 3, Brookshire could quickly become Tesla’s largest energy storage manufacturing facility, beating Lathrop’s full output on its own. And building it in 16 months is fast for a facility this size.
Electrek’s Take
It’s impressive how quickly Tesla can get a new factory to production.
However, the spec that matters most with Megapack 3 isn’t the 5 MWh. It’s the Megablock. Grid batteries don’t fail to get built because the cells aren’t good enough — they stall on interconnection, permitting, and the slow, expensive work of wiring gear in a field. Moving that into the factory is the kind of unglamorous manufacturing win that actually moves deployment numbers, and it’s the same playbook Tesla ran on the Supercharger and that turned out more than alright.
The open question is cells. Tesla needs a lot of large-format cells to fill a 50 GWh factory, and a chunk of that still depends on suppliers and on how the current US tariff picture shakes out for imported LFP.
Tesla has already started reporting lower gross margins on its energy business due to high tariffs on LFP cells, and its own production isn’t coming close to 50 GWh.

title: Watch Tesla driver plea with police after FSD drove 64 mph in a 45
content:
A police department in Parker, Colorado, pulled over a Tesla going 64 mph in a 45 mph zone whose driver insisted they weren’t responsible, because the car was running “Full Self-Driving.”
Of course, Tesla will never take responsibility for that incident, but the frustrating part is that Tesla already has the solution and yet it refuses to implement it.
“These systems are designed to assist you, not drive for you”
The Parker Police Department shared the stop in a video this week. The driver’s excuse, as the department told it: “I wasn’t driving. I had auto assist on.” They were adamant enough to demand a supervisor.
The department’s reply was blunt. “Driver assistance technology does not replace the driver,” it said. “Whether your vehicle has adaptive cruise control, lane centering or full self-driving, you are still legally responsible for operating your vehicle safely.”
Legally, that isn’t close. Every driver-assist system you can buy in a new car today is a Level 2 system, which means the human is driving and the software is helping. Tesla’s “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” is Level 2. The name says one thing. The fine print, and the law, say another.
Tesla wants the name without the responsibility
Here’s the real problem, and it belongs to Tesla more than to the driver. Tesla sells a $99-a-month package called “Full Self-Driving.” Its CEO has spent a decade telling people the cars can basically drive themselves, and late last year Musk claimed FSD drivers can now text and drive.
But when something goes wrong, Tesla’s position flips. Suddenly the system is only “supervised,” the driver was always responsible, and the manual always said to keep your hands on the wheel.
So Tesla gets to market the car as self-driving and disclaim it as a mere driver aid, depending on which is more convenient in the moment. A driver at a traffic stop pointing at his dashboard is just that contradiction showing up on the side of the road.
The speeding isn’t a glitch. Tesla removed the fix
This is where Tesla loses credibility when it comes to FSd speeding: Tesla was speeding because Tesla designed FSD to drive over the limit, and then took away the tool owners used to rein it in.
I know this one first-hand. Tesla’s “Full Self-Driving” got me a ticket last month. In FSD v14, Tesla scrapped the adjustable speed offset that used to let drivers cap how far over the limit the car would go, and replaced it with fixed presets: Sloth, Chill, Standard, Hurry, and Mad Max. On a 50 km/h road in Standard mode, my car accelerated itself to 78 km/h, 28 over, with my foot nowhere near the pedal. A radar unit did the rest. With the old offset, I’d have set it to +15 and stayed out of trouble.
That’s the “easy fix” owners keep asking for: let the driver set a hard cap. Tesla’s head of AI, Ashok Elluswamy, has now said the company won’t do it, calling a user-set speed limit an “anti-pattern” and arguing Tesla would rather make FSD “smarter” than let owners override it. Tesla is supposed to make FSD smarter for a decade. The car meanwhile still ships with a mode literally named “Mad Max” that deliberately blows past speed limits, while you can’t trust ‘Standard mode’ to stay under the limit.
Regulators have noticed. Sweden told the EU to reject Tesla’s “FSD” unless the speeding behavior is removed. The gap between a product called “Full Self-Driving” and a car that knowingly breaks the speed limit is not a small one.
Electrek’s Take
To be clear, the driver’s excuse is absurd, and I have no problem with Parker police writing the ticket. If your car is speeding, you’re speeding. A cop is not going to cite your software subscription. When I got my ticket last month, I didn’t even mention FSD to the cop and just took the ticket.
Top comment by Damon Ekstrom
While I agree that the driver's excuse is absurd, I think this also shows why FSD will never see full autonomy, at least not in consumer vehicles.
I remember having to deactivate FSD multiple times, because my Model 3 would repeatedly blow past the speed limit. Once Tesla took away the ability to control the speed of the car, I knew I was going to have to be more alert than ever before. It was bad enough being on edge, worrying that the car would drive appropriately, but then I had to start worrying about whether I would get a speeding ticket. because the car now viewed speed limit signs as a suggestion.
Again, this is why FSD will always be a level 2 aid.
But I’m tired of the pile-on that stops at the driver, because Tesla built this confusion on purpose and profits from it. You cannot name a Level 2 system “Full Self-Driving,” tell people they can text behind the wheel, design the thing to drive over the speed limit, and then hide behind “the driver is always responsible” when the radar goes off. Pick one.
There’s an easy fix sitting right there, give owners back a hard speed cap, and Tesla is refusing it on principle and calling driver control an “anti-pattern.” That’s a company telling you it knows better than the driver and the posted limit both.
If Tesla wants drivers to take full responsibility for FSD, the least it could do is give them back the controls to drive it responsibly. Right now it’s doing the opposite.

title: World's first sodium-ion electric haul truck gets to work in China
content:
Electric Heavy Machinery
Sodium-ion Battery
Jo Borrás
| Aug 6 2026 - 5:01 am PT
While Americans fret over whether or not electric vehicles are up to the challenge of hauling them back and forth to the Piggly Wiggly
, Tonly is putting a fleet of advanced sodium battery electric haul trucks to work mining heavy ore.
Co-developed by Chinese equipment brand Tonly Heavy Industry and the chemistry experts at Hina Battery, the prototype 676 kWh “Haixing” series batteries fitted in this Tonly K120E electric haul truck deployed at the Tangshan Sanyou limestone mines are a world’s-first, offering super fast 0% to 100% charging times in under minutes over a usable lifespan of a positively massive 8,000 cycles (!) without the geopolitical headaches of lithium.
The Haixing batteries also offer respectable energy density specs at 165 Wh/kg, improved thermal stability (read: fire safety) compared to lithium, and –
the killer app for ultra class haul trucks
– superior cold-weather performance.
Cold blooded
Tonly haul truck at Peruvian mine; via Tonly.
These trucks are earmarked to work in the coldest regions of northern China,
where nighttime temperatures can frequently plummet to -20°C in areas like Harbin and Shenyang
. Those extreme temperatures don’t just wreak havoc on conventional lithium-ion battery range, they make it almost impossible for the big diesel engines that these big BEVs are replacing to even
let alone run efficiently
That’s why just about everyone who tests EVs in extreme cold comes out impressed with their performance compared to diesel. That includes semi trucks, light-duty BEVs, and (of course)
electric school buses
“Most of the winter it’s 30 to 35 below (zero),” offered West Grand County School District Director of Transportation, Bethany Aurinwhen, in a 2024 interview. “When it’s up to 20 below that’s good day, and (the electric school bus)
has performed extremely well
Putting people first
Autonomous Tonly haul trucks.
The sort of extreme temperatures that cripple diesels don’t just slow down a mine’s operations, they put the people behind the wheel of these massive machines at serious safety risk from cold-related injuries like frostbite and hypothermia.
That’s why stories like last month’s announcement that Tonly will deliver 800 autonomous TLE135 mining trucks to Xinjiang Hanxiang matter so much
Lower emissions, less pollution, reduced hearing loss from diesel drone, superior safety, and autonomous, all-weather performance. That’s a value proposition that’s going to be tough to beat – which explains just about every single political lobbying dollar being spent by the oil companies right now.
Gas and oil knows they’re beat.

title: 超2GW！天合/晶澳/尚德等6企组件订单密集落地
content:
近期光伏组件市场订单及项目进展持续更新，晶澳、琏升科技、天合光能、尚德、正泰新能等企业相继取得海外组件订单或实现项目交付，覆盖不丹、孟加拉、中东、欧洲等多个市场。同时，极电光能钙钛矿屋顶光伏项目实现并网投运，推动新型光伏技术进一步落地应用。
天合光能签署中东1.5GW组件订单
近日，天合光能与中东Al-Raebi贸易与太阳能系统公司签署合作备忘录（MOU）。根据协议，双方计划围绕2026年至2029年约1.5GW光伏项目开展合作，涉及中东地区大型地面电站及工商业光伏项目。
根据合作内容，天合光能将充分发挥领先的TOPCon 3.0技术优势及丰富的全球项目经验，结合Al-Raebi深耕中东市场多年积累的本地资源与项目开发能力，推进中东区域光伏项目落地。
晶澳组件供货不丹120MWp光伏项目
近日，晶澳获南非光伏组件订单，将为不丹120MWp Jamjee Solar PV Project供应全部组件，据悉该项目已于去年开工，预计2027年初并网。
正泰新能签孟加拉国337MW组件订单
8月3日，正泰新能与孟加拉SR Renewable Energy在浙江海宁签署合作备忘录（MOC），双方达成337MW光伏组件供应合作意向。
根据协议，正泰新能计划于2026年至2028年向SR Renewable Energy供应总计337MW光伏组件，产品将应用于孟加拉工商业光伏及大型地面电站项目。双方约定，在采购与供应协议正式签署后，正泰新能将向SR Renewable Energy提供包括技术支持、市场推广活动在内的全面支持，共同推动孟加拉光伏市场的发展。
极电光能钙钛矿屋顶光伏项目投运
7月31日，极电光能宛山湖园区6.7MW钙钛矿屋顶分布式光伏项目正式并网投运。该项目采用极电光能自主研发的钙钛矿光伏组件，是目前钙钛矿领域单体商业化规模较大的屋顶光伏项目之一。
据了解，该项目利用园区厂房屋顶资源，铺设近1.5万片2.81㎡钙钛矿光伏组件，采用“自发自用、余电上网”模式运行。
琏升科技供货四川70MW光伏项目
7月29日，琏升科技眉山智能制造基地完成天王星PRO高效异质结组件四川巴中通江分布式光伏项目首次发货。本次供货项目规模为70MW，所用组件为琏升科技G12-0BB天王星PRO系列。
据了解，该项目主要利用通江县厂房及公共建筑屋顶建设，属于县域分布式光伏项目。此次交付的天王星PRO组件采用G12-0BB双面双玻异质结技术，量产最高功率达765W，组件转换效率超过24.63%，最高双面率接近95%。
尚德Ultra T 3.0组件批量出货海外
近期，尚德最新一代Ultra T 3.0高效四分片组件实现批量出货，产品已陆续交付欧洲、澳大利亚、新西兰、日本等海外市场。
据了解，Ultra T 3.0组件基于N型TOPCon技术打造，采用四分片设计，组件效率最高突破25.2%，电池转换效率最高达27.5%。产品通过优化电流传输路径及封装结构，提升组件发电性能与可靠性，适用于分布式光伏及大型地面电站等应用场景。

title: 超3.3GWh，阳光电源等5企储能订单新进展
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，阳光电源、新源智储、鹏程无限、远东储能、高特电子等5家储能企业接连签约、交付新项目，覆盖独立储能、用户侧储能、高压级联储能等细分领域。
阳光电源签约独立储能项目
8月1日，栖霞市人民政府网站宣布，近日已与阳光新能源在安徽合肥举行台阳新能源栖霞寺口200MW/800MWh独立储能项目合作协议签约仪式。
阳光新能源是阳光电源旗下专业投资开发平台，专注于光伏、风电、储能等领域的项目投资、开发与运营。此次签约的台阳新能源独立储能项目，计划总投资约8.36亿元，拟建设200MW/800MWh新型独立储能电站，采用阳光电源自研自产的电化学储能设备。
新源智储哈萨克斯坦储能项目并网调试
8月1日，由新源智储负责工程设计、储能系统集成及全套设备供货的哈萨克斯坦科克舍套3.45MW/7.72MWh储能项目顺利完成全流程并网调试。
该项目是哈萨克斯坦历史上首套实现并网的储能系统，项目坐落于哈萨克斯坦阿尔卡雷克220kV变电站站外，采用新源智储自主开发的POWERCABIN 3系列液冷储能系统。系统搭载314Ah大容量电芯及直流1500V集成技术。
江苏盐海化工60MWh储能项目并网
8月6日，鹏程无限宣布，江苏盐海化工30MW/60MWh用户侧储能项目6月13日并网发电。项目储能系统核心设备由新能安提供，其中直流侧储能舱由鹏程无限交付。
针对盐海化工的特殊工况，鹏程无限交付的是储蔚D+直流侧储能系统。储蔚D+采用鹏程无限自研314Ah电芯，标准20尺集装箱设计，系统最大RTE效率达96%，辅源功耗降低20%，可放电量提升4%。
远东储能助力独立储能电站并网
8月5日，远东储能宣布，近日，湖北省武汉黄陂区临空产业园50MW/100MWh储能电站并网运行。项目位于湖北省武汉市黄陂区临空产业园内，总装机规模50MW/100MWh。
这是武汉市首座大规模液冷网侧独立储能电站，采用远东储能液冷储能系统解决方案。储能电池采用314Ah磷酸铁锂电芯，核心配置远东储能PowerSTROM 5000液冷储能集装箱，共设置10个5MW/10MWh储能单元。
高特电子高压级联储能项目并网
8月4日，高特电子宣布，近日明阳威俊400MW/2400MWh高压级联储能项目实现全容量成功并网。
据悉，项目坐落于内蒙古包头土默特右旗，高特电子为该项目储能系统提供BMS技术生态全栈解决方案。本次400MW/2400MWh项目顺利并网落地，进一步验证了高特电子BMS技术在大容量高压级联储能赛道的工程落地实力。

The EU has greenlit a €780m ($900m) Dutch state aid scheme to support up to 400MW of green hydrogen production capacity.
The package will award funding by early 2027 through a competitive bidding process, with selected projects receiving 10-year variable per-kilogramme subsidies and direct grants covering up to 80% of investment costs.
Hydrogen from recipients must comply with the EU’s renewable fuel of non-biological origin (RFNBO) criteria.
It follows EU sign-off on the Netherlands’
€290m ($333.4m) sustainable aviation fuel initiative
, which encompasses hydrogen-based fuels, and its
$103m ($117m) green maritime fuels
vessel investment scheme, bringing the tranche of investments to almost €1.18bn ($1.36bn).
The Netherlands is positioning itself as a leading north-west European hydrogen hub, capitalising on extensive gas infrastructure, industrial clusters, and major ports to support the production and import of green hydrogen.
The Port of Rotterdam in particular has become home to huge clean hydrogen investments, and Dutch gas transmission system operators are working closely with neighbours to embed the country in the region’s planned hydrogen pipeline network.
While the Netherlands missed the May 2025 deadline to transpose the EU’s Renewable Energy Directive III, it has since implemented key elements, including the transport and accelerated renewable energy permitting provisions.
Phased amendments to national legislation have brought the country broadly into alignment with many of the directive’s requirements.

title: 4v4 团队格斗游戏《漫威斗魂》发售，Steam 国区 298 元起
content:
IT之家 8 月 6 日消息，集结传奇漫威角色的 4v4 团队格斗游戏《漫威斗魂》今日正式登陆 Steam 平台，本作由知名格斗游戏开发商 ARC SYSTEM WORKS 制作，PlayStation Publishing LLC 发行，国区售价 298 元起。IT之家附游戏商品页（https://store.steampowered.com/app/3787240/_/?l=schinese&cc=cn）。
本作提供三个版本购买，具体定价如下：
- 标准版：298 元
- 数字豪华版：418 元
- 终极版：498 元
集结传奇漫威角色组建战队，激战终极 4v4 团队格斗游戏 —— 由 PlayStation Studios、Arc System Works 与 Marvel Games 倾情奉上。快来打造你的梦之队，在激烈的 4v4 格斗中点燃战魂。首发即可从 20 位经典漫威角色中挑选队员，每位角色均以全新动漫风格精心塑造，并各自隶属于独特的超级英雄或超级反派派系。
《漫威斗魂》核心特色：
- 尝试不同组合，探索全新连招、协同效应与对战策略，在基于漫威宇宙经典场景的动态场地中激战，部分场地包含可互动的场地切换效果
- 战斗体验沉直观，海量招式、连招与策略，值得玩家反复钻研
- 支持传统输入与快捷键自定义，配合简单连招，入门轻松流畅
- 包含 39 项 Steam 成就，支持跨平台多人、家庭共享、Steam 云存档等功能
语言支持方面，本作对简体中文提供完整支持：界面、字幕、音频均为简体中文。游玩本作需要绑定第三方账号，即 PlayStation Account，同时游戏采用 Easy Anti-Cheat 内核级反作弊保护。
最低配置：需要 64 位处理器和操作系统，Windows 11 系统，Intel Core i5-8400 或 AMD Ryzen 5 1600X 处理器，16 GB 内存，NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 6GB 或 AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT 8GB 显卡，需要 27 GB 可用存储空间。
推荐配置：需要 64 位处理器和操作系统，Windows 11 系统，Intel Core i7-8700 或 AMD Ryzen 5 3600X 处理器，16 GB 内存，NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 8 GB 或 AMD Radeon RX 7600 XT 16 GB 显卡，需要 27 GB 可用存储空间。

title: Epic 喜加二：《Beacon Pines》《We Were Here Together》游戏免费领取
content:
IT之家 8 月 6 日消息，Epic 本周送出的游戏是《Beacon Pines》《We Were Here Together》，下周送出的游戏是《Caravan SandWitch》。
领取链接：《Beacon Pines》，《We Were Here Together》
IT之家附《Beacon Pines》游戏简介：
《Beacon Pines》是一款设定在神秘书籍中的可爱而又诡异的冒险游戏。你将同时扮演这本书的读者和主角卢卡。
在老仓库发生了一些奇怪的事情，卢卡和他的朋友们似乎是唯一注意到这一切的人。深夜悄悄溜出去，交新朋友，揭开隐藏的真相，以及收集能够改变命运的词语！
在帮助卢卡调查比肯派恩斯的奇怪事件时，你将收集到特别的金色护符，每个护符上都刻有一个词。这些护符可以在故事的某些关键时刻使用，以填补一个空白词，从而彻底改变接下来的事情。
作为这本书的读者，您将通过《编年史》来探索故事的转折点：一个随着您的选择而分支生长的互动故事树。探索一组事件可以解锁新的魅力，以便在另一条分支上使用，从而让您在完全不同版本的故事之间来回跳跃，以揭开贝肯派恩斯核心的 mysteries。
IT之家附《We Were Here Together》游戏简介：
叫上你的好朋友，启程前往鬼魅游荡的 Castle Rock，依靠沟通和合作两大武器，解决一系列谜题，最终逃出生天！
一切开始于那发点亮黑夜的信号弹，接着便是无线电的求救信息，让你们从梦中惊醒。你的探险家同僚被困南极大陆，而驻守大本营你的们两个必须合作完成救援行动。不过你们可不知道你们惹上了多大的麻烦...
你们要想办法从大本营赶到求救信号的地点。穿过南极的荒芜的冻土之后，迎接你们的是一座充满谜题、秘密和惊险刺激的中世纪城堡。而且你们要独自迎战！唯独智慧和沟通，才能战胜物资的匮乏。细心观察，合作沟通是逃离这所恶灵 Castle Rock 的唯一方法。
对于 We Were Here 系列的老玩家，这次值得期待的东西一点也不少：更多解密、更长的故事主线、全新游戏机制以及隐藏在 Castle Rock 中的各种小彩蛋...
扣人心悬的情节: 揭开城堡背后的黑暗历史，会一会被邪恶腐化的杰斯特。说真的，这家伙到底是人么？
事无巨细的沟通: 为了推动故事进展，沟通可少不了。测试你的语言功底，能不能准确描述周遭环境
绞尽脑汁的谜团: 合作解密，逃出生天。
迷雾笼罩的环境: 探索探险队大本营，冰封的南极山谷，还有充满邪恶气息的 Castle Rock。
注意：本游戏仅支持合作模式。需要两位玩家联网并配有话筒。
交流沟通才能找到出路。
你和你的探险小伙伴必须穿越南极的冰原，潜入一座充满不详气息中世纪城堡。游戏开始，玩家只有一部对讲机。你能想办法和队友保持一个沟通频道么？
为此，你们必须同心协力，合二为一。/i]
浸入式的合作游戏体验，和队友一起绞尽脑汁，挑战紧张刺激的谜题。一同发掘全新的游戏环境和背后不可告人的秘密。
你并非孤身一人...
黑暗吞噬了曾经辉煌一时的 Castle Rock 和周遭的一切。你能找出这所破败的城堡背后的真相，并逃出生天么？还是说，你跑得了一时，却还是逃不过城堡的主人的魔爪呢?

title: 即日起，ChatGPT 可以调用 Adobe Photoshop、Lightroom 来修图、设计了
content:
IT之家 8 月 6 日消息，Adobe 去年底借助 OpenAI 的 Apps SDK，把 Photoshop、Acrobat 和 Adobe Express 带入 ChatGPT。时间来到今天（6 日），合作范围得到进一步扩大，新推出的 Adobe 插件几乎涵盖旗下整套创意软件。
用户安装插件后，可以直接在 ChatGPT 中调用 Photoshop、Premiere、Acrobat、Lightroom、Illustrator 和 InDesign 等 70 多款 Adobe 工具。
IT之家测试发现，用户可以打开 ChatGPT 设置菜单，在插件页面中添加 Adobe 插件。完成设置后，只需在提示词输入框中输入“@Adobe”和具体任务，便可调用相应工具。
Adobe 称，插件与 OpenAI 的 Codex 编程应用及近期发布的 Work 套件配合使用时效果最佳，用户不登录 Creative Cloud 账户也能使用基本功能，登录后则可保存不同会话中的工作进度，并直接访问云端文件。此外，Creative Cloud 账户还可用于调用 Adobe Firefly 提供的生成式 AI 模型。
Adobe 希望用户通过新插件完成照片编辑、营销视频制作和 PDF 生成等任务，同时也不会打算用 ChatGPT 取代现有专业软件。
Adobe Firefly 及智能体 AI 副总裁福雷斯特 · 基表示：“我们希望，无论人们在哪里工作，都能使用 Adobe 的专业级创意和生产力工具。ChatGPT 中的 Adobe 插件并不是创意专业人士每天依赖的旗舰应用的替代品。需要精确操作和充分掌控创作过程时，旗舰应用仍能提供更深入的功能。”

title: 存储涨价后：苹果上调多款 iPhone、iPad、Mac 及安卓手机以旧换新折抵价，最高达 25%
content:
IT之家 8 月 6 日消息，9to5mac 今日发现，苹果悄悄更新了官方以旧换新（Trade In）估价表，上调了多款 iPhone、iPad、Mac 以及 Apple Watch 设备的最高回收价格，部分设备涨幅接近 30%。同时，苹果也在以旧换新列表中新增了谷歌 Pixel 9 系列和一加 13 等 Android 机型。
在 iPhone 产品线中，iPhone 16 Pro Max 的折抵金额从 695 美元上调至 720 美元，iPhone 16 Pro 从 560 美元上调至 630 美元，涨幅约 12.5%。
iPhone 15 Pro Max 从 490 美元升至 530 美元，iPhone 14 Pro Max 从 375 美元升至 405 美元。此外，iPhone 13 Pro 从 260 美元涨至 285 美元，iPhone 12 Pro Max 从 220 美元涨至 240 美元。
Mac 产品线的调整幅度较为显著。Mac Studio 从 1045 美元大幅上涨至 1305 美元，涨幅约 25%；MacBook Pro 从 690 美元涨至 855 美元，MacBook Air 从 520 美元涨至 580 美元，Mac mini 从 375 美元涨至 480 美元。iMac 从 355 美元涨至 380 美元，Mac Pro 从 2045 美元涨至 2195 美元。
iPad 方面，iPad Pro 由 690 美元提升至 720 美元，iPad Air 由 460 美元提升至 490 美元，iPad mini 由 265 美元提升至 300 美元，标准版 iPad 最高回收价格则由 235 美元提升至 260 美元。
Apple Watch 系列中，Apple Watch Series 10 最高回收价格由 150 美元提高至 165 美元，Apple Watch Series 9 由 130 美元提高至 135 美元，Apple Watch Series 8 由 90 美元提高至 95 美元，Apple Watch Series 7 由 65 美元提高至 70 美元。
值得一提的是，苹果以旧换新价格通常为“最高估值”，实际金额会根据设备型号、年份、存储配置以及外观和功能状态进行评估。
另外，苹果此次新增了部分可参与回收的机型，包括三星 Galaxy S21 Ultra 5G、Google Pixel 9 Pro XL、Google Pixel 9 Pro、Google Pixel 9、OnePlus 13 以及 OnePlus 13R 等型号。
部分安卓手机估值也有所变化，例如三星 Galaxy S22+ 5G 最高回收价格由 80 美元提升至 85 美元，三星 Galaxy S22 5G 由 80 美元提升至 85 美元；Google Pixel 8 Pro 则由 165 美元下调至 155 美元，Google Pixel 7 Pro 由 95 美元调整至 90 美元。
苹果表示，设备最终可获得的回收抵扣金额可能因产品状况、上市年份以及具体配置有所不同，并非所有设备都符合换购抵扣条件。
