title: Ford Fathom Electric Pickup Starts at $29,945
content:
Automotive & Mobility

The automaker's new battery-electric truck matches Maverick hybrid pricing while offering compact SUV interior room & hands-free driving.
August 6, 2026
1 Min Read
The name of Ford's upcoming mid-size EV pickup truck.
Ford Motor Co.
At a Glance
Starting price of $29,945 includes destination charges, matching Ford's Maverick hybrid pickup.
Interior space exceeds Toyota RAV4 compact SUV with frunk and bi-directional charging included.
BlueCruise hands-free driver assistance available via subscription on all Fathom models.
Ford has continued the slow drip of news for its upcoming
low-priced battery-electric pickup truck
, with the announcement of the name Fathom and the starting price of $29,945, including destination charges. That’s almost exactly the same as the company’s
Maverick mid-sized hybrid-electric pickup
, for comparison.
Pre-ordering will open early next year, and Ford has revealed that the Fathom will have more interior space than a Toyota RAV4 compact SUV. There is an Apple CarPlay/Android Auto-supporting touch screen infotainment system (in contrast to the bring-your-own-device philosophy of would-be rival Slate), a frunk, and bi-directional charging capability.
Ford has not yet announced a switch from the costly DC bi-directional charging seen in the
F-150 Lightning
that necessitates a costly home inverter to the more affordable AC bi-directional charging that does not, but it would be in keeping with the Fathom’s cost-effective approach.
Additionally, every Fathom will be able to employ Ford’s subscription-based BlueCruise hands-free driver assistance system.
Kay Hart, general manager for Ford’s Model e electrification effort, says that the company “scoured the Ford archives, looking at how this company has named vehicles for more than a century.”
But after naming the current hybrid-electric mid-size pickup after Ford’s second-generation compact sedan, the Maverick, the company passed over the name from its original compact sedan, the Falcon, in favor of Fathom. This name communicates the notion of depth below the surface, according to Hart.
Prospective buyers will probably be more concerned with the price of options and Fathom’s capabilities than the truck’s name. We’ll find out in 2027, when Ford starts delivering them.

title: CoreWeave Enters APAC Data Center Race With Indonesia Expansion
content:
CoreWeave is expanding its AI cloud platform into Asia-Pacific, announcing plans for three facilities in Indonesia to establish its first regional footprint. The Greater Jakarta deployment totals 360 MW of contracted IT power and is expected to come online in 2028, serving AI labs, startups, enterprises, and government customers across Southeast Asia.
The expansion comes as AI infrastructure providers build regional capacity to reduce latency and meet data residency requirements, moving compute closer to customers as enterprise AI adoption spreads beyond North America and Europe.
“CoreWeave goes where we can bring AI pioneers the capacity, performance, and reliability they need to build and scale their ideas,” Chief Operating Officer Sachin Jain said in a statement. “Indonesia is investing heavily in AI education and digital capacity, and it’s paying off. The country is becoming one of Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing destinations for global tech investment.”
Related:
Do We Really Need Mega Next-Gen Data Center Campuses?
CoreWeave will lease the facilities from an unnamed colocation provider while owning and operating the compute environment. The 360 MW represents the combined critical IT load across the three sites, a company spokesperson told
Data Center Knowledge
Global Push
The Indonesia deployment signals more than geographic expansion for the
neocloud
provider, according to Dave McCarthy, research vice president for cloud and edge infrastructure at IDC.
“CoreWeave is signaling that it intends to compete globally against legacy hyperscalers, transitioning from a North American and European player into a global AI infrastructure platform,” McCarthy said. “Securing this level of scale in APAC establishes first-mover advantage as regional enterprise AI adoption ramps up toward 2028.”
The move extends CoreWeave’s rapid infrastructure buildout. As of March 31, 2026, the company operated 49 data centers worldwide with more than 1 GW of active power and more than 3.5 GW of contracted power supporting AI workloads. Indonesia will be the first location for its data center footprint in Asia-Pacific.
CoreWeave has grown rapidly from a specialized GPU cloud provider into one of the industry’s largest AI infrastructure platforms, competing with hyperscale cloud providers for AI training and inference workloads.
Why Indonesia?
Rather than entering more established markets such as Singapore or Japan, CoreWeave said it chose Indonesia for its growing AI ecosystem and investments in digital infrastructure.
“CoreWeave picked Indonesia because the country has already built AI infrastructure momentum, heavy government and private investment in data centers, and AI education, making it a natural entry point into Southeast Asia, not because it beat out a shortlist of rivals,” a company spokesperson said.
Related:
New Data Center Developments: August 2026
McCarthy said Indonesia also offers practical advantages over more mature regional markets.
“Indonesia offers what traditional tier-1 hubs like Singapore or Tokyo currently struggle with: scalable power availability, ample land, and strong national tailwinds for digital infrastructure,” he said. “While mature markets face severe power constraints and higher operating costs, Indonesia provides CoreWeave the physical runway required for a mega-scale buildout right at the demographic center of Southeast Asia’s booming digital economy.”
CoreWeave said the investment supports Indonesia’s efforts to strengthen digital infrastructure, expand domestic AI capabilities, and position itself as a leading regional digital economy. The company also plans to hire and train an operations team in Indonesia.
The company declined to identify its colocation partner.
Regional Compute
The expansion reflects a broader shift in AI infrastructure. Early AI investments centered on massive training clusters in the US and Europe. As inference workloads grow and governments adopt stricter data residency requirements, enterprises want AI infrastructure located closer to users and data.
Related:
Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta Pivot from Buy to Build in AI
“We are seeing the transition from centralized global AI clusters to localized, sovereign AI deployments,” McCarthy said. “As AI workloads shift from raw foundation model training to real-time inference and domain-specific fine-tuning, latency constraints and strict data residency regulations mandate in-country compute. Deploying native AI cloud infrastructure directly within regional borders is becoming a hard requirement for enterprise and public-sector adoption across Asia.”
CoreWeave said the Indonesia deployment is being driven by both existing customer demand and anticipated growth across Southeast Asia. Enterprises, AI-native companies, and governments require AI compute to be close to their data and users due to latency-sensitive workloads and data locality requirements, the company said.
The announcement comes as Cushman & Wakefield research reveals that Asia-Pacific’s data center development pipeline hit a record 26.5 GW in the first half of 2026, driven by surging demand from hyperscalers, cloud providers, and AI platforms.
With 7.1 GW added to the pipeline and 1.4 GW of operational capacity delivered, the region is witnessing unprecedented growth in digital infrastructure. Southeast Asia, in particular, has emerged as a key growth engine, accounting for nearly 50% of under-construction capacity.
While CoreWeave declined to discuss additional Asia-Pacific projects, it said the company will continue expanding as customer demand grows.
The deployment marks CoreWeave’s first step into the region. More broadly, it reflects the next phase of AI infrastructure, as providers compete not only on the scale of their GPU clusters but also on their ability to deliver regional cloud platforms that satisfy enterprise requirements for performance, regulatory compliance, and data sovereignty.

title: Do Data Centers Really Drive Up Local Temperatures?
content:
There is plenty of talk in the data center industry about
cooling methods
and how best to dissipate heat from facilities.
However, what happens when the heat leaves a data center and is absorbed into the surrounding area? Does it raise temperatures, and if so, by how much?
These are important aspects to explore, especially as local communities
become more sensitive
to the impact of data centers on their surroundings.
Do Data Centers Contribute to Local Temperature Increases?
All the heat produced inside data centers needs to go somewhere, and in most cases, it is the area immediately surrounding them.
The result is localized
temperature increases
of up to 16 degrees Fahrenheit (around 8 degrees Celsius), according to researchers who
examined
how data centers can create localized “heat islands.”
Notably, that study examined the impact of large-scale AI data centers on local temperatures. It is not clear whether smaller data centers can raise local temperatures to the same extent.
Related:
Evaporative Cooling in Data Centers: Why the Industry Hesitates to Move On
Another study
focused on facilities in the Phoenix area. It concluded that data centers raised overall local temperatures by about 4 degrees Fahrenheit. However, it also found that air directly emitted from data centers could be up to 25 degrees higher.
Thus, it seems clear that data centers do have a measurable, albeit variable, impact on local temperatures.
Data Centers vs. Other Sources of Localized Temperature Increases
On balance, it is worth noting that data centers are not the only entities that raise local temperatures as a byproduct of their operations.
Office buildings
also do the same thing. So do
parked cars
– especially dark-colored ones sitting in the sun, which can raise ambient temperatures by nearly 7 degrees Fahrenheit.
Paved surfaces
, too, are a significant source of heat islands in urban areas.
Ways to Keep the Area Around Data Centers Cooler
So, it is not just data centers that can make life hotter for people and animals living in their vicinity. However, given the increasing
controversy
surrounding data center projects, data center operators are liable to face especially strong scrutiny of their facilities’ impact on local temperatures.
One impactful change data centers could make is
switching from evaporative cooling
, which emits significant heat into the environment by using moisture to extract and release heat.
Liquid cooling systems generally have less impact on ambient temperatures, especially when they circulate heated coolant through media like the ground, which absorbs most of the heat. However, liquid cooling systems are significantly more expensive to install and operate.
Related:
Turning Off the Tap: The Case for Seawater Cooling in Data Centers
Discharging heat
into nearby bodies of water is another possible solution. The caveat to this approach is that it would heat the water, potentially creating new issues. However, this may be tolerable in warmer climates where aquatic life has already adapted to high water temperatures.
A highly effective way to keep areas near data centers cooler is to distribute heated air or coolant more evenly, preventing heat from concentrating. However, this would require infrastructure to distribute heat over dozens of miles, a complex and costly undertaking.
In short, most data centers currently have limited options to keep ambient temperatures low. But in contexts where minimizing localized temperature increases is a high priority, solutions exist – they just cost a lot.

title: Hinton, Fei-Fei Li, and Andrew Ng Clash Over AI Risks at Ai4
content:
LAS VEGAS — Three influential AI researchers offered sharply different visions for the technology’s future during a rare joint appearance at the Ai4 conference on Wednesday, debating everything from superintelligence and mass job displacement to open-weight models and government regulation.
The session, billed as “The Architects of Intelligence: A Historic Convergence,” brought together Geoffrey Hinton, a pioneering deep learning researcher and AI safety advocate; Fei-Fei Li, co-director of the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI; and Andrew Ng, founder of DeepLearning.AI and Landing AI. In a wide-ranging discussion, they explored where AI is headed and what it means for business, policymakers, and society. While all three agreed AI will transform nearly every industry, they differed on how quickly the technology will surpass human capabilities, how disruptive it will be for workers, and how aggressively governments should intervene.
Related:
FLOPS vs Megawatts: Who’s Winning in 2026 Supercomputing?
On stage at the Ai4 conference: (from left to right) Fei-Fei Li; Geoffrey Hinton; panel moderator Yun-Hee Kim, Deputy Editor at Washington Post Intelligence; and Andrew Ng. (Photo: Shane Snider)
The debate matters far beyond Silicon Valley. Data center developers, utilities, and infrastructure investors are
committing unprecedented capital
to AI, betting that demand will continue to climb for years. Yet the panel underscored that even the technology’s architects disagree on the speed of AI’s progress, the economic disruption it will cause, and the regulatory framework that could influence how quickly new AI infrastructure is built.
Hinton Warns AI May Surpass Humans Within Two Decades
Hinton, often referred to as the “godfather of AI,” said artificial intelligence could surpass human intelligence within the next five to 20 years.
“I think it’s going to be smarter than us,” Hinton said.
He argued that AI will eliminate many forms of routine intellectual work, comparing today’s white-collar occupations to manual labor displaced by mechanization.
“If AI can do routine intellectual labor, any job that consists mainly of routine intellectual labor is going to be done by AI,” Hinton said.
Hinton also warned about
AI-enabled cyberattacks
, the concentration of power among leading AI companies, and what he sees as the need for stronger government oversight before increasingly capable models are deployed.
Ng Pushes Back on Job Loss Narrative
Ng challenged the notion that AI is already causing widespread job losses, arguing that current evidence points instead toward workers becoming more productive by using AI tools.
“The people who thrive in the future are people working with AI,” he said.
Rather than replacing entire professions, Ng said AI is automating individual tasks while enabling employees to take on broader responsibilities. He urged workers to learn to use AI effectively rather than competing directly with it.
Related:
Do We Really Need Mega Next-Gen Data Center Campuses?
Ng also defended open-weight models, arguing they are critical to maintaining competition and preventing a handful of companies from controlling access to advanced AI technologies – particularly as China expands its own AI ecosystem.
Ng backs open-weight models to spur competition and access to advanced AI. (Photo: Shane Snider)
Li Urges Practical Governance and Public Investment
Li repeatedly called for a more measured conversation, arguing that public debate has become dominated by extreme narratives that obscure practical questions about deployment, education, and policy.
“We cannot have a rational debate,” she said, if discussions continue to be driven by fear rather than evidence.
She argued that AI should be viewed primarily as a tool that augments human capabilities while policymakers update existing regulatory frameworks in sectors such as healthcare, transportation, finance, and education, rather than imposing sweeping AI-specific restrictions.
Li also called for greater public investment in AI research and education, describing AI as foundational infrastructure whose long-term development should not be driven solely by private companies.
Related:
IDCA CEO Calls for Global Consensus on Data Center Development
Li urges sector-specific policy updates over sweeping AI rules, focusing on deployment. (Photo: Shane Snider)
Open-Weight Models Divide AI Leaders
The panel also revealed deep divisions over how open model weights should be.
Hinton argued that openly releasing model weights could make it easier for malicious actors to adapt advanced models for cyberattacks and other harmful uses.
Ng countered that open-weight models are essential to innovation, competition, and broader access to AI technology.
Li rejected framing the issue as a simple choice between open and closed models, arguing that different applications require different levels of openness depending on their risks.
Shared Optimism, Different Paths for AI and Infrastructure
Asked what headline she hopes to see within five years, Li avoided making predictions about model capabilities. Instead, she said she hopes AI becomes as invisible as electricity – powering breakthroughs in healthcare, literacy, scientific discovery, and food security without becoming the story itself.
Hinton closed on a more cautious note, saying AI could dramatically improve living standards if society addresses its risks before they become crises.
The discussion offered no consensus on AI’s future. Instead, it highlighted that even among the researchers whose work laid the foundation for modern AI, there remains profound disagreement over how quickly the technology will evolve, how disruptive it will become, and what guardrails should govern its deployment – questions that will shape the
infrastructure investments
now transforming the
global data center industry

title: Australia home battery volumes triple year-on-year - Energy Storage
content: Australian home battery energy storage installation volumes have roughly tripled their year-on-year level since the Cheaper Home Batteries scheme began July 2025, according to Sunwiz data. Installation volumes were 990 MWh in June 2026, down 1.55% on the previous month but significantly up on the 320 MWh recorded in July 2025. The slight decline in monthly installation volumes was reflected in states and territories data. South Australia, the Australian Capital Territory (ACT), and Western Australia (WA) saw residential battery growth, while Victoria, Northern Territory (NT) and Tasmania returned negative volumes, with New South Wales steady. National residential ESS registrations | Image: SunWiz SunWiz managing director Warwick Johnston said the capacity registered in July 2026 was roughly comparable to that registered in June, because systems installed in April were still being registered in in June. “Our analysis of installation month figures that eliminate the smoothing effects seen in our charts reveals a market that is quickly recovering,” Johnston said. “June is likely to be 750 MWh and July 945 MWh – far lower than the 3.2 GWh installed in April but comparable to volumes in October 2025.” The national average size for a system installation was 22.6 kWh in July, marking the third straight month of decline from April’s 44 kWh. The average installation size in August 2025 was 20.7 kWh National average system size fell to 22.60 kWh in July | Image: SunWiz July’s national average system size of 22.6 kWh also marks a third straight monthly decline from April’s 44 kWh and June’s 26.16 kWh, though remains above the August 2025 average size of 20.7 kWh. As the market shifts toward smaller capacities, Victoria’s average system size now sits at 29.94 kWh, well above all other states and territories, which range from 17.69 kWh in Western Australia and 21.72 kWh in the Australian Capital Territory, Tasmania and the Northern Territory. title: CIP reaches financial close on co-located solar project with 750 MWh battery in Mexico - Energy Storage
content: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) has made ist final investment decision on the 420 MW La Esperanza Solar project, combined with a 150 MW/750 MWh BESS in Mexico. The co-located project in Campeche, on Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula, is the first CIP investment in Mexico to reach financial close. CIP said the project will strengthen system reliability, resilience and flexibility in a region where electricity demand has increased the need for both power generation and storage capacity. Construction is underway, with commercial operations expected in 2028. The project’s five-hour BESS will be one of the largest in Mexico when commissioned. Mexico’s Ministry of Energy has recognized La Esperanza Solar as a priority project in the country’s planning framework and the solar and BESS installation is being developed in close coordination with the federal government and other relevant authorities, according to CIP. The La Esperanza Solar has been developed through CIP’s Growth Markets Fund II (GMF II). The project financing comprises approximately $510 million in debt facilities provided by a consortium of five international and regional commercial banks: BNP Paribas, JPMorgan Chase Bank, Natixis CIB, Santander and Scotiabank. Equity is funded by the project owners: CI Growth Markets Fund II with an expected co-investment from leading Mexican retirement fund administrator, Profuturo. Peter Halmø, head of Latin America and managing director at CIP, said reaching financial close was a major milestone for the GMF II fund. “We have been active in Mexico for several years, and this will be our first project in the country to start construction – a step that reflects both the strength of the team and project and the close collaboration with contractors, authorities, and partners,” Halmø said. “Pairing solar with battery storage is central to bringing more renewable energy onto the Mexican grid, and we are proud to help build a more reliable, lower-carbon power system.” The post CIP reaches financial close on co-located solar project with 750 MWh battery in Mexico appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: Eolian starts building 1 GWh battery project for PJM data centers in Ohio - Energy Storage
content: Eolian has started construction on its 200 MW/1.06 GWh Flint Grid battery energy storage project in Licking County, Ohio. The 5.3-hour duration system is being built next to the New Albany data center and industrial load and is the largest BESS in Ohio and on the PJM grid footprint. Eolian is working with grid operators, regulators, and other industry stakeholders on research and policy measures to fully integrate big batteries into wholesale electricity markets. These measures include devising technical frameworks for optimal bidding protocols, new market products for energy storage participation, resource adequacy and capacity accreditation, as well as revenue optimization across multiple wholesale market segments. Eolian’s founder and CEO, Aaron Zubaty, emphasized the developer’s position that BESS can provide fast responding, flexible capacity to back up and stabilize the traditional grid. He added that projects like Flint Grid should be recognized for their ability to balance demand from data centers and other heavy industrial energy users. According to the Flint Grid Project website, the facility is being constructed very near a completed Amazon AWS data center, as well as a Meta data center and a Google data center both under construction. “There’s growing consternation about how the US can rapidly scale infrastructure to support America’s growing electricity demand, but not nearly enough conversation about how to use existing technology to unlock the wasted capacity that already exists on the grid” said Zubaty. “Flint Grid demonstrates how companies like Eolian have been investing in solutions to unlock the grid and reduce price pressures on consumers using proven and scalable technology. This project requires hundreds of millions of dollars to construct, and we committed the necessary capital and resources years before today’s demand forecasts became headline news.” The CEO called on policymakers to avoid undermining long-term investments that could make good use of existing transmission infrastructure as they consider changes to competitive electricity markets. Eolian’s Flint Grid BESS is the first grid-scale BESS permitted by the Ohio Siting Board and is the first large-scale battery energy storage system to qualify for the PJM capacity market and the largest battery storage system to clear the 2027/28 Residual Capacity Auction, representing more than 50% of all new battery storage capacity in that capacity year. It has been in development since 2018 and is expected to begin commercial operation ahead of the 2027-2028 PJM capacity year. Besides Flint Grid, Eolian has funded or developed more than 4 GW of commercialized BESS projects across the United States. In Jan. 2026, Eolian, which is backed by Global Infrastructure Partners, now part of BlackRock, partnered with data center developer CyrusOne on a new data center in Texas that will use the existing grid interconnection owned by Eolian’s Chishold Grid BESS. Microgrid Also in Ohio, Veolia has been selected as a project developer to operate and maintain a 350 MW microgrid and 430 MWh BESS which will support an unnamed data center, providing 100% of its power requirements and taking it off the main electricity grid. The microgrid will integrate BESS, gas engines, linear generators, and medium-voltage infrastructure. It will be located in New Albany and according to local news outlet The Columbus Dispatch Veolia was asked not to name the client and it has been brought on to the project ahead of its commercial readiness. Besides energy, Veolia specializes in water and waste management worldwide. “Our work on this project shows how Veolia can help developers accelerate speed-to-power while maintaining the reliability required for mission-critical AI operations, all while protecting the community,” said Karin Hamel, CEO of Veolia Energy, North America and Chief Growth Officer for Veolia in North America. Meanwhile, the West Chicago City Council announced a temporary 180-day moratorium on new data centers and BESS on July 20. The council said the temporary ban would give it time to study their uses and benefits and consider zoning policies for data centers and BESS being proposed throughout the Chicago region. According to the City’s statement, West Chicago’s current zoning rules do not fully address “the unique features” of data centers and battery energy storage systems. “The moratorium preserves current conditions while the City determines whether additional regulations are needed to protect the community and support its long-term goals,” the statement added. The City can extend or end the moratorium before the 180-day period is complete. The City is asking residents, businesses, property owners, emergency responders, utility providers, industry representatives, and other interested stakeholders to help shape its approach. title: Hydrostor signs offtake agreement for CAES project in southern California - Energy Storage
content: Canadian compressed air energy storage (CAES) developer Hydrostor has signed an offtake agreement for its 500 MW/4,000 MWh project in Kern County, California. Hydrostor and local power provider Clean Energy Alliance have signed an agreement covering 60 MW, providing a level of revenue certainty for the under-construction Willow Rock Energy Storage Center. On-site work at the Willow Rock project began in July 2026, after securing a permit from the California Energy Commission in December 2025. Willow Rock Energy Storage Center is Hydrostor’s first utility-scale project in the United States. The CAES developer has an operational 2 MW demonstration project deployed in 2020 in Ontario, Canada. Hydrostor’s CAES works by mining underground caverns using established hard-rock mining techniques. The company then floods the caverns and when air is compressed in, it displaces water to the surface. This creates constant pressure, making the system space efficient. Jon Norman, president of Hydrostor, told pv magazine in May that the company’s CAES system can achieve around 60% to 65% round-trip efficiency. In a press release, Hydrostor chief commercial officer Jordan Cole described the offtake agreement for Willow Rock as a “key milestone” for the project, as the company begins significant works on the project site. Greg Wade, CEO of CEA, said investing in long-duration energy storage would allow the provider to capture excess solar energy during peak production for discharge when demand is high. “This innovative facility in Kern County will play a vital role in helping CEA meet both state reliability mandates and our customers’ growing energy needs with clean, dependable capacity,” Wade said. title: Revera Energy breaks ground on first asset in 2 GWh Scottish BESS portfolio - Energy Storage
content: Revera Energy has started construction on the 200 MW/400 MWh Windyhill battery energy storage system (BESS) in Bearsden, Scotland. The London-headquartered company is backed by global investment firm Carlyle which set it up in 2025. To date, it has several projects underway in the United Kingdom and Australia. Windyhill is Revera’s first Scottish battery to break ground, moving into the construction phase just under eight months after Revera achieved financial close on the project in February via non-recourse senior debt financing – a secured loan – provided by Santander CIB. Besides Windyhill, Revera has two other BESS projects in Scotland – the Hunterson and Kincardine batteries – both are 400 MW, four-hour duration systems (800 MWh storage capacity). The trio of batteries are backed by an investment of more than GBP 500 million ($665 million) and represent almost 2 GWh of energy storage capacity on Scotland’s grid in an area prone to transmission bottlenecks due to high levels of wind generation. Commenting on the ground breaking at Windyhill, Revera Energy’s UK acting head and operating partner at Carlyle, Ron Kiecana, said the development reflects the caliber and dedication of the team. “Today marks a defining milestone for Revera in Scotland,” said Kiecana. “I could not be prouder of what this group has built together, and I’m just as excited for what lies ahead as we work toward a full gigawatt of storage under construction across Scotland by year’s end.” GE Vernova is on board as Windyhill’s technology partner, while Mitie and OCU are delivery partners on site. Danske Commodities will provide route-to-market services when the BESS begins commercial operations, targeted for the first quarter of 2028. Revera has also entered a 10-year revenue floor deal with Danske Commodities covering 100% of project capacity. title: Batch eFT.3 Review: A 28 MPH fat tire e-bike built for the streets
content:
Micah Toll
| Aug 7 2026 - 6:15 am PT
Fat tire e-bikes have become synonymous with rugged adventure. Browse the category and you’d think every 20-inch fat tire bike is destined for sandy beaches, forest trails, or rocky singletrack. In reality, though, most of them spend their lives on city streets, bike paths, and neighborhood roads.
That’s what makes the
Batch Bicycles eFT.3
refreshing. Instead of pretending to be an off-road machine, it embraces what many riders are actually looking for: a comfortable, practical commuter that happens to ride on fat tires.
The first clue is in the tires themselves.
While they’re the familiar 20×4-inch size, Batch skipped the aggressive knobby tread in favor of a smoother, commuter-oriented pattern.
Combined with a suspension fork and an included suspension seatpost, the setup is designed less for conquering trails and more for soaking up potholes, expansion joints, cracked pavement, and all the other imperfections that make urban riding uncomfortable.
Check them out in my video review below to see what I mean.
That philosophy of a road-focused commuter e-bike carries throughout the rest of the bike.
The eFT.3 arrives commuter-ready with full-coverage fenders, integrated front and rear LED lighting, and a sturdy rear rack. Those aren’t glamorous accessories, but they’re the kind of equipment that makes an e-bike more useful as a transportation tool.
Even riders who never intentionally venture out in the rain will appreciate fenders after rolling through a puddle or wet streets, and the rear rack means groceries or a work bag don’t have to live on your back.
Visually, the bike also stands out in a sea of matte black e-bikes. My test bike’s bright blue paint gives it plenty of personality without being flashy, and it’s a welcome change from the increasingly monochrome e-bike market.
I know they say that black is the best-selling bicycle color, but it’s just so boring. Give me colors, please!
Power comes from a 750W rear hub motor paired with a torque sensor, and it’s a combination that works well. The torque sensor gives pedal assist a much more natural feel than the cadence sensors found on many entry-level fat tire bikes, while the Class 3 setup provides pedal assist all the way to 28 mph (45 km/h).
The throttle is limited to 20 mph (32 km/h), as required for Class 2 e-bikes, but having that higher assisted top speed makes longer commutes feel much more practical.
The motor itself has no shortage of power. It accelerates confidently and never feels like it’s struggling.
There is one catch, however.
It’s loud.
Not just slightly louder than average, but noticeably so whenever you accelerate. Performance isn’t affected, and some riders won’t care, but if you’ve grown accustomed to the whisper-quiet motors appearing on many newer e-bikes, it’s something you’ll immediately notice.
A 48V, 15Ah LG battery provides 720 Wh of capacity, which is a healthy size for this category. As always, real-world range depends on speed, rider weight, terrain, and assist level, but it’s large enough that I never found myself worrying about making it home.
Component-wise, Batch seems to have made practical compromises .
The Shimano Tourney 7-speed drivetrain sits at the bottom of Shimano’s lineup, and no one is going to mistake it for premium equipment. Still, this isn’t a performance bike chasing lap times or trying to impress anyone with mid-shelf or top-shelf components. For commuting and everyday riding, it shifts reliably and gets the job done. It will probably require more frequent maintenance and you should avoid smacking it on any curbs, but it gets the job done.
The Tektro hydraulic disc brakes, on the other hand, punch above their weight. Equipped with 180 mm rotors, they offer confident stopping power with the predictable feel and lower maintenance that hydraulic systems are known for.
One design decision I particularly appreciated is something the bike
have: a folding frame.
Many 20-inch fat tire e-bikes include a folding mechanism
simply because that’s become the norm. But the reality is that plenty of owners never fold their bikes. In fact, there’s a good chance that the
majority
of folding e-bike owners never fold their bikes.
Overall, the eFT.3 feels like a company that understood its assignment. It isn’t trying to convince riders they’re buying an electric mountain bike simply because it has fat tires. Instead, it’s a comfortable, practical urban commuter that uses those oversized tires to improve ride quality rather than trail capability.
The loud motor is my biggest criticism, and at an
MSRP of $1,999
(currently discounted to
around $1,799
through September), it isn’t competing in the budget category. The Shimano Tourney drivetrain is also fairly basic, especially at that price point. But one could argue that those compromises are partially balanced by thoughtful commuter features, a large battery, hydraulic brakes, Class 3 performance, and a comfortable ride that feels purpose-built for everyday transportation.
If your riding consists primarily of pavement, bike paths, and city streets, and you appreciate the confidence and comfort that fat tires provide, the Batch Bicycles eFT.3 is well worth a closer look. It’s proof that not every fat tire e-bike needs to dream of mountain trails – sometimes the best adventure is simply making your daily ride more enjoyable.

Mitsubishi is joining the rapidly growing ranks of robot builders, with plans to build up to 1,000 of its Highlanders humanoid robots per month at one of the automaker’s ICE engine plants in Kyoto – and if the plan comes together, the automaker could begin mass-producing its new worker-bots as early as next year.
While the normals probably think of Mitsubishi as primarily an also-ran automaker

By utilizing humanoid robots in our own manufacturing facilities and supporting the production of Highlanders products, we aim to leverage the outcomes of this collaboration to drive our growth and enhance corporate value.”

Highlanders and humanoids, by Mitsubishi.

content:

Subaru’s
big EV incentives have helped boost sales, but they’re quickly taking a toll on the company’s profits.
Subaru spends big to sell new EVs in the US
Subaru now sells three electric SUVs in the US, including the updated Solterra, the Uncharted, and Trailseeker.
While the two new electric SUVs, the Uncharted and Trailseeker, have helped boost overall EV sales, they are taking a big hit on Subaru’s profits.
Between the three, Subaru has
sold 11,638 electric vehicles
through July. While Solterra sales are down 34% this year (5,275), the Uncharted (2,850) and Trailseeker (3,513) have led to a higher overall total.
After reporting
fiscal first-quarter earnings
on Wednesday, Subaru said incentive spending resulted in a ¥24.9 billion ($155 million) hit to profits.
According to new data from Motor Intelligence (via
Automotive News
), Subaru’s marketing costs per vehicle rose 40% to $2,698.
Incentives on gas-powered cars, including the BRZ, Outback, and Legacy, increased 27% on average, while truck spending rose 49%.
2027 Subaru Trailseeker (Source: Subaru)
Average spending on EVs was considerably higher. Subaru spent $9,650 for the Solterra, $9,155 for the Uncharted, and $8,982 for the Trailseeker on average. In comparison, average spending on the Outback was just $3,036.
Subaru’s overall incentives were still lower than the average of $3,479, but its 40% increase significantly outpaced the market, which rose 4.4%.
Higher spending led to a 44% drop in Subaru’s operating profit, which totaled ¥42.6 billion ($270 million) in the fiscal first quarter.
2027 Subaru Uncharted (Source: Subaru)
Subaru’s electric SUVs share a platform and are developed in partnership with Toyota. Toyota also sells three electric SUVs in the US, including the new bZ, C-HR, and bZ Woodland.
While Solterra sales have slipped this year, the Toyota bZ is among the top-selling EVs in the US. In the first half of the year, the bZ was the
fourth-most-popular EV

title: Telo raises its tiny electric truck's tow rating to 8,000 lbs
content:
TELO Trucks
Fred Lambert
| Aug 7 2026 - 7:06 am PT
Telo is raising the tow rating on its Mini-sized electric truck to 8,000 lbs, up from the 6,600 lbs it previously advertised.
The startup says months of real-world towing convinced it the little MT1 can safely pull more than a truck that size looks like it should. That new number puts a 152-inch pickup roughly on par with a base Ford F-150.
Co-founder and CTO Forest North announced the change in a video, framing it around his own needs. “In the beginning, we set a stake in the ground that we wanted to be able to tow over 6,000 pounds. I personally have a travel trailer and I wanted to make sure that I could tow that,” he said. “Now that we’re further into it, we have towed a bunch of things. We understand towing and what this vehicle can do.”
The MT1 is about as small as a modern pickup gets. At 152 inches long, it’s the size of an electric Mini Cooper, yet it carries a full 60-to-96-inch bed and seats up to five. It runs a dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup rated at 500 hp, with a 77 kWh standard pack good for 260 miles or a 106 kWh long-range pack rated at 350-plus miles. Telo starts it at $41,520 and is targeting first deliveries in late 2026.
Why Telo thinks a small truck can tow big
North’s argument leans on the physics that favor an electric drivetrain when there’s a trailer on the hitch.
The first is braking. A four-wheel-drive electric truck that can move a lot of power in and out of its pack can regen down a long grade almost indefinitely, he argues, instead of cooking its brakes. “That means that we can regen for miles and miles and miles going down a pass — you’re not touching your brakes and yet you have complete control over your vehicle and your trailer,” North said.
Heat is the other half of it. Combustion trucks dump most of their energy as heat and then have to shed even more of it under load, which is exactly what SAE’s J2807 tow standard is built to stress with tests like the 11-mile, 6% Davis Dam grade run. North says that math barely applies to an EV: “For us, it really doesn’t change the equation that much. We have so much torque and so much horsepower together, and it’s instant. That makes starting on a grade so easy.”
Then there’s the packaging. The MT1’s hitch sits close to the rear axle, giving a shorter lever arm so trailer tongue weight doesn’t lift the front end the way it would on a longer truck. And despite its footprint, the MT1 isn’t light — North puts it at over 4,000 lbs — riding on a steel chassis with a crossmember tying the hitch to the frame. Small, in his telling, is a structural advantage: the same strength takes less mass than it would on a full-size truck.
North was blunt about the limits. For long hauls, “a big diesel truck is probably going to be better for the near term.” The MT1’s pitch is shorter trips, where a compact, easy-to-park truck that tows well is more convenient than a full-size rig.
The 8,000-lb number unlocks a new class of trailer
The jump from 6,600 to 8,000 lbs isn’t a random bump. It’s aimed at a wave of trailers that carry their own batteries and motors.
Telo already showed this off in July, when
the MT1 towed Pebble’s 5,800-lb Flow electric travel trailer
. The Flow’s “Easy Tow” active propulsion system uses the trailer’s own drivetrain and regen to cut the effective load on the tow vehicle, which is how a truck the size of a Mini pulled a full-size camper without drama. North says a lot of these new powered trailers land in the 6,000-to-8,000-lb range, so the higher rating is what lets the MT1 be a real option for them.
That same electrical headroom is what makes the regen story credible. Telo
confirmed 400 kW sustained charging
for the MT1 in June, running a dual 800V/400V pack architecture. A truck that can absorb that many kilowatts on a charger can also absorb a lot of regen coming down a hill.
How 8,000 lbs stacks up against other trucks
Against full-size electric pickups, 8,000 lbs is on the low end. But the point isn’t the number on its own — it’s the number relative to the size of the truck.
Here’s where the MT1 lands:
Telo MT1 (152 in): 8,000 lbs
Ford F-150 Lightning: 10,000 lbs
Tesla Cybertruck: 11,000 lbs
Rivian R1T: 11,000 lbs
GMC Hummer EV pickup: 12,000 lbs
Chevy Silverado EV: 12,500 lbs
For gas comparison, a 2025 F-150 tows anywhere from about 8,400 lbs with the base 2.7L V6 up to 13,500 lbs fully optioned. So Telo’s tiny truck now claims to tow roughly what an entry-level full-size F-150 does, in a package nearly four feet shorter and thousands of pounds lighter. None of the full-size EV trucks come close to the MT1 on footprint or on the $41,520 starting price.
Electrek’s Take
This is impressive and exciting, but I still think it’s worth staying skeptical.
Telo has done a lot with very little. The company has raised roughly $20 million total — including a Series A
led by Tesla co-founder Marc Tarpenning
— and it’s trying to get to production readiness and pass federal requirements on that. In an industry where startups routinely burn through hundreds of millions before building a single sellable vehicle, that capital efficiency is genuinely notable. The towing physics North describes are real, too. Instant torque and heavy regen do make EVs good tow vehicles – albeit for shorter distances depending on the energy capacity.
But Telo is trying to build a Swiss army knife: a truck that’s tiny yet tows 8,000 lbs, charges at 400 kW, seats five, carries a Hummer-sized bed, and starts at $41,520. Each of those is a strong claim on its own. Stacking all of them into one production vehicle, and hitting every one consistently once real units are rolling off a line, is a much harder problem than showing it on a prototype. Tow ratings especially tend to get conservative once liability and warranty teams get involved.
And all of it still hangs on the biggest “if” of all: whether Telo actually reaches volume production. The prototype work is impressive. Deliveries are targeted for late 2026. We’ll see if the production truck can do everything the pre-production one promises.

title: Tesla admits Cybertruck PCS defect, extends warranty to 8 years
content:
Tesla has officially acknowledged that the power conversion system (PCS) in pre-2026 Cybertrucks is defective, and it’s extending the warranty on those trucks to 8 years or 150,000 miles.
The reversal comes after months of owners paying up to $7,200 to replace a part Tesla now admits “does not meet our reliability standards.” The automaker sneakily tried to let the clear manufacturing defect pass warranties.
What Tesla is finally doing
In a statement posted to its official Cybertruck account, Tesla said it “identified PCS electronics in pre-2026 Cybertrucks that do not meet our reliability standards and have made design changes to address this in newer vehicles.”
That’s the admission owners had been waiting for. It came with a list of fixes.
Pre-2026 trucks, meaning the 2024 and 2025 Foundation Series and standard builds, get their PCS coverage extended to 8 years or 150,000 miles, which basically means it’s now part of the powertrain warranty rather than the overall warranty.
The 2026 Cybertruck, which already ships with a redesigned PCS, carries a shorter 7-year/70,000-mile warranty on the part. Owners who already paid out of pocket will be reimbursed in the coming weeks. And a software update now lets the truck Supercharge even when the PCS has failed, so a dead unit no longer strands the vehicle. Tesla says it’s also covering Supercharging for affected owners until it clears the parts backlog.
The warranty math is the whole story
We reported in July that the PCS failures were starting to be widespread. A self-selected owner poll showed 91 of 223 Cybertrucks, nearly 41%, had needed a PCS replacement, with new failures logged every week. The part combines the onboard charger and the DC-DC converter, so when it dies, home charging drops from 48 amps to 24 and then quits entirely.
Here’s the problem. The 2024 and 2025 trucks shipped with Tesla’s basic 4-year/50,000-mile warranty, and the PCS wasn’t singled out for anything longer. A unit that failed outside that window left the owner with a $5,000 to $7,200 bill. Tesla had quietly been discounting the repair to around $1,000 as a “goodwill” gesture, which, as we said at the time, was the company all but admitting the part was defective.
Now it’s saying so out loud, and moving the coverage to 8 years. For a defect hitting 40% of trucks, that’s the difference between a manageable problem and a $7,000 gut punch.
Tesla has run this play before. It extended warranties on the eMMC memory failures in its older touchscreens back in 2020, but only after NHTSA opened an investigation. Other automakers do it too. Hyundai and Kia extended warranties over their ICCU failures earlier this year. And Tesla has recalled Cybertrucks before to replace faulty inverters.
Electrek’s Take
Credit where it’s due: this is the right outcome. An 8-year/150,000-mile warranty, reimbursements for owners who already paid, and a software fix so a failed PCS doesn’t kill charging entirely. That’s what taking responsibility for a manufacturing defect is supposed to look like.
Top comment by Henry
🚗 The REAL bummer here is Tesla refuses to replace my PCS at 42,000mi on Model Y LR 2020 that they KNOW is defective for $3,765!! There was a prior recall on these defective PCS parts for Model 3's and even though my car was built with one -- NHTSA did not include my model year.
Clearly the PCS is a big problem for ALL Tesla customers -- it's a question of when not if yours will fail out of warranty.🚕🚧🚧
I even filed a NHTSA complaint and nothing. The Tesla service centers in Irvine and Aliso Viejo, ca were very nasty about it and refused any goodwill assistance. So now I get to wait and see when my 12v battery starts dying since the PCS charges that too!
But it’s a bummer it took this long, and it took pressure to get here. Owners were eating $7,000 repair bills while Tesla’s first instinct was a quiet $1,000 discount instead of an admission before we reported on the issue.
It took the owner forums, our reporting, and other outlets hammering on this for weeks before Tesla put its name to the problem. Doing the right thing only after you’re pushed into it isn’t quite the same as doing the right thing.
And that’s the pattern worth watching. There’s a real tendency here to let a clear manufacturing defect run past a short warranty and make the customer eat the cost. A part that fails on 40% of trucks isn’t a fluke. It’s a defect, and Tesla knew it well before this statement. The warranty extension is welcome. The instinct to see how many owners would just pay up first is not. We’ll be watching whether the reimbursements actually land, and whether it takes a failure rate this high, or an NHTSA nudge, to get the same result next time.

content:
Peter Johnson
| Aug 7 2026 - 6:46 am PT
now accounts for over one-third of Europe’s small electric van market. Kia’s first electric van has quickly become the most popular e-LCV across Europe and the UK.
Kia PV5 EV van sales rise in Europe and the UK
After launching the PV5 at the end of 2025, Kia’s electric van proved to be a bigger hit than expected.
According to the most recent figures from the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (
), the PV5 accounted for 37% of all electric vans in the small (C-segment) market in Europe, ranking as the best-seller in 12 countries.
The PV5 was the top-selling small EV van in the UK (3,361 units) and in Germany (2,206 units). In Denmark (1,222), the Netherlands (1,196), Norway (739) and Sweden (1,414), it was the best-selling van across all engine types.
In five countries, the PV5 already accounts for over 50% of electric C-segment van sales through the first half of 2026, including: 63% in Denmark, 62% in Ireland, 59% in Sweden, 58% in Finland and 54% in the UK.
“The customer response to the introduction of the PV5 in Europe has been overwhelming,” Sjoerd Knipping, Chief Operating Officer of Kia Europe, said.
Kia PV5 Cargo (Source: Kia)
Not just in terms of sales, but also “with how the PV5 is adding new value across mobility,” Knipping explained.
In the first six months of 2026, Kia sold 13,166 PV5s. The PV5 is available in Passenger, Cargo, and Chassis variants for businesses and personal use.
In the UK, the PV5 Cargo is the best-selling electric van so far in 2026. July marked the first time Kia sold over 1,000 electric vans in a single month in the UK, including 784 PV5 Cargo and 235 PV5 Passenger models.
Kia PV5 (Source: Kia)
Kia has already sold more PV5 models this year than expected. Through July, Kia registered 3,239 PV5 Cargo and 1,141 PV5 Passenger vans. The strong demand propelled Kia into third in the UK’s electric light commercial vehicle market.
Why is the PV5 so popular? It’s much more than an average van, combining Hyundai’s advanced software with the dedicated E-GMP.S platform.
The Kia PV5 Cargo Long Range sets a new Guinness World Record (Source: Kia)
Kia’s electric van has proven its capabilities in real-world situations. The PV5 Cargo
set a new Guinness World Record
in October after driving 693.38 km (430.84 miles) on a single charge.
With a full lineup of electric vehicles, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, and EV9, plus the PV5 van, Kia now ranks as the second-most-popular EV brand in the UK year-to-date. In July, it was the best-selling EV brand with 3,731 registrations.
Kia PV5 Passenger 7-seat (Source: Kia UK)
With deliveries of new EV2 variants set to begin and the “rapid rise of the PV5,” Kia UK’s president and CEO, Paul Philpott, expects the momentum to continue for the rest of 2026.
Kia is also launching new PV5 variants, including a 7-seater (2-2-3), Prime, and a Cargo High Roof model. Next year, Kia will introduce
the larger PV7
electric van, followed by the PV9 by 2030.
With a full lineup of electric vans, Kia plans to sell 232,000 PBVs by the end of the decade.

title: 134GWh！特斯拉/鹏程无限等4企储能项目新动态
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期储能产业链项目持续推进，覆盖储能系统、电芯及钠电池等多个领域。其中，特斯拉得州储能超级工厂正式投运，鹏程无限54GWh储能电芯基地加快建设，浙江衢州10GWh钠电项目完成备案，湖北沃橙20GWh钠电储能基地启动环评，储能产业扩产布局持续推进。
特斯拉得州储能超级工厂投产
8月6日，特斯拉宣布其位于美国得克萨斯州储能超级工厂已正式投运。该工厂从破土动工到建成投产历时仅16个月，规划设计年产能达到50GWh，专门负责生产特斯拉最新一代储能产品Megapack 3。
目前，特斯拉已形成美国、中国两大储能制造基地布局。在美国，公司拥有位于加州拉斯罗普（Lathrop）和得州布鲁克郡（Brookshire）的两座储能超级工厂，其中Lathrop工厂已实现Megapack量产，年产能约40GWh；此外，特斯拉在中国上海建设的储能超级工厂也已投产。此次得州工厂投运后，将进一步提升其储能系统制造能力。
10GWh钠电项目拟落地浙江衢州
7月30日，浙江绿储能源科技有限公司年产10GWh钠离子电芯及储能电池包生产基地项目完成备案。
该项目由衢州绿芯新能源有限公司投建，总投资约40亿元，固定资产投资约36亿元。其中项目一期计划投资20亿元，固定资产投资约18亿元，建设年产5GWh钠离子电芯及储能电池包生产基地项目，拟于2026年10月开工，2028年9月建成；项目二期计划投资20亿元，固定资产投资18亿元，建设年产5GWh钠离子电芯及储能电池包生产基地项目。
湖北沃橙20GWh钠电储能基地启动环评
7月9日，十堰市张湾区20GWh钠电储能零碳制造基地及高端新型电池技术研究院建设项目正式启动环境影响报告书（表）编制工作。该项目由湖北沃橙新能源有限公司投资建设，总投资12.16亿元。
根据规划，项目将建设4条5GWh钠电地埋式储能系统生产线，并配套建设高端新型电池中试研发、试验验证等功能于一体的中试研究院及中试基地，推动钠电储能产品研发、中试与量产一体化发展。
鹏程无限54GWh储能电芯基地建设加速
近日，深圳鹏程无限新能源有限公司储能电芯制造基地建设已进入冲刺阶段，各项工作正全速推进，预计10月底全面竣工交付。
据悉，鹏程无限储能电芯制造基地总规划年产54GWh储能电芯，项目分两期建设。一期主要建设电芯前工序、后工序及容量厂房三大核心生产车间，并配套仓储设施及相关辅助用房，计划11月上旬启动试生产。
该项目于2026年2月开工，6月底完成主体建设。目前，项目正同步推进土建收尾、钢结构安装、地坪施工、围护结构建设及室外管网铺设等工作。

title: 天合光能发布2026半年报业绩
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，8月6日，天合光能发布2026年半年度报告，披露上半年营收情况及业务重点内容。
上半年，天合光能公司实现营收约319.85亿元，同比增长2.99%；归母净利润亏损2.70亿元，较上年同期实现大幅减亏，减亏幅度达90.75%；扣非净利润亏损28.90亿元。
图：天合光能2026年上半年财务数据
业绩报告显示，本期归母净利润大幅改善，主要来自处置T1 Energy部分股权及剩余股权公允价值变动带来约26.2亿元非经常性损益贡献。
分季度看，第二季度天合实现归母净利润1320.67万元，单季度归母口径实现盈利，但扣非后依旧亏损。
现金流层面成为本期报告的重要亮点，报告期内天合经营活动产生的现金流量净额78.74亿元，同比大幅增长175.14%，经营回款质量明显提升。截至报告期末，天合总资产1147.85亿元，归属于上市公司股东的净资产206.84亿元。
光伏业务方面，天合光能光伏组件上半年出货量超25GW，210组件累计出货突破260GW，公司持续深耕高价值市场，高质量订单占比稳步提升。
此外，天合储能业务表现亮眼，全球累计交付超25GWh，一季度业务同比增速超300%，储能及分布式系统业务实现正向利润，已经成为天合重要的业务增长板块。
天合还透露，技术研发层面，公司始终保持高投入，持续巩固技术储备优势。2026年上半年，天合在研发上投入21.11亿元，占营业收入比例6.60%。此外，天合上半年新增专利419件，持续推进TOPCon3.0、THBC电池以及银包铜、铜浆等金属化降本技术的研发迭代。
针对当前行业发展形势，天合光能也在财报中提示了相关的经营风险。天合表示，当前光伏行业产能过剩，产品价格持续下行，组件主业盈利修复存在不确定性；同时海外地缘环境、贸易政策变化，股权资产公允价值波动均会对公司经营业绩带来扰动。天合将依托光储协同的业务架构，持续优化产品结构，提升全球市场竞争力，积极应对行业周期挑战。

title: 15.57 亿千瓦！全国用电负荷今年第四次创新高
content:
感谢IT之家网友 I'm OK 👌 的线索投递！
IT之家 8 月 7 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，全国用电负荷再创新高，达到 15.57 亿千瓦，这也是今年第四次创新高。
7 月 29 日以来，全国用电负荷持续高位运行，日最大负荷（除周末假期外）均超过去年极值，北京、辽宁、江苏、江西等 25 个省（自治区、直辖市）用电负荷累计 78 次创新高。
据IT之家此前报道，今年 7 月 10 日，全国用电负荷今年以来首次创历史新高，最高达到 15.18 亿千瓦，较历史极值增加 1000 万千瓦。今年以来用电需求屡创历史新高主要由三方面因素共同拉动：
一是工业用电量稳步增长。高技术制造业、高端装备制造业蓬勃发展，新能源汽车、储能、算力装备等新兴产业用电持续扩容。
二是服务业用电量较快增长。今年以来充换电服务业、互联网数据服务业用电量增速均超过 40%。
三是高温天气抬高用电负荷。随着居民生活品质持续提升，全国空调降温负荷占比接近 30%，部分省份超过 40%。
官方表示，近年来，我国电力基础设施建设取得显著成效，超过 40 亿千瓦的发电装机提供了强大供电保障能力，特别是 19 亿多千瓦新能源为午高峰用电提供了有力支撑，用电负荷创历史新高时刻新能源发电出力超过 6 亿千瓦，贡献了 40% 以上的高峰出力，有力支撑午高峰电力平稳运行。

title: AI 需求挤爆云计算，消息称 AWS 要求工程师关闭闲置服务器减少资源浪费
content:
IT之家 8 月 7 日消息，据《The Information》今日报道，亚马逊 AWS 最近对工程师提出一项颇为“朴素”的要求，让他们关闭不再使用的云计算机。
据报道，亚马逊此番要求主要针对闲置的 EC2 实例。随着 AI 正以越来越快的速度消耗计算资源，全球最大的云服务供应商也开始感受到算力紧缺的压力。
数据显示，AWS 的资源利用低下问题非常严重，大约 65% 的 EC2 实例在 30 天测量周期内，平均 CPU 利用率低于 20%。
亚马逊为此升级了计算优化器（IT之家注：Compute Optimizer），自动分析 14 天内的服务器 CPU 使用率和 IO 数据，并标记峰值 CPU 利用率低于 15%、网络流量非常低的虚拟机。
同时，AWS 过去一年内新增了 3.8 吉瓦的电力容量，足以为 280 万户家庭提供电力。
亚马逊当前计算资源紧张的原因非常明确，搭载 GPU 的云计算实例是训练、运行大语言模型的核心资源。如今的 AI 热潮，已经让云计算市场竞争激烈。

title: Anthropic 为自研 AI 芯片开出高薪，模型训练岗位薪资高于实际造芯工程师
content:
8 月 7 日消息，据 Wccftech 今日报道，Anthropic 目前正在扩大内部芯片设计团队，并计划开发自研 ASIC 芯片。
与此同时，公司不同芯片相关岗位之间出现了明显的薪资差异：负责训练 AI 模型进行芯片设计的研究工程师岗位，年薪最高可达 85 万美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 574.9 万元人民币）
，而实际负责设计 Anthropic 首款 ASIC 芯片的工程师岗位，薪资范围约为 32 万至 48.5 万美元
（现汇率约合 216.4 万至 328 万元人民币）
。Wccftech 称其为“薪酬倒挂”。
Anthropic 发布的招聘信息显示，负责“Chip Design RL（芯片设计强化学习）”方向的研究工程师岗位，主要工作是构建强化学习环境，让 Claude 等 AI 模型学习芯片设计流程，包括 RTL 代码生成、验证以及物理设计优化等内容。
该岗位薪资范围为 50 万美元至 85 万美元
（现汇率约合 338.2 万元至 574.9 万元人民币）
。相比之下，负责实际芯片设计工作的 Silicon Engineer 岗位薪资范围约为 32 万美元至 48.5 万美元
（现汇率约合 216.4 万元至 328 万元人民币）
Wccftech 指出，两类岗位所需技能存在较高重合度，包括完整 ASIC / FPGA 设计流程、RTL 到流片、UVM 与形式化验证、物理设计、PPA（性能、功耗、面积）优化、DFT（可测试性设计）以及 EDA 工具使用经验等，同时都要求具备实际芯片开发经验。
目前，Anthropic 尚未公布首款自研 ASIC 芯片的具体规格、制造合作方或发布时间。公司此前表示，其芯片战略将采用多芯片路线，以满足人工智能模型训练和推理需求。
AI 企业利用人工智能辅助芯片设计并非首次出现。此前，月之暗面推出的 Kimi K3 模型曾被报道能够在较大程度自动化完成芯片设计流程。该模型利用开源 EDA 工具并自行构建 GPU 编译器，在 48 小时内完成一款模拟芯片设计方案，面积约 4mm²，采用 Nangate 45nm 工艺库，并在仿真环境中实现超过 8700 tokens/s 的解码吞吐量。
Anthropic 首次确认自研 AI 芯片：专为 Claude 定制，公司正在组建团队

title: Caviar 推出 24K 镀金版 Meta 雷朋智能眼镜 Odyssey，售价 6130 美元限量 24 副
content:
IT之家 8 月 7 日消息，奢侈定制品牌 Caviar 昨日推出了一款基于 Meta Ray-Ban 智能眼镜的限量定制版产品，命名为“Odyssey”（奥德赛）。
该系列提供 24K 金和 925 银两种装饰版本，售价分别为 6,130 美元（现汇率约合 41,460 元人民币）和 6,840 美元（现汇率约合 46,262 元人民币）。该系列限量发售 24 副（对应荷马史诗《奥德赛》的卷数）。Caviar 还提供实心贵金属定制服务。
Odyssey 系列以 Meta 与 EssilorLuxottica 合作推出的 Ray-Ban Wayfarer 智能眼镜为原型，由 Caviar 珠宝工匠手工打造。
24K 金版本在顶部镜框、镜腿末端、铰链及拍摄按键上采用黄金镀层装饰，铰链旁饰有希腊风格金银丝细工玫瑰花图案，并手工填充黑色珐琅。镜腿和鼻梁处带有浮雕雕刻。
925 银版本采用相同的黑色 Wayfarer 框架，将金色装饰替换为银质。两种版本均附带天然鳄鱼皮充电盒，盒扣饰有 Caviar 珐琅徽章。
在功能方面，Odyssey 保留了原版 Ray-Ban Meta 智能眼镜的全部特性，包括用于音乐播放、通话和语音助手的开放式音频扬声器、触控面板及拍摄按键、1200 万像素摄像头（支持拍照和录制竖屏视频）、以及 Meta AI 语音交互功能。续航、存储和无线连接规格与原版一致。
Caviar 此前以定制奢华版 iPhone 闻名，曾推出过售价高达 156,890 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 106.1 万元人民币）的 iPhone 17 Pro Max 定制版本。
此次 Odyssey 的推出正值智能眼镜市场升温之际，三星与 Google 合作、分别携手 Gentle Monster 和 Warby Parker 推出的智能眼镜产品预计将于 2026 年秋季上市。

title: EA《麦登橄榄球 27》登陆 Apple Arcade，支持苹果 iPhone、iPad、Mac 及 Apple TV
content:

《Madden NFL 27 Arcade Edition》支持玩家选择当前 NFL 球队，并带领球队完成完整赛季。游戏提供生涯经营模式（Franchise）和快速比赛（Quick Play）两种玩法，玩家可以根据游玩时间选择不同体验。

title: Linux KVM 曝出虚拟机逃逸漏洞，嵌套虚拟化功能成攻击突破口
content:
感谢IT之家网友 Coje_He 的线索投递！
IT之家 8 月 7 日消息，开发者 Hyunwoo Kim 近日在 GitHub 平台报告一起 Linux KVM 虚拟机逃逸漏洞，黑客可利用其实现 KVM 虚拟机逃逸和宿主机内核代码执行。
据悉，此漏洞被命名为 Zapscape，编号为 CVE-2026-64561。该漏洞潜伏在 KVM/x86 Shadow MMU 模拟机制的释放后重用（IT之家注：UAF）中，具体位于 Shadow Pages 执行的递归 zap 路径中。
攻击者只需要使用客户机操作就能触发该漏洞，使宿主机内核的 Shadow Page 遭到破坏。影响公有云平台，以及开启嵌套虚拟化的环境。
同时，攻击者可利用公有云的虚拟机实例，触发宿主机内核崩溃，使同一服务器上的其他虚拟机全部受到影响，并以 Root 权限在宿主机执行代码，控制宿主机及所有客户机。

title: Meta 旗下 AI 模型测试时意外入侵第三方企业系统
content:
IT之家 8 月 7 日消息，据路透社报道，Meta 公司于当地时间周三表示，公司一款 AI 模型在网络安全测试期间入侵了另一家企业的系统，引发人们对前沿 AI 模型的担忧。
IT之家从原报道了解到，本次事件发生的主要原因在于，为 Meta 提供网络安全评估服务的独立公司 Irregular 因配置错误，使 Meta 的模型在测试过程中意外获得了互联网访问权限。
据消息人士透露，本起事件的涉事模型是 Muse Spark 1.1。Meta 曾号称，该产品是现实编程、智能体任务最出色的模型之一。
Irregular 发言人对此表示，本起事故与 Anthropic 披露的 AI 模型逃逸事件类似，不涉及沙箱逃逸、高级网络攻击行为。
如今美国立法者正在担忧，越来越强大的 AI 模型是否会冲出人类设定的边界，用于实施或发动网络攻击。一批共和党总检察长已要求 OpenAI 保留 Hugging Face 入侵事件的相关文件。

title: Take-Two CEO 泽尔尼克：某些情况下，光盘对消费者已经没有太大意义了
content:
IT之家 8 月 7 日消息，Take-Two CEO 施特劳斯 · 泽尔尼克今日出席公司 2027 财年第一季度投资者电话会议，被投资者问及索尼决定 2028 年停止生产实体游戏，对公司有何影响。
泽尔尼克对此回应称：
我不会评论索尼的决定。就我们的情况而言，我司目前超过 90% 的业务都是通过数字渠道发行的，我们已经是一个数字化的企业了。
所以在某些情况下，尤其是在大型游戏中，光盘（注意，我说的是光盘）对消费者来说已经没有太大意义了。
而且大多数情况下，你无论如何都需要联网注册才能开始游玩，所以如果你已经联网了，那下载数字版又有什么关系呢？反正都一样，而且数字版方便得多。
在我看来，全数字化就是世界发展的方向，我认为索尼理解这一点。但这并不意味着我们完全放弃实体盘，我相信我们仍然会偶尔推出实体版游戏，就像音乐行业如今仍存在黑胶唱片一样。但在其他情况下，实体版本已经没有意义了。
IT之家注意到，Rockstar 官方确认，《侠盗猎车手 VI》游戏将只有数字版和附带下载码的盒装版。

title: 华为鸿蒙 HarmonyOS SDK 游戏新特性公开，含 AI 超分、控显分离、硬件光追等
content:
IT之家 8 月 7 日消息，ChinaJoy2026 已顺利落下帷幕，华为 HarmonyOS 开发者官方微博今日分享了 HarmonyOS SDK 的游戏新特性，包括 AI 超分、控显分离、硬件光追等。
据IT之家此前报道，在今年 6 月，华为手机官方宣布，HarmonyOS SDK 26 正式发布，在易用、空间化、智能化全面升级，其中就带来了游戏秒启秒开功能。
而据多名用户分享，升级了华为鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 7 开发者 / 花粉 Beta 版系统的平板 / 手机，已实装游戏秒启秒开特性，并支持《原神》《洛克王国》等游戏极速启动。
关于华为鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 7 的新特性，IT之家仍在发掘中，感兴趣的小伙伴可以关注后续报道。
- 《华为 HarmonyOS 7 花粉 Beta 版超百项更新曝光：全局沉浸空间、小艺基于 Agentic 全面进化重构等》
- 《华为鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 7 花粉 Beta 版开启报名：适配 Mate 80、Pura 90、畅享 90 系列等机型》
AI 超分技术方面，该特性依托华为移动端 NPU 软硬协同能力实现。在 HDC 2026 上展示的《异环》游戏已通过 AI 超分技术将渲染分辨率提升至 1080P，画面清晰度提升 1.5 倍，海底隧道光幕、游动鱼群等细腻场景得以完整呈现。
控显分离特性主要面向折叠屏设备，该方案将屏幕划分为两个对称的独立区域，上半屏承载核心渲染画面，下半屏集中交互触控，深度还原复古掌机的交互逻辑。该特性从 API 版本 26.0.0 开始新增，目前仅支持部分折叠屏设备，且需基于 Vulkan API 开发。
硬件光追方面，华为 Mate 80 Pro Max 风驰版已在《暗区突围》游戏中率先支持 3000 万条光线同时渲染的硬件光线追踪，并首次实现 90 帧与均衡光追同时开启，兼顾高画质与高帧率体验。
本届 ChinaJoy（7 月 31 日至 8 月 3 日）华为游戏中心以“鸿蒙游戏玩在一起”为主题，携 50+ 款热门游戏亮相上海新国际博览中心 N3 馆 01 号展位，打造 1000+ 平方米的赛博游乐场。截至目前，鸿蒙平台已上架游戏超 3 万款，合作厂商达 1000 余家，全面支持 20 余个主流游戏引擎。

title: 撤回的撤回：微信已支持删除“你撤回了一条消息”灰色小字
content:
感谢IT之家网友
I'm OK 👌
8 月 7 日消息，“微信时刻”官方公众号今日发文，宣布微信现在可以“撤回”你的撤回了。简单来说，微信用户现在可以删除消息撤回后留在聊天界面中的撤回提示词。
此前，用户在聊天中撤回消息后，聊天框内会留下一行灰色小字提示“你撤回了一条消息”，该提示无法被手动清除。
更新后，用户只需长按这行提示文字，即可选择“删除”，使自己的对话界面恢复干净。需要注意的是，该操作仅能删除自己页面中的撤回提示，对方界面中的提示字依然存在。
此次更新还引发了用户对微信撤回规则的整体回顾。目前微信撤回功能覆盖多个场景：发送文字消息后，在 2 分钟内长按消息可选择撤回，撤回后 5 分钟内点击“重新编辑”，原内容会返回输入框供修改后重发；若连续发送多条错位消息，可长按其中任意一条并选择“撤回本次发送的全部消息”，实现批量撤回。
在拍一拍场景中，用户不慎触发“拍一拍”后，可在 2 分钟内长按该条提示进行撤回，且对方界面不会显示任何撤回记录，实现无痕撤销。文件撤回方面，Word、Excel、PPT、PDF 及压缩包等文件类型在发送后 3 小时内均可撤回。
IT之家注：若用户希望发送高重要性照片，可通过聊天界面“文件”入口发送，该方式同样适用于 3 小时内撤回规则，而直接通过相册发送的照片则不在此撤回规则覆盖范围内。

title: 索尼 WH-1000XM4C 耳机曝光：XM4 衍生版本，续航时间略有下降
content:
IT之家 8 月 7 日消息，据 @billbil_kun 今日爆料，索尼正在准备推出全新的 WH-1000XM4C 无线降噪耳机，预计将作为 WH-1000XM4 的衍生版本推出。
他预测这款耳机在欧洲的售价为 249.99 欧元（现汇率约合 1,949 元人民币），预计将于 2026 年 9 月 7 日发布。不过，具体发布活动安排以及不同地区售价仍需等待索尼官方确认。
索尼 WH-1000XM4C 首发将提供三种配色，分别为铂金银（Platinum Silver）、黑色以及薰衣草。
其中，薰衣草配色与此前 WH-1000XM4 较为传统的配色风格有所不同，可能面向更加注重外观设计的用户群体。
从曝光信息来看，WH-1000XM4C 整体规格将延续 WH-1000XM4 的设计基础。该耳机预计搭载索尼 HD 降噪处理器 QN1，支持 Personal NC Optimizer 降噪优化、Adaptive Sound Control 自适应声音控制以及环境声模式。
音频方面，WH-1000XM4C 预计支持 Hi-Res Audio 高解析音频、40mm 驱动单元、DSEE Extreme 数字声音增强技术、360 Reality Audio 以及 10 频段可调均衡器。同时，该耳机预计支持 LDAC 编码和 Hi-Res Audio Wireless 无线高解析音频传输。
在功能方面，新款耳机预计支持双设备同时连接、多点连接功能，并提供清晰通话、Quick Attention 快速注意模式、Speak to Chat 聊天检测以及触控操作等功能。该产品还预计支持 Personalised Spatial Audio 个性化空间音频功能，并通过 Sony | Sound Connect 应用进行管理。
续航方面，WH-1000XM4C 预计可提供最长 34 小时续航播放时间（关闭降噪），开启主动降噪后续航约为 27 小时。作为对比，原版 WH-1000XM4 在关闭降噪情况下最长续航约 38 小时。
目前曝光信息显示，续航可能是 WH-1000XM4C 与原版 WH-1000XM4 之间较明显的差异，其他核心功能基本保持一致。不过，由于索尼尚未公布完整规格，目前无法确认该产品属于轻量版型号，还是针对旧款产品的小幅更新版本。
如果该价格最终确定，WH-1000XM4C 的定位将低于 WH-1000XM4 最初上市价格约 100 欧元。但目前 WH-1000XM4 已经退出官方产品线，而 WH-1000XM5 在部分促销活动中的价格也可能接近 190 欧元，因此 WH-1000XM4C 上市后的市场定位仍有待观察。

Wie schaffen es Schnecken, mit demselben Schleim zu kriechen, zu haften und sich zu schützen? Forschende zeigen, dass sie dessen chemische Zusammensetzung je nach Aufgabe gezielt anpassen.
Nach einem Regenschauer sind Schnecken besonders aktiv. Auch auf dem Max-Planck-Campus in Potsdam-Golm hinterlassen gewöhnliche Bänderschnecken (Cepaea nemoralis) ihre glänzenden Schleimspuren. Forschende aus der Abteilung „Biomaterialien“ erkannten im Schleim ein vielversprechendes Naturmaterial. Denn die Schnecke produziert nicht nur eine einzige Art von Schleim, sondern kann ihn je nach Bedarf so variieren, dass er flüssig, fest, klebrig oder rutschig wird.
Für das Forschungsteam wurde der Schneckenschleim damit zum Gegenstand einer materialwissenschaftlichen Analyse: Wie schafft es die Schnecke mit denselben Grundbausteinen völlig unterschiedliche Materialeigenschaften zu erzeugen? Die Antwort liefern die Forschenden in einer Studie, die nun im Fachjournal Science erschienen ist. Darin zeigen sie erstmals umfassend, mit welchen biochemischen Rezepten die Bänderschnecke ihren Schleim gezielt an unterschiedliche Aufgaben anpasst.
„Schneckenschleim mag auf den ersten Blick unscheinbar wirken, ist aber ein unglaublich vielseitiges Material,“ sagt Dr. Franziska Jehle, korrespondierende Autorin der Studie. „Dass die Schnecke mit den gleichen Grundbausteinen gezielt die Eigenschaften ihres Schleims verändern kann, macht sie für die Forschung so spannend.“
Der Baukasten des Schneckenschleims
Um zu verstehen, wie die Natur diese Materialvielfalt erzeugt, analysierten die Forschenden fünf verschiedene Schleimarten. Sie untersuchten Schleim, der die Fortbewegung ermöglicht, als starker Klebstoff an Oberflächen wirkt, das Tier vor Austrocknung schützt, das Gehäuse während längerer Ruhephasen verschließt und zur Verteidigung dient.
Dabei zeigte sich, dass die Schnecke für die verschiedenen Schleime stets die gleichen Komponenten verwendet, die sie in unterschiedlichen Mengen zusammenmischt. Bei den chemischen Bausteinen handelt es sich um Proteine, vor allem Kollagen, und Kalzium.
Überrascht hat die Forschenden, dass sie Kollagen VI als zentralen Bestandteil des Schleims identifiziert haben. Denn das Protein ist vor allem für seine strukturgebende Funktion in menschlicher Haut, Knochen und Gelenken bekannt. Gemeinsam mit ungeordnetem Kalziumkarbonat, das die Schnecke im Drüsengewebe speichert und bei Bedarf zusammen mit dem Schleim abgibt, trägt der Anteil von Kollagen VI entscheidend dazu bei, die Eigenschaften der verschiedenen Schleime zu steuern. Offenbar verändert die Schnecke über die Gesamtmenge an Proteinen und den Anteil an Kollagen VI, wie dicht das Proteinnetzwerk im Schleim ist. Das wirkt sich unmittelbar auf die mechanischen Eigenschaften aus: Je engmaschiger das Proteinnetz ist, desto zäher ist der Schleim. Kalzium dient in seiner Ionenform entweder der Vernetzung oder als Calcit der Verstärkung des Materials.
Von der Natur lernen
„Die Erkenntnisse dieser Studie reichen weit über die Biologie der Schnecke hinaus“, sagt Prof. Peter Fratzl, Co-Autor der Studie und Direktor am Max-Planck-Institut für Kolloid- und Grenzflächenforschung. „Natürliche Materialien erzielen mit wenigen Bausteinen eine enorme Vielfalt an Funktionen. Wenn wir die Prinzipien dahinter verstehen, ist das für die Entwicklung nachhaltiger Materialien von großer Bedeutung.“
So könnten sich nach dem Vorbild von Schneckenschleim beispielsweise umweltfreundliche Klebstoffe, funktionelle Beschichtungen oder Materialien für medizinische Anwendungen herstellen lassen.

IRiS sucht Forschungsideen für robuste robotische Schwärme: Gefragt sind Beiträge aus Robotik, Kommunikation, Navigation, Künstlicher Intelligenz und Mensch-Schwarm-Interaktion.

Download
Agentur für Innovation in der Cybersicherheit startet neue Forschungsinitiative
IRIS – Robuste Interaktion robotischer Systeme in heterogenen Schwärmen für den Einsatz in Krisen- und Katastrophensituationen
Am 4. August 2026 veröffentlichte die Agentur für Innovation in der Cybersicherheit GmbH (Cyberagentur) die Ausschreibung für das Forschungsprogramm IRIS. Das Forschungsprogramm zielt darauf ab, innovative Ansätze zu entwickeln, die es autonomen robotischen Systemen in heterogenen Verbünden ermöglicht, auch in sehr herausfordernden Situationen robust interagieren können. Betrachtet werden soll die Interaktion zwischen Roboter und Roboter sowie Mensch und Schwarm.
Im Zentrum von IRIS steht eine sicherheitsrelevante Frage, die angesichts aktueller technologischer und geopolitischer Entwicklungen an Dringlichkeit gewinnt: Wie können autonome robotische Systeme in Schwärmen auch dann zuverlässig zusammenwirken, wenn Kommunikationskanäle ausfallen, Lokalisierung unzuverlässig wird oder äußere Einwirkungen die Koordination erschweren? Für Einsatzlagen in Krisen- und Katastrophensituationen ist diese Fähigkeit von grundlegender Bedeutung.
Mit IRIS greift die Cyberagentur zentrale Erkenntnisse und Ideen aus dem Ideenwettbewerb HAL2025 „Autonome intelligente Systeme im Schwarm“ auf und überführt sie in ein Forschungsprogramm mit klarer Anwendungs- und Umsetzungsperspektive. Damit wird ein offener Innovationsprozess konsequent weitergeführt: „Aus konzeptionellen Ansätzen und Wettbewerbsideen soll nun anschlussfähige Forschung entstehen, die wissenschaftliche Originalität mit sicherheitsrelevanter Wirksamkeit verbindet“, betont Dr. Eva-Maria Heinke, Referatsleiterin für Unbemannte Systeme und Robotik in der Cyberagentur.
Für die Bedarfsträger liegt die strategische Relevanz des Programms auf der Hand. Heterogene robotische Verbünde können perspektivisch Aufklärung, Schutz, Transport, Unterstützung und Lagebilderzeugung in Umgebungen übernehmen, in denen Menschen nicht oder nur unter hohem Risiko eingesetzt werden können. Besonders bedeutsam wird dies dort, wo (gezielte) Störungen im elektromagnetischen Spektrum, GPS-Ausfälle oder dynamische Umgebungen klassische Systeme an ihre Grenzen bringen. IRIS adressiert deshalb die Frage, wie sich robuste, selbstorganisierende und adaptive Verbünde entwickeln lassen, die auch unter widrigen Bedingungen handlungsfähig bleiben.
Tom Weber, Programmleiter von IRIS, betont: „Wir suchen Beiträge aus Robotik, Kommunikation, Navigation, Künstlicher Intelligenz und Mensch-Schwarm-Interaktion. Wir erwarten Forschungsideen, die robuste robotische Schwärme unter realen Störbedingungen neu denken.“
Von dem Programm mit einer Laufzeit von über drei Jahren werden entscheidende Impulse für die innere und äußere Sicherheit in Deutschland erwartet. Die Ergebnisse der Forschungsarbeiten werden in Form eines Demonstrators evaluiert, um die Praxistauglichkeit der entwickelten Technologien sicherzustellen.
Die Ausschreibung richtet sich an Forschungseinrichtungen und Unternehmen, die mit innovativen Konzepten zur Weiterentwicklung robuster und autonomer Schwarmrobotik beitragen möchten. Interessierte sind eingeladen, ihre Vorschläge bis zum 6. Oktober 2026 einzureichen. Weitere Informationen finden sich auf der Website der Agentur für Innovation in der Cybersicherheit.

title: Wenn Sicherheit zum Unsicherheitsfaktor wird
content:
Wenn Sicherheit zum Unsicherheitsfaktor wird

Eine neue Studie von CISPA-Forscher Ali Mustafa und Kollegen zeigt, dass öffentlich zugängliche URL-Scanning-Dienste unbeabsichtigt sensible persönliche Informationen preisgeben können.
| Quelle:
Lea Mosbach
| Copyright:
Download
URL-Scanner-Dienste sind mittlerweile häufig Bestandteil moderner Sicherheitsabläufe. Sie helfen dabei, Phishing-Webseiten oder Malware frühzeitig zu erkennen und Nutzende vor dem Aufruf einer URL zu warnen. Allerdings kann die gängige Praxis der Dienste, gescannte URLs zu veröffentlichen, unbeabsichtigt sensible Nutzerdaten offenlegen. Die erste systematische Untersuchung der so entstehenden Risiken hat CISPA-Forscher Ali Mustafa gemeinsam mit Kollegen des Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy und der Universita Ca’ Foscari Venezia vorgenommen.
URL-Scanner-Dienste wie URLScan, VirusTotal oder Cloudflare Radar analysieren Webseiten automatisch auf verdächtige Inhalte. „Sie prüfen beispielsweise Netzwerkanfragen, die Reputation der Seiten oder eingebettete Skripte und helfen so Unternehmen und Privatpersonen, schädliche Webseiten frühzeitig zu erkennen“, erklärt Ali Mustafa. Viele Unternehmen nutzen laut dem CISPA-Forscher solche Dienste inzwischen als festen Bestandteil ihrer Sicherheitsmaßnahmen. So prüfen sie zum Beispiel automatisch Links in eingehenden E-Mails der Mitarbeitenden. Doch genau hier entsteht ein bislang zu wenig beachtetes Risiko.
Die Kehrseite des Komforts
Internetadressen bestehen heute oft nicht mehr nur aus einem Link zu einer Webseite. Sie enthalten häufig auch sogenannte Tokens. Das sind zufällig erzeugte Zeichenfolgen, die als digitaler Schlüssel dienen. Solche Links werden etwa für Passwort-Zurücksetzungen, Anmeldungen ohne Passwort oder den schnellen Zugriff auf Dokumente und Buchungsunterlagen verwendet. „Das ist für Nutzende überaus bequem. Es kann aber zum Problem werden, wenn URL-Scanner-Dienste, die Links veröffentlichen. Denn Dritte können darüber auf Dokumente oder personenbezogene Informationen zugreifen und unter Umständen sogar Aktionen im Namen der betroffenen Person ausführen“, erklärt Mustafa.
Aber warum machen die Scanning-Dienste die Links überhaupt öffentlich? „Zum einen demonstrieren die öffentlichen Scan-Feeds, wie umfangreich und schnell die Analysen der Services sind. Die Veröffentlichung ist wahrscheinlich Teil des Businessmodells. Zum anderen dienen die öffentlichen Feeds dazu, Erkenntnisse über verdächtige URLs mit anderen zu teilen“, so Mustafa weiter.
Das Problem erstmals im großen Maßstab betrachtet
Einzelne Berichte über veröffentlichte Zugangslinks mit sensiblen Informationen tauchten in der Vergangenheit hin und wieder in Blogbeiträgen oder Fallberichten aus der IT-Sicherheitsbranche auf. Die Forschenden wollten jedoch wissen, wie verbreitet das Problem tatsächlich ist. Dafür entwickelten sie das Analysesystem LEAKYLINKS. Damit konnten sie Internetadressen aus den öffentlichen Feeds von sechs großen URL-Scanner-Diensten sammeln, irrelevante Einträge herausfiltern und mithilfe eines Large Language Models automatisch analysieren, ob die verbleibenden Links sensible personenbezogene Informationen zugänglich machen könnten.
Insgesamt sammelte und analysierte das Team automatisiert mehr als zwei Millionen URLs von sechs verschiedenen URL-Scanner-Diensten und identifizierte mit 97 Prozent Präzision über 4.000 Fälle, in denen öffentlich zugängliche Links den Zugriff auf sensible Informationen ermöglichten. „Darunter befanden sich unter anderem Visa-Unterlagen, Regierungsdokumente und Buchungsinformationen. Wir waren selbst überrascht, was wir da alles gefunden haben“, sagt Mustafa.
Damit die Untersuchung nicht selbst zum Datenschutzrisiko wurde, legten die Forschenden großen Wert auf ethische Standards. Sie verzichteten weitgehend darauf, die gefundenen Inhalte manuell auszuwerten. Stattdessen übernahm das auf geschützten internen Servern betriebene Sprachmodell die automatische Klassifizierung. So mussten die Forschenden nur einen kleinen Teil der Ergebnisse selbst überprüfen, und sensible Daten wurden weder an externe KI-Dienste noch an andere Dritte übermittelt.
Stießen sie auf tatsächliche Datenlecks, informierten die Forschenden die betroffenen Organisationen sowie die Betreiber der untersuchten URL-Scanner-Dienste nach den Grundsätzen der Responsible Disclosure. Welche Unternehmen betroffen waren, nennt das Paper bewusst nicht, um zusätzlichen Schaden zu vermeiden.
Wer beobachtet die veröffentlichten Links?
Die Forschenden wollte außerdem wissen, ob die veröffentlichten Links überhaupt von Dritten beobachtet werden. Dafür richteten sie sogenannte Honeypages ein. Das sind speziell präparierte Köder-Webseiten, mit denen sich Zugriffe nachvollziehen lassen. Sie ließen diese URLS durch die Scanning-Dienste laufen und auf deren Seite veröffentlichen.
Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass die öffentlichen Feeds keineswegs unbeachtet bleiben. Die Forschenden registrierten automatisierte Besucher:innen, Zugriffe auf eingebettete Inhalte und weitere Aktivitäten, die deutlich über gewöhnliches Surfverhalten hinausgingen. Trotzdem bleiben sie bei der Interpretation vorsichtig. „Wir können keine böswillige Absicht nachweisen", sagt Mustafa. Der beobachtete Datenverkehr zeigte jedoch, dass veröffentlichte Links tatsächlich von Dritten aufgerufen werden.
Wie sich das Risiko verringern lässt
Laut Mustafa gibt es verschiedene Möglichkeiten, das Risiko für Datenlecks deutlich zu verringern. „Website-Betreiber:innen könnten sensible Zugangslinks kürzer gültig machen oder zusätzliche Sicherheitsabfragen verlangen. URL-Scanner-Dienste sollten Links mit potenziell sensiblen Inhalten standardmäßig nicht öffentlich anzeigen.“ Nach Berechnungen der Forschenden blieben selbst dann mehr als 99 Prozent aller gescannten URLs weiterhin öffentlich verfügbar. „Der Nutzen der Dienste würde also kaum eingeschränkt, das Risiko für Betroffene jedoch deutlich sinken“, sagt Mustafa.
Für ihn zeigt die Studie vor allem eines: Sicherheitsrisiken entstehen oft nicht durch einzelne Fehler, sondern durch das Zusammenspiel verschiedener Systeme. Gerade deshalb müsse bei der Entwicklung digitaler Sicherheitsinfrastrukturen stärker berücksichtigt werden, welche unbeabsichtigten Folgen deren Zusammenspiel haben kann.
