title: AWS Tells Engineers to Cut CPU Waste Amid Crunch
content: Amazon Web Services leaders met with engineers in May and delivered a sobering message: To ensure AWS has enough capacity for all its customers at its popular EC2 cloud server business in the future, engineers should save capacity however they can, according to a person with knowledge of the meeting. That includes capacity on servers that run on central processing units, as well as those running on AI chips, which have long been in short supply, the person said. CPUs are the chips that have powered the last several decades of the internet age. Since then, some engineers within AWS have found it takes much longer to get capacity on CPU servers for their work. One said it now takes a few days to get capacity for servers they used to get in a few hours, which could make it harder to meet deadlines on projects. The engineer said they’ve never experienced such long wait times during their several years of working at AWS. AWS has given teams deadlines set for later this year to reduce the amount of compute used, according to someone with knowledge of the plans. Engineers are decommissioning idle EC2 virtual servers—known as instances—that they started using for software development but now no longer need, allowing them to reallocate this capacity to customers, the person said. The compute crunch that has bedeviled the tech sector this year is increasingly expanding to older technologies. It’s no secret that skyrocketing demand for AI chips, such as Nvidia’s graphics processing units, has contributed to a shortage of AI capacity. But many companies are finding that even CPU-powered servers are in short supply, thanks to AI’s rising demand for CPUs. A lack of the memory chips that work with CPUs and of physical data center space are also contributing to the capacity crunch. A big factor is that companies are using more CPUs as more employees are building software with agents, said Jing Xie, co-founder and managing director at Elendil Labs, a firm that helps financial services firms use AI. Xie said he’s seen clients’ IT spend per employee double because they’re doing more work using AI agents, which can require paying for more cloud compute and typically creates a need for CPUs. Even in AI development, CPUs play a big role: For example, when AI firms prepare data for use in training models, CPUs read the raw data from documents, images and videos. “Basically, a lot of what’s getting built and produced and run is requiring more CPUs than in the past,” Xie said. The ratio of CPUs to GPUs used in AI inference—the running of models—was one to four in April, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said in the company’s earnings call that month. In July, Intel’s finance chief, David Zinsner, said that ratio was approaching parity. AMD and Arm executives have made similar comments. AWS disputes that anything has changed in how it runs, noting in a statement that even with “heavy demand, we continue to satisfy the overwhelming majority of compute needs for both our internal and external customers. We work closely with internal teams to meet their compute needs while ensuring they use EC2 resources as efficiently as possible…just as we’ve always done.” Amazon says its engineers can operate more efficiently using the same guidance AWS gives its customers: for instance, turning off idle instances or switching to a type of instance more appropriate for a particular customer’s workload. If a customer is not using all of the capacity in a particular instance, they can switch to a smaller one. AWS recommends that when a customer is using less than 40% of an EC2 server’s CPU and memory chip capacity over a four-week period, they should switch to a smaller machine. AWS offers software enabling customers to run automated scans checking for underutilized servers. Amazon says its guidance to employees has not changed in light of the ongoing memory crunch. Balancing internal capacity needs with those of customers has become a challenge for many big tech companies in the past couple of years. Last year, Google created a council of senior executives to decide how to allocate computing capacity between Google Cloud, its DeepMind AI research unit and its consumer businesses. Even so, tensions have arisen. Google’s star AI researcher, Noam Shazeer, left the lab earlier this summer over frustrations with his access to compute, The Information reported . When companies can manage compute effectively, they can more quickly turn capacity into revenue. Microsoft Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood on the company’s most recent earnings call last month attributed some of the growth of its Azure cloud service to “efficiency gains” it made in managing its CPU and GPU fleets. “We saw…good work this quarter in particular from our engineering teams to make as much of that available as we could,” Hood said. “And because of the supply-demand imbalance we’ve been talking about, when we can make efficiency gains, they are quickly monetized.” A consultant who helps companies use AWS said he hasn’t seen operational shortages for the CPU computing capacity customers commit to via contracts. However, access to AWS spot instances—the overflow server capacity it sells at a deep discount but can reclaim with two minutes’ notice—has become more difficult to obtain in large quantities in recent months, the person said.

title: Amid the EV Wreckage, Harbinger Motors Says Unsexy Van Chassis Pay Off
content: Amid the electric vehicle frenzy at the beginning of the decade, U.S. and European carmakers rushed into EV development programs costing tens of billions of dollars each, while EV startups raised additional billions from investors expecting a bonanza in returns. Meanwhile, Harbinger Motors, a startup in Garden Grove, Calif., said it would make something more prosaic—chassis for electric delivery trucks. Today, major carmakers have written off large swaths of those programs and canceled many of their planned EVs, and multiple startups have gone out of business. Harbinger, however, is pumping out its chassis and last week announced an 18-month contract with the Army to develop, alongside military vehicle supplier American Rheinmetall, prototype autonomous vehicles to transport supplies to troops in combat. Harbinger is one of the few U.S. EV startups to emerge from the wreckage of the EV mania in reasonable shape. It is preparing to go public in an initial public offering by early next year, according to Axios. The company declined to comment. In November, it raised a $160 million Series C round, bringing its total venture funding to $354 million since 2022. But Harbinger’s latest move—its contract with the Pentagon—reflects a broad industry shift to defense tech as Western carmakers and next-generation battery developers worry about competing with China. Flying taxi startups, too, have developed combat zone versions of their aircraft in anticipation of Pentagon orders for such vehicles. In June, the Army awarded General Motors and Ford contracts to produce prototypes of a six-seat vehicle that would ferry soldiers to combat zones, carrying enough batteries to charge an array of arms including drones and directed energy weapons. Both carmakers plan to submit modified versions of their existing commercial pickup trucks. The Army ultimately would order 600 of the winning design. The industry is making other moves to counter China: In an announcement Thursday, Ford released the name and price of an electric midsize pickup that it intends to launch next year specifically to challenge Chinese vehicles. It called the vehicle Fathom, and said the base model would start at $28,350. Harbinger CEO John Harris said its Army contract could evolve into a large deal involving multiple combat vehicles. And he said it involves exactly the same chassis Harbinger uses in its commercial vehicles, so it has no added development costs. “That’s a whole collection of different vehicles that we can be a part of,” Harris told me. Harris said Harbinger’s unusual decision to go for commercial chassis rather than a complete EV has paid off. He said that in the early 2020s, most automakers made fundamental errors when they leapt into EVs that led to their difficulties with the vehicles today. The automakers as a group relied too heavily on federal tax credits and other subsidies, rather than building vehicles that could stand on their own without government support, and they didn’t spend enough time thinking through what they were producing, he said. “They decided that they didn’t have to build the right product, that they could just build what they wanted to build and count on trade controls and frameworks and make people buy them,” Harris said. Harbinger, conversely, decided to manufacture the core technology underlying unsexy commercial vehicles—everything they need to actually run—but let customers add on their own body using other suppliers. These medium-size commercial vehicles usually travel predictable routes averaging 60 to 80 miles a day, well within the range of an EV battery. There is typically no status in such vehicles—few delivery van customers are attempting to show off their style. Customers care about quality and price, expecting the truck overall to last up to 20 years. The chassis, unlike most EVs in the West, are “actually scalable, can actually be done profitably,” he said. “It’s the inherent difference in what we do versus what most people in the segment have done.” Harbinger manufactured a little over 500 chassis last year at its California factory and is aiming to double production this year, Harris said. This does not mean electric commercial vehicles are a slam dunk. Since 2022, at least seven electric van and truck startups have closed: truck makers Mullen Automotive, Lordstown Motors, Canoo and Nikola; delivery van developer Electric Last Mile Solutions; and bus maker Proterra. Price is key. To cut down his costs, Harris vertically integrated the company, designing and manufacturing Harbinger transmissions, electric drive units and battery packs—virtually everything apart from the lithium-ion battery cells, which it buys from Panasonic, as well as tires and copper wire. “It’s always been about making this foundational element and not the complete product,” Harris said. “Because we see that that’s where the most interesting part of the value is.”

title: Canva Hits AI Speedbump on Costs, ChatGPT Competition
content: Executives at Canva, the design software app with more than 200 million users, had high hopes for a rollout of AI tools that marked the biggest product launch in the startup’s 13-year history. Instead, the privately held company has dealt with a series of stumbles related to AI. First, the unexpected popularity of new AI features drove up the company’s costs and forced it to slow its introduction of those features to more users. The company slashed its revenue growth forecast for the year to 20%, executives told investors this week. Another previously unreported issue caught the eye of executives. The company noticed that more of its users in recent months had turned to ChatGPT instead of Canva after OpenAI rolled out a new image model in April that was better at creating useful designs for things like posters, according to a person with knowledge of the situation. User growth was already under pressure from other factors. The company typically hits a slump as students take a break from using the design tool for classwork. A jump in student users over the last year exacerbated the slowdown, according to the person and a second. The episode highlights the evolving challenges presented by AI for older software companies. They are rapidly trying to roll out AI tools to gird against rival products, including those created by the makers of AI models that underpin their tools. At the same time, these software companies are also trying to wean themselves off expensive models used to run those products. These high high costs threaten business models like Canva’s, which has reached a $42 billion valuation by cheaply serving hundreds of millions of people who use the software for free, and converting a subset to paid customers. A Canva spokesperson noted that “tens of millions of images are now brought into Canva each month to edit, collaborate, share and publish,” and that a Canva feature integrated with Google’s Gemini and ChatGPT called Magic Layers had been used more than 118 million times since it launched less than six months ago. “This reflects the enormous opportunity we’re seeing to help people take an idea from first prompt to finished product, all in one place,” the spokesperson said. Hitting the AI ‘Reality Curve’ As recently as April, Canva executives were beaming with optimism about AI at their annual conference. The biggest product launch in its history would allow users to automate their design process, such as letting Canva’s AI decide which font looked best on an ad campaign, executives said. But soon after, Canva realized that it had underestimated how much users were going to use AI in its seat-based subscription accounts, which quickly racked up AI costs for the startup, the person with knowledge of the situation said. (Canva users received a certain amount of AI uses for free and a larger number as part of paid subscriptions.) In response, Canva focused efforts behind trying to lower its AI costs by moving AI usage to smaller models from OpenAI and Anthropic, as well as open-source models, the person said. It has also been developing in-house models, and also is now pushing users towards usage-based pricing instead, the person said. That’s a path that other companies providing AI-powered products, including Anthropic , Atlassian and HubSpot , have followed. Cliff Obrecht, Canva’s co-founder, acknowledged the challenge in an interview: “We have such prolific free usage, and before AI the cost of serving that usage was very low. With AI, those costs became much higher. The unit economics changed, which made it far more important for us to bring those AI costs down.” He added: “I don’t know where we are on the peak optimism curve on AI, but I very much feel we’re now moving to the reality curve where these businesses are needing to prove they are either profitable or have a path to profitability.” The Sydney, Australia-based company told investors this week that second quarter revenue rose 25% from the year-ago quarter, to $922 million. And the company predicted full-year growth would slow to 20% “to get the economics right” of launching its AI tools. That would put revenue at roughly $3.6 billion for the year, a person familiar with the figure said. The projected slowdown is steeper than those expected at similar software companies that are publicly traded, like Figma and Atlassian. Unlike those companies, Canva has stayed private—one of a number of high-profile tech firms that have sidestepped initial public offerings, including similarly aged Databricks and Stripe. Canva has taken advantage of a multiyear run of profitability to pour more than $1 billion into developing its own AI models, hiring researchers and buying startups. It said it still generated $99 million of free cash flow in the second quarter and had nearly $1.5 billion of cash on its balance sheet. But, by some measures, investor interest is waning ahead of a potential IPO. Caplight, which tracks the secondary market for startup shares, has seen a declining number of offers for Canva stock for months. And four existing investors said they were surprised by the company’s revenue forecast. One called the revenue growth “mediocre.” Another called it “a pretty significant deceleration.” The Australian Financial Review earlier reported some details of the company’s slowdown. The company is still conveying confidence about a near-term turnaround. Canva expects “reaccelerating growth” in 2027, CEO Melanie Perkins wrote in the letter. She called it an “important turning point for Canva.” The key will be rolling out AI that runs on its own in-house models more widely. The company told investors it had “reduced the cost per task by nearly 90%” since April, in part by “intelligently routing tasks between our proprietary and frontier models.” The company’s AI capabilities draw on its own library of hundreds of millions of design templates and assets, it said. Obrecht said Canva wouldn’t have to rely as heavily on frontier models to help Canva users make presentations or create images much longer. “You can see the model layer commoditizing,” he said, referencing price decreases for OpenAI’s Luna model and new launches for open-source models from DeepSeek and Moonshot. Obrecht said the company had “built the foundations of being an AI native company ourselves. That took us a little longer than we wanted.”

title: Figma, Canva Showing Growing Pains of AI Pivot
content: Welcome back! Software companies have been at pains to flaunt the success of their AI products, as they seek to dispel investor fears that AI apps are threatening their existence. Two reports this week show that developing popular AI products is only half the challenge. Canva, the design software company popular among students and business owners, warned investors this week that its annual revenue growth would slow to 20%. The reason: it was tapping the brakes on a planned AI rollout expected to drive paying subscriptions—after demand had proved higher and more expensive to serve than anticipated. Then on Thursday, Figma said it expects a slowdown in revenue growth for the September quarter, to 36% from 48% in June. In its case, the publicly traded design software company suggested it’s still figuring out how to generate sales from new AI tools that are still in beta, or testing phases, or early in their release. Both companies are cognizant that any success they have with AI comes at a potentially high cost. Canva COO Cliff Obrecht told my colleagues that before AI, the cost of serving its many free users was “very low.” With AI, “those costs became much higher. The unit economics changed, which made it far more important for us to bring those AI costs down,” he said. Figma, which largely sells subscriptions to corporate clients, says the costs are likely to hit its gross margins. “We do not charge our customers for their usage of products that are currently in beta, and we bear the cost of inference without offsetting consumption revenue,” said CFO Praveer Melwani in a call with investors. One solution for both is to lower costs with models they train themselves. Canva is heavily pushing its own in-house AI model it says is much cheaper and faster at creating images and videos than top models from AI labs. But these weren’t ready in time for the rollout of its AI features. Figma executives said the company is also investing more in its in-house AI models. It’s started to ramp up use of these alongside frontier models to run its new Figma AI agent. But training a model also takes time and money—and investors are an impatient lot. Figma shares fell about 15% Thursday after the release. Only a Sliver of Forward Deployed Engineers Are Delivering AI Returns, Study Finds Only a fraction of the roughly 17,000 tech consultants working in the U.S. with the title of forward deployed engineers are helping businesses or government agencies see returns from AI agents, according to a new study from executive recruiting firm Christian & Timbers. The job of forward deployed engineer—a hybrid role that’s part-software engineer, part business consultant— has been all the rage in 2026 . Pioneered by Palantir, this year companies including Meta, Google, Amazon, Salesforce, and new ventures started by the likes of Anthropic and OpenAI have ramped up efforts to hire people for FDE roles aimed at helping businesses use their AI products. But Christian & Timbers found that, so far, only about 12% of FDEs have helped several enterprises deliver 10 million or more in cost savings or revenue, by building custom AI agents. Christian & Timbers interviewed more than 250 C-suite hiring executives and 300 forward deployed engineers across 180 companies, the majority of which were large enterprises, and compiled data from LinkedIn and Indeed. It’s another data point suggesting that enterprises are still in the early stages of figuring out how to get returns from  their spending on in artificial intelligence. Whether or not they succeed could help determine whether enterprises spend big sums on AI firms that themselves need to see a big return on their own investments in the tech. Christian & Timbers CEO Jeff Christian said that which companies hire the best FDEs will help determine how successful their AI products are: “All that matters is how you get them to work and automate stuff….it’s the deployment now that matters.” The overwhelming majority of the so-called group of “elite” FDEs, or about 80%, are employed by Palantir. The others work for Anthropic, OpenAI’s DeployCo, Google, Amazon, and Microsoft, Christian told me. Typically those high-level FDEs specialize in working in one particular sector, such as semiconductors or financial services. Of the other FDEs, most are early career engineers making between $175,000 and $300,000 in compensation. Palantir CEO Alexander Karp has been salty about the industry copying its forward deployed engineering model. In late July, Karp said at a customer event: “For those of you who are too young to remember, the concept of FDE was derided by everyone in Silicon Valley…derided by every company that’s now copying it.” Demand for FDEs has surged, Christian & Timbers found. While only 10% of the companies it studied had planned to hire FDEs at the start of the year, approximately 70% had hired or planned to hire FDEs by the end of the June quarter. title: Missile Interceptor Startup Furientis Attracts Blue-Chip Investors
content: Over the last year, we’ve seen more generalist venture capital firms make forays into defense tech, a niche once relegated to specialized investors comfortable with revenue based on uneven government contracts and who weren’t restricted from investing in weapons makers by their limited partners. Furientis, a startup founded last year that builds missiles for intercepting attacks, is close to raising $25 million in a funding round that would value it more than $125 million including the money invested, two people familiar with the investment tell us. And we’re hearing Benchmark, known for backing Uber and Snap in their early days, has been in talks to lead, the people said. Furientis would stand out as a Benchmark investment. So far this year, the venture firm has led investments in AI agent startup Gumloop and sales platform Monaco, the type of asset-light software investments that have been the firm’s bread and butter over decades. That said, it also led a $170 million round for the space data center company Starcloud earlier this year. And it bought $250 million in shares in late 2025 and early 2026 in Cerebras, the AI chips designer that went public earlier this year. Benchmark and Furientis declined to comment. Details of the round could change. If it goes ahead with the investment, Benchmark would be joining an increasingly crowded field of VC firms backing defense tech. The commercial success of SpaceX and Anduril, and a defense-tech friendly Trump administration, have attracted more investors to these startups. Ribbit Capital, the Micky Malka-founded firm that once hewed to a fintech focus, recently co-led a $300 million round for another missile startup, Mach Industries. Kleiner Perkins, known for investments in Amazon and Google, earlier this year backed autonomous ship builder Saronic Technologies, leading its Series D at a $9.25 billion post-money valuation. And OpenAI investor Thrive Capital has backed multiple rounds in Palmer Luckey’s Anduril Industries, recently co-leading its Series H funding round at a $61 billion post-money valuation. Some traditional venture capital firms have in the past shied away from defense tech not only because of the high costs of building and running hardware businesses, but also because selling to one buyer (the government) doesn’t scale in the way traditional VC businesses have. But the war with Iran has depleted American missile supplies, making novel solutions all the more appealing to the U.S. government. The Pentagon recently allocated $53 billion to missile and rocket production and is also attempting to simplify the procurement process, which might accommodate startups selling into the government. The El Segundo, Calif., Furientis aims to solve the supply crunch by making missile interceptors en masse and for a lot less than legacy defence contractors. Co-founder and CEO Brody Franzen, who previously worked at Virgin Galactic and the missile startup Castelion , told Fortune earlier this year that Furientis is using commercial off-the-shelf components and automotive-style assembly processes to keep costs to $250,000 per missile, compared to the $1 million to $5 million cost of its legacy competitors. Silent Ventures, a solo GP firm led by defense tech investor Jackson Moses, led Furientis’s $5 million pre-seed round in May. Bessemer Ventures, Multiball Capital and SV Angel also invested. title: Nvidia Weighs Radical Idea: Less Rubin Ultra Chip Memory
content: Nvidia is weighing a radical step to deal with a shortage of advanced high-bandwidth memory chips: using less of it than planned in its next-generation graphics processing unit, the Rubin Ultra. Over the past few weeks, Nvidia has been testing at least three versions of the Rubin Ultra GPU, some of which have less memory than what the company initially announced, according to three people with direct knowledge of the trial. Nvidia is considering the lower-memory versions partly because it may not be able to secure enough advanced memory to supply its original design, according to the three people. Having less memory could affect the chip’s performance, although Nvidia could compensate in other ways. But an AI firm using the reduced-memory chip to run a large AI model may have to use more chips than it would have otherwise. Nvidia’s possible move reflects how the AI boom has taxed the chip industry’s ability to produce enough supply to meet soaring demand from data centers. That has created an intense shortage of memory chips, a component of GPUs, which has driven up prices. Higher costs have created ripple effects throughout the tech industry, forcing companies to spend more than planned and also causing companies like Apple to raise retail prices for hardware. Nvidia didn’t have a comment. What is extraordinary about this situation is that the shortage of memory chips is in some ways due to the popularity in recent years of Nvidia’s GPUs, which use memory. And now Nvidia is itself having to look at alternative memory configurations. The current three Rubin Ultra testing samples would represent something of a downgrade in memory from what is in Nvidia’s Rubin chip, which is in mass production now and rolling out to customers. The impact of a memory reduction may not significantly hurt customer demand for the Rubin Ultra, according to two Nvidia customers. Because a chip with less memory would likely cost less than the original design, one customer said the change could even benefit companies seeking to cut spending by giving them a cheaper option. Another said that while large amounts of memory are important for running the biggest frontier AI models, their company is not worried about the memory specifications of any single chip. Instead, it’s focusing on maintaining a longer-term partnership with Nvidia over several generations of hardware. Nvidia may also be able to offset some of the impact of less memory through its broader server design. Faster networking and more efficient ways to store data could allow customers to spread models and workloads across more Rubin Ultra chips. The testing of downgraded memory appears to contrast with Nvidia’s public confidence that it had secured sufficient memory supply. In mid-July, Nvidia’s senior vice president of hardware engineering, Andrew Bell, told a group of reporters that Nvidia has a team that attempts to predict and fix supply chain issues years out. “We were in front of the memory problem, so it’s not gonna hold us back anytime soon,” Bell said. “The pricing, of course, is a problem for the whole world, and probably the pricing will be the bigger challenge. But for supply, we’re in shape.” There’s Still Time To be sure, Nvidia hasn’t finalized all the specifications for the Rubin Ultra, according to the three people and one Nvidia customer. Nvidia doesn’t plan to ship the chip until late next year, which means it still has time to adjust the design based on memory availability, costs and customer demand. SemiAnalysis first reported the possible memory chip downgrade in a note to its clients last week. Nvidia hasn’t decided on the Rubin Ultra’s selling price. High-bandwidth memory can account for more than half of an advanced AI chip’s component cost, according to Epoch AI, and versions with less memory could be significantly cheaper while remaining suitable for many AI applications. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang first unveiled the Rubin Ultra at Nvidia’s annual developer conference in 2025. He said each GPU would contain 1 terabyte of HBM4E–the most advanced version of the high-bandwidth memory used in AI chips, designed to move more data, hold more memory and use power more efficiently than the last version, HBM4. That memory would be spread across 16 memory stacks, according to a slide displayed at the conference. The versions Nvidia has been testing have fewer stacked layers of memory chips and less memory per die, and in some cases they use HBM4, the older version. Some versions tested have as little as 192GB of total memory, while others have 256GB, compared to the initial 1TB, according to the three people and one Nvidia customer. Nvidia says its Vera Rubin chip comes with up to 288GB of HBM4. By reducing the amount of memory in each GPU, Nvidia could spread what memory it does have across a greater number of GPUs, maintaining its production volume more easily, according to the people. Manufacturing Challenges One of the reasons Nvidia is weighing a memory downgrade is that memory suppliers may struggle to produce enough HBM4E to meet Rubin Ultra’s planned schedule, the people said. The greater capabilities of HBM4E require denser memory chips and faster electrical connections. Packaging the HBM4E when the components of a chip are assembled is also harder. Nvidia has taken steps to address possible memory supply constraints, including striking a $500 billion partnership with the parent company of memory-making giant SK Hynix late last month. That partnership will aim to co-develop new memory technologies including HBM4 and HBM4E in multiple configurations. That partnership was designed to “help us secure a stable supply of high-bandwidth memory,” said Raj Mirpuri, Nvidia’s vice president of global AI clouds and infrastructure, in a July briefing with reporters. He added that SK Hynix would be making an investment to increase its production capacity for the HBM that would be made available to Nvidia. That’s after SK Hynix already said in June it plans to double its memory chip capacity over the next five years.

title: Ocean-Powered Data Center Startup Set to Double Valuation to $2 Billion
content: AI data centers need boatloads of power, a need that’s set off a flood of investment into startups harnessing nuclear or solar energy to run the servers. Now one startup is raising money to power AI from a different source: the ocean. Panthalassa, a 10-year old startup making technology that aims to generate electricity from the movement of waves and use it to run graphics processing units, is raising $225 million at a nearly $2 billion valuation after the investment, according to two people with direct knowledge of the deal. The fundraise will double Panthalassa’s valuation from just three months ago, when it raised $140 million at a roughly $1 billion valuation after the investment. Venture capital firm 8090 Industries and South Korean investment firm Hanwha Asset Management, which invested in the startup’s last fundraise in May, are co-leading the new funding round, the people said. Additional investors may co-lead the round alongside the two firms, a third person said. Panthalassa, named after the ocean that encircled the supercontinent Pangea hundreds of millions of years ago, is building large, buoy-like structures that float in the ocean, capture energy from waves and convert it into electricity. As the vessel, shaped like a lollipop, bobs in ocean swells, pressurized water rushes through a tube and up into an internal turbine, which spins and generates power. The company hopes to use this electricity to run data centers in the ocean. The system would work like this: The electricity powers an on-board GPU cluster, which sits in the submerged part of the structure. Cool ocean temperatures keep the GPUs from overheating at no cost. The data center then beams AI results generated by the GPUs to satellites and sends them back to land. In running data centers offshore, Panthalassa may be able to skirt some of the rules and local pushback a data center on land and in the U.S. faces. State and local governments in the U.S. have passed over 300 bans on data center development since 2023, with dozens more under consideration, The Information reported in June. While the idea of underwater data centers may seem somewhat outlandish, tech companies have wondered about the concept for years. In 2018, Microsoft conducted a test called Project Natick that involved submerging a small data center in the waters off Scotland’s Orkney Islands. More recently, a Chinese company began operating a 24-megawatt data center in the waters off Shanghai, which will be powered by an offshore wind farm. Panthalassa’s ambitions have attracted a slew of high-profile backers. Kleiner Perkins Chairperson John Doerr, Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund, Max Levchin’s SciFi Ventures and Figma CEO Dylan Field invested in the prior round. The company used the funding to help complete a manufacturing facility near Portland, Ore. The startup is yet another company pitching itself as a new source of clean, reliable energy to AI companies and data centers. Valar Atomics, which is making small nuclear reactors, on Monday announced its $1 billion funding round led by Sequoia Capital at a $6 billion valuation after the investment. In June, the nuclear fusion startup Helion Energy tripled its valuation to $15.5 billion , raising $465 million led by Josh Kushner’s Thrive Capital. Other startups also hope to develop data centers in far-flung places: Starcloud, which makes space-based data centers that run on solar energy, told investors it was in talks to raise funding at a valuation of about $2.2 billion, The Information reported in April. SpaceX and Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin have plans for similar efforts. Garth Sheldon-Coulson, Panthalassa’s CEO, co-founded the company with Brian Moffat, the chief innovation officer. It is structured as a public benefit corporation, a designation used by Anthropic and others that allows companies to put social responsibility mandates into their articles of incorporation. Sheldon-Coulson previously worked as an investment associate at asset management firm Bridgewater and as a research fellow at Stanford University. Moffat was previously a senior engineer at Dollar Shave Club and researched methods for capturing ocean wave energy at other companies.

title: SoftBank’s OpenAI-Backed Loan Highlights Risks in Financing Strategy
content: If you’re one of those executives at Alphabet, Meta Platforms or Amazon who deals with investors, here’s an idea: Put a large photo of SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son on the wall of your office. Next time a visiting investor complains about your AI spending, point to the photo. That should end the discussion. As much as big tech firms are spending on AI, at least they’re financing much, if not most, of it through internally generated cash. SoftBank in contrast has so far spent $54.6 billion on OpenAI shares by raising money through a combination of various kinds of loans and asset sales. And it’s now gone even further: On Thursday, SoftBank revealed that this week it had borrowed $10 billion using its OpenAI stake as collateral. As SoftBank has committed to put a further $10 billion into OpenAI in October, there’s a good chance it will make that payment using money borrowed against other OpenAI shares. The risk of borrowing against its OpenAI stake is obvious. SoftBank’s disclosures say that under this new financing, finalized on Wednesday, it would have to cough up cash if the “fair value” of its OpenAI shares drops significantly. You can imagine a scenario whereby a slowdown in OpenAI’s business causes its valuation to drop, forcing SoftBank to sell some of its shares to meet the banks’ request for cash, thereby putting even more pressure on OpenAI’s valuation. To be sure, that’s probably not going to happen. SoftBank could raise cash in other ways if it had to. Moreover, the chances of OpenAI shares falling enough to trigger a request for cash are likely small. After all, SoftBank estimates that as of June 30, its stake in OpenAI had gained $45 billion in value. That gives it plenty of headroom if anything were to go wrong. Even so, there are certainly precedents for tech stocks to drop as sharply as they once rose. Son has a seemingly limitless appetite for risk, but even he may be stretching things a bit. California’s Time Machine So this is what California and several other Democrat-led states want to preserve? Warner Bros. Discovery, the company they want to keep out of the clutches of Paramount Skydance, on Thursday reported an 11% drop in revenues and lower profits for the second quarter. WBD’s report showed its streaming business is growing, but not enough to offset declines in its cable channel and film studio business. One of the big reasons for the revenue decline was that its cable channels lost the rights to broadcast NBA games, thanks to rising costs. In other words, WBD doesn’t have the scale to compete with bigger firms, including Netflix and Amazon Prime Video—something a combination with Paramount might fix. The states, however, want to preserve the status quo. In their lawsuit, they argued that allowing two of Hollywood’s five film companies and two of five cable channel owners to combine would hurt movie theaters, the cable industry and audiences. It’s as though the state attorneys general who put together the lawsuit climbed into a time machine set to 1990, when Netflix, Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV Plus didn’t exist and cable was still the main way people watched TV. The states won an injunction blocking the merger from closing pending a trial, which the court has set for March of next year. You can see where this is going. Freezing the deal for another six or nine months won’t help WBD’s competitive ability, given that its management has already spent much of the past year trying to sell the company rather than focusing on competing with its rivals. And if the deal is killed, both Paramount and WBD will be worse off. By trying to hold back the march of the time, the states may simply accelerate the decline of these Hollywood icons. title: Why U.S. Robotics Startups Are Stuffing Parts From China in Luggage
content: On a muggy morning in April, a venture capitalist from San Francisco arrived in China’s southern tech hub of Shenzhen with a long shopping list. His friends at U.S. robotic startups had asked him to bring back humanoids and various robotic components from China. He headed to Shenzhen’s Huaqiangbei district, the world’s biggest electronics bazaar. At one store, he bought humanoids, which he arranged to ship back to the U.S. He then went upstairs to component floors—a labyrinth of countless stalls barely larger than walk-in closets—to pick up robot parts that control motion, manage power and carry signals. Instead of shipping those components as freight, he packed them in a suitcase and took that with him on a flight back to San Francisco. This episode isn’t unusual. American humanoid startups say there are many components they can only buy from Chinese suppliers. To speed up their development of humanoid prototypes, U.S. startup employees have hand-carried such components from China in suitcases back to the U.S. without going through formal import processes, which are more time-consuming and costly. Under those processes, it can take several weeks to prepare the proper paperwork for imports and go through customs clearance, in addition to paying import taxes and shipping fees. China’s strength in robotics is becoming an increasingly delicate geopolitical issue. Late last month, the Trump administration banned the import of foreign-made humanoids and quadrupeds on national security grounds, due to their potential to conduct surveillance and other risks. The ban doesn’t currently apply to robot components. But it could impact U.S. robotics startups as they move from prototyping to mass production, unless they assemble their robots in the U.S. While the Trump administration’s policy didn’t officially target any single country, no nation comes close to having China’s clout in the robotics category. It controls 63% of the key companies in the global supply chain for humanoid robot components, according to German think tank Mercator Institute for China Studies. Chinese robot makers are far ahead of the U.S.—and the rest of the world—in humanoid mass production, accounting for the vast majority of global shipments. Many U.S. research labs have been buying humanoids from Chinese robot makers such as Unitree Robotics and AgiBot to work on physical AI models and other projects, because no U.S. alternatives are readily available and affordable. The race to develop intelligent humanoids is shaping up to be a critical new frontier in the intensifying technological competition between the U.S. and China. And China’s rapid advancements in robotics and dominance in the industry’s supply chain give it a big advantage. “The big difference between U.S. companies versus Chinese companies is the location of the supply chain. If you look at a Chinese company, everything is in driving distance,” said Jeff Cardenas, CEO of Austin, Texas–based humanoid developer Apptronik. “If we want to compete in the next phases of this race, we need to start to colocate that supply chain and start to build up regional manufacturing zones similar to what we see in Shenzhen. And we think of this as the American Shenzhen.” China doesn’t restrict exports of humanoids or their components, provided they are only for civilian use, such as services or industrial production. U.S. robotics startup employees and investors who schlep parts into the country in their luggage are probably not breaking laws, unless they violate airline safety rules or fail to pay import duties. U.S. residents are required to declare goods valued at more than $800 when they enter the border and pay appropriate duties. It’s unclear how often venture capitalists or startup employees declare robotic components they’re carrying in suitcases. There can also be a safety issue. Some American customers buy robots in China from Unitree and take them apart so they can carry them home on commercial flights, a Unitree sales manager in China said. As Unitree’s robots run on large lithium battery packs with capacities that exceed civil aviation limits by several times, the company advises those customers to remove the battery and buy a replacement from Unitree’s online store. But not every customer wants to do that. To get around the restrictions, the sellers sometimes print a fabricated battery label and swap it with the authentic one, according to the Unitree sales manager, who said they have done this for American customers. This practice would be illegal. Unitree didn’t respond to a request for comment. U.S. robotics startups have been using all kinds of channels to gain access to components from China. Before Palo Alto, Calif.–based humanoid startup K-Scale Labs shut down late last year, its employees transported dozens of actuators, parts that turn energy into movement, from China to the U.S. over several trips, according to two former staff. The former employees said other employees traveled to several cities in China, visited suppliers, picked up samples of new actuators and brought them back in their luggage to the U.S. Those trips allowed the company to quickly procure component samples, they said, sidestepping the formal import processes, which take weeks. K-Scale also used Taobao, the Chinese shopping site operated by Alibaba Group, to buy robotic parts such as sensors that the company couldn’t find in the U.S. When the team needed to quickly build a prototype of a robot, they ordered components on Taobao and had them delivered to one of K-Scale’s suppliers in China, according to the former employees. The Chinese supplier then put all the parts in boxes and shipped them to the U.S. K-Scale also used WeChat, the Chinese messaging and social media app, to find robotic parts vendors. Workers assemble joints and motors for the EngineAI PM01 humanoid robot at the company’s workshop in Shenzhen, China in May 2025. Photo by Qilai Shen/Getty Images Some U.S. startups, such as the Y Combinator–backed Robotics Center of Silicon Valley, have made a business out of importing robots and components from overseas so they’re available on shorter notice to customers in the U.S. Customers visit the startup’s San Francisco office to look at its hardware offerings and place orders, which ship from U.S. warehouses, including one in Mountain View, Calif. The startup can also handle the paperwork for importing batteries, which require their own U.S. certifications. U.S. startups can also turn to component brokers in China. One such broker is based in a cluttered office in Shenzhen, near the Huaqiangbei electronics bazaar, where shelves are full of sample catalogs and tiny components in small ziplock bags. The broker, who declined to be named, said more than half of his customers are from overseas organizations, mostly startups and university labs in the U.S. and Canada. The broker gathers small orders from many customers and consolidates them into bigger orders for factories. When a customer wants a component that a specific Chinese humanoid robot is using, the broker reaches out to their friends at the humanoid maker’s component suppliers. Those friends will make sure the factory that manufactures the component in question will produce a few extra units, declare them as a defective batch to be discarded and send them to the broker. Despite U.S. companies’ various efforts to work remotely with China’s supply chain, robotics startup founders who have worked in both the U.S. and China say being physically close to Chinese component suppliers makes a huge difference. Robin Han, CEO of Shanghai-based humanoid startup Sudo AI, previously ran Hillbot, a U.S. humanoid startup based in San Diego. Last year, Han and other Chinese Hillbot co-founders left Hillbot and launched Sudo in Shanghai as a separate new startup. Han said moving to China helped speed up a lot of things. “If we were still based in the U.S. today, we would be moving a lot more slowly,” he said. For example, when Sudo needs to make changes to the specification of the lenses in its robot’s camera system, its engineers can hail a cab or ride a bike to visit a camera component supplier’s office 15 minutes away. The supplier has its own lab, and Sudo engineers can browse through all the lens options and pick a new one. The supplier can deliver the new camera system in half a day. If there are any issues, Sudo’s engineers can easily go back to the supplier’s lab to fix them. By comparison, when Han was running Hillbot in California, making changes to a camera system took a few months. First the team would set up many phone calls with suppliers in China, and the suppliers would ship samples based on what they discussed on the calls. After checking those samples, Hillbot would request adjustments, which would involve more phone calls and shipping of new modified samples. Like other U.S. startups, Hillbot employees transported small components that didn’t contain batteries—such as camera systems and fingers for humanoid hands—in suitcases on commercial flights to save shipping time, according to Han. Being based in China makes it much easier to identify the best suppliers and closely collaborate with them to design custom components, Han said. “For sensors alone, you can easily find suppliers for 200 or 300 types of sensors,” he said. “If you need a completely new design for cables, you can find many vendors who can do that for you.” But when his previous U.S. startup worked remotely with a Chinese supplier to assemble a humanoid prototype using off-the-shelf components, the finished prototype that was delivered to the U.S. had limited capabilities and didn’t work with some of his software tools, according to Han. “The supply chain for humanoid robots is still in the early stage of development, and many of the suppliers of humanoid components in China don’t have offices in the U.S. This makes it harder for U.S. companies to work with those suppliers,” he said. While U.S. robotics companies continue to rely on China’s supply chain, Chinese robotics companies view the U.S. as a potentially lucrative market. But the Trump administration finds this problematic. Last month, when the Federal Communications Commission announced its ban on foreign robot imports, the White House said in a statement that data collected by foreign-made robots could enhance the capabilities of foreign intelligence services. The import ban doesn’t apply to existing products that have previously received FCC authorization. But it could have a significant impact on future products from Chinese robot makers—and their American customers who use them for their own research or product development. The ban came just as some Chinese humanoid makers were starting to build a local presence in the U.S. In January, Shanghai-based AgiBot launched a small U.S. office in Sunnyvale, Calif., with half a dozen employees. The startup’s global sales are growing fast—it shipped more than 5,100 humanoids last year, and another 5,000 in the first three months of 2026. A lot of its U.S. sales are to universities and private labs, said Peng Chen, AgiBot’s business development director and director of physical AI in the U.S. Many industry executives say blocking the imports of Chinese humanoids won’t solve the fundamental problem facing the U.S.: The lack of a U.S. supply chain for advanced robotics continues to be a glaring structural gap. The palms of humanoid robots are seen on August 5, 2026, in Shenzhen, China. Photo by Stringer/Getty Images For some components, such as drone motors, finding a U.S. supplier is nearly impossible, according to Ted Larson, CEO of OLogic, a Santa Clara, Calif.–based engineering consultancy. “There is nobody that makes a drone motor cheaply in the U.S., period.…And so you have to be OK with going to China to get them,” Larson said. It’s the same for gimbal motors, which eliminate shaking in the flight of an electric aircraft and are also used in humanoids to create smooth head and neck movements. “There is no such thing as a cheap outrunning gimbal motor that’s U.S. made. It just doesn’t exist,” he said. That will become a bigger issue as U.S. startups move beyond the prototype phase into mass production. At that point, startups will need much bigger volumes of components than component brokers or electronics bazaars can supply. “The question is, at what quantity can you get those parts? You can even get sample batches and things for hand carrying,” Cardenas, CEO of Apptronik, said. “But that’s not gonna solve the long-term scaling challenges that we’re facing.”

title: ASME BPV III中国国际工作组新主席上任
content:
8月4日，美国机械工程师学会(ASME)锅炉和压力容器规范第III卷(BPV III)中国国际工作组(以下简称“工作组”)2026年第一次工作会议暨第四届主席换届选举大会在上海核工院举行。经与会委员投票，公司副总经理矫明全票当选新一届工作组主席，中机生产力促进中心核设备安全与可靠性中心主任周舟、上海电气核电集团副总裁江才林当选工作组副主席。
矫明表示，工作组将持续打通国内行业与ASME常态化沟通渠道，立足国内重点核电工程，带领行业持续攻坚超厚锻件射线检测、相控阵超声检测、核设备增材制造等前沿技术，携手行业伙伴共促装备技术升级，双向推进标准互通转化，持续提升中国核电在国际核电标准制定领域的话语权、影响力与核心竞争力，为我国核电产业自主化、规模化、高质量发展筑牢根基。
会上，ASME国际事务部主任John Hasselmann为第三届工作组主席、公司二级咨询王勇颁发荣誉证书，高度肯定其任期内工作组的突出成果，并对上海核工业联合全行业持续推进ASME核电规范本土化应用表示赞赏。
本次大会紧扣国内外核电工程建设中规范应用前沿热点，汇聚全行业专家力量，围绕容器接管断裂韧性评价边界、焊接接头缺陷验收准则等近50项关键技术议题展开深入研讨，并达成广泛共识。
ASME BPV III中国国际工作组于2011年由国家电投集团联合ASME共同发起设立，旨在联动国内全产业链共同深耕国际核电标准领域。十余年来，工作组累计研讨500余项行业共性技术难题，向ASME国际委员会提交180余份专业技术咨询文件，为国内核电产业培养50余名精通国际规范的高端标准专家，现已成为国内核电领域权威的跨行业标准交流、技术攻关、国际对接核心平台，是我国核电参与全球标准制定的关键载体之一。

title: 华能海南昌江核电公司4号机组二回路联合水压试验顺利完成
content:
华能海南昌江核电公司4号机组二回路联合水压试验顺利完成
2026年8月6日04:29，在华能昌江核电公司与各参建单位共同旁站见证下，4号机组二回路联合水压试验完成，为该机组后续冷态功能试验全面开展筑牢关键前置基础。
二回路水压试验是机组二回路系统继爆破吹扫工序之后的核心关键性试验，属于华龙一号核电机组建设安装阶段强制性验收环节。试验主要针对蒸汽发生器二次侧系统、主蒸汽管线、给水系统、附属阀门支吊架及全部配套管路，全方位核验整体结构耐压强度、焊缝及法兰密封性能、整体安装施工质量，提前排查高压工况下渗漏、形变、承压不足等潜在隐患，是机组从设备安装转向系统调试不可或缺的核心工序。
为保障4号机组二回路水压试验安全、精准、按期落地，华能昌江核电公司组织各参建单位，结合4号机组现场施工实际进度编制实施分级管控细则、制定应急处置预案。项目团队细化升压分级步骤、优化现场施工逻辑，动态调配试压设备、检测仪表、作业人员等核心资源，严格压实安全生产与质量管控责任。试验全过程实行24小时专人值守，升压、稳压、泄压全流程多单位联合监测，严控升压速率、保压时长、压力波动等关键参数，全过程守住核电施工安全底线与质量红线。
华能昌江核电公司始终坚守“安全第一，质量第一”的核电建设基本原则，协同中核工程、中核咨询、中核五公司等参建单位凝心聚力、协同攻坚。二回路水压试验节点的顺利完成，标志着华能昌江核电公司4号机组建设进度稳步并行推进，持续完善海南自贸港清洁能源供给布局。项目全体参建人员将以本次节点为新起点，稳步推进后续系统调试、冷试、热试等关键工作，全力保障4号机组高质量按期投产，助力华能核电产业规模化高质量发展，为华能集团加快建设世界一流企业、海南省构建新型电力系统持续贡献核电力量。

title: 哈尔滨市聚变与超导产业技术创新联盟成立
content:
2026-08-07 15:57 来源：科技日报
8月7日，哈尔滨市聚变与超导产业技术创新联盟成立大会暨第一次成员大会举行。
在黑龙江省科技厅、哈尔滨市科技局指导下，哈尔滨工业大学牵头组建哈尔滨市聚变与超导产业技术创新联盟。联盟不仅全面整合哈尔滨工业大学在机器人、先进焊接与连接、特种复合材料、极端环境模拟等领域的国家级优势科研力量，吸纳了哈工程、黑龙江省原子能研究院、哈电集团等一批本土科创力量与产业主体，同时汇聚了中科院等离子体研究所、核工业西南物理研究院、中国科学技术大学、华中科技大学、西南交通大学等高校院所，以及西部超导、新奥科技、能量奇点等国内聚变和超导领域顶尖核心高校院所和企业，共66家成员单位，初步构建起覆盖基础研究、技术攻关、装备制造、工程应用的全链条协同体系。
当前，全球核聚变能源研发正处在从科学实验转向工程实现的关键阶段，已成为大国科技竞争的战略制高点。我国已将核聚变能源纳入“十五五”规划未来产业布局，行业发展迎来历史性机遇。
哈尔滨作为国家重要的老工业基地，在高端装备制造、特种材料等领域积淀深厚，在人工智能、机器人等新兴赛道加速发力，在高端人才培养方面产教融合、无缝对接，拥有哈工大、哈工程、省科学院等顶尖高校院所和国家重点实验室，以及哈电集团等一批与国家能源战略同频共振的骨干企业。哈尔滨市聚变与超导产业技术创新联盟的成立，既是落实国家培育新质生产力战略部署的关键举措，也是推动黑龙江省、哈尔滨市发展未来产业、积极融入国家能源战略布局的务实行动。
相关负责人表示，联盟将发挥平台纽带作用，围绕高温超导材料、超导磁体装备、聚变等离子体智能调控等核心领域，建立联合攻关、平台共享、标准共建机制，常态化开展学术交流、产业调研、供需对接、政策宣讲、人才培训等活动，积极对接国家可控核聚变重大战略需求，协同攻坚聚变堆关键材料、超导磁体、等离子体控制等核心技术，畅通科技成果产业化渠道，深入挖掘能源装备、高端制造、新材料等应用场景，着力打造“聚变与超导”区域创新品牌，为培育黑龙江省及哈尔滨市新的经济增长引擎提供有力支撑。

title: 国家能源局关于印发《电力安全生产“十五五”行动计划》的通知
content:
国家能源局关于印发《电力安全生产“十五五”行动计划》的通知
国家能源局关于印发《电力安全生产“十五五”行动计划》的通知
各省(自治区、直辖市)能源局，有关省(自治区、直辖市)及新疆生产建设兵团发展改革委，北京市城市管理委、天津市工业和信息化局、辽宁省工业和信息化厅、上海市经济信息化委、重庆市经济信息化委，各派出机构，全国电力安全生产委员会企业成员单位：
为贯彻落实党中央和国务院关于加强安全生产工作的决策部署，统筹发展和安全，深入践行“四个革命、一个合作”能源安全新战略，筑牢能源强国建设安全基础，持续提升电力安全生产水平，保障电力系统安全稳定运行和电力可靠供应，特制定《电力安全生产“十五五”行动计划》。现予以印发，请遵照执行。
电力安全生产“十五五”行动计划
为深入贯彻落实习近平总书记关于安全生产的重要指示批示精神，按照党中央、国务院决策部署，扎实做好“十五五”时期电力安全生产工作，推进电力安全治理体系和治理能力现代化，制定本行动计划。
以习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想为指导，深入贯彻党的二十大和二十届历次全会精神，认真落实四中全会部署，坚持人民至上、生命至上，坚持总体国家安全观，深入践行能源安全新战略，统筹发展和安全，以推进电力安全治理体系和治理能力现代化为主题，以推动治理模式向事前预防转型为主线，持续强化稳定可靠的系统运行能力、安全规范的生产作业能力、快速有力的应急管理能力、智慧赋能的科技保安能力，着力防范化解系统性重大安全风险，坚决遏制重特大事故，全面提升电力系统本质安全水平，夯实能源强国建设基础，为推进中国式现代化提供安全可靠的电力保障。
到2030年，电力安全治理体系和治理能力现代化建设取得明显进展，电力安全生产责任全面落实，电力安全风险分级管控和隐患排查治理双重预防机制有效运转，重大灾害防范和应急处置能力显著增强，电力建设施工作业风险有效管控，以科技为核心的本质安全建设全面推进，推动实现从“要我安全”向“我要安全”转变，电力安全生产形势持续稳定。
(一)夯实安全管理基础
加强政治引领作用，坚持党的全面领导，严格执行第一议题制度，持续深学细悟习近平总书记关于安全生产重要论述，以理论领航安全治理、压实全链条安全生产责任。健全主体责任体系，压紧压实企业安全责任制，推动责任下沉基层、织密责任落实网络。督促企业规范提取和使用安全生产费用，保障安全生产所需资金投入。健全监督管理体系，落实“三管三必须”要求，完善电力安全监督管理权责清单，优化省级电力安全委员会运行机制。深化“党建+安全”融合机制，将安全生产嵌入基层党建各环节，夯实一线班组安全生产工作基础。
(二)加强常规发电安全管理
加强转型背景下火电机组风险管控，健全新工况下煤电机组风险监测预警机制，加强发电厂全停隐患排查治理，强化机组本质安全与延寿管理，提升燃气轮机技术自主可控性。加强核电机组电力安全相关风险管控，提升涉核外电网线路保障水平。加强水电站风险管控，推动水电智能化监测预警系统建设，推进智能化运维，健全流域联合调度与协同管理机制。加强大坝风险管控，健全大坝安全法规标准与风险管控体系，推进大坝安全智能化监测检测技术应用。
(三)加强新业态新主体安全管理
加强新能源发电安全管理，完善海上风电、“沙戈荒”新能源基地等重点场景安全技术标准，健全新能源发电企业安全管理体系，推行安全生产标准化认证，强化全周期安全风险评估与防控。提升新能源发电二次系统专业化管理能力，加强二次专业队伍建设与能力认证。加强新型储能安全管理，完善全链条安全标准体系和安全评价机制，强化新型储能安全监管和信息共享。
(四)加强电网安全运行主动防控
提升系统运行控制能力，加快研究“双高”电力系统稳定基础理论，强化复杂电力系统仿真分析能力。推动电力系统运行方式分析计算向规划设计和实时运行两端延伸，将电网最小等效开机评估校核纳入方式分析。强化电网合理分区运行能力，构建多元黑启动电源体系。加强电网风险管控，健全事故风险防御和运行风险管控体系，强化大电网稳定破坏风险管控，推进重要输电通道沿线森林草原火灾防范，加强电网电压失稳、振荡风险监测与管控。优化“三道防线”，巩固和完善电力安全防御体系，加强电力市场环境下安全校核力度。强化配电网安全管理，健全配电网安全运行风险管控机制，有效管控县域全停风险，加强主配微协同安全调度，提升市县级调度机构安全管控能力。深化电力监控系统网络安全防护，强化关键信息基础设施安全防护，加强新业态新主体网络安全防护，打造自主可控、安全可靠的电力网信基础设施供应链。
(五)提升涉网安全管理能力
完善涉网安全管理体系，健全电力二次系统涉网安全技术监督体系，培育涉网检测和技术监督服务市场主体，规范涉网检测和运行管控，强化涉网性能动态监测。加强新能源和新型并网主体涉网管理，规范并网验收标准与运行参数管理，研究健全新能源建模、参数实测机构管理及监督评价机制。加强常规电源涉网管理，推动新工况下一次调频技术攻关，科学布局各类动态无功资源，强化最小开机管理。加强地方电网和用户侧涉网管理，规范地方电网与大电网调度安全管理，加强用户侧涉网控制保护配置及参数的技术监督。
(六)加强设备安全管理
严把设备入网关，建立设备全流程质量追溯机制，严格电力设备招标采购管理，探索建立设备质量“黑名单”和重大缺陷电力设备“召回”制度。加强设备运维检修，推行以可靠性为核心的设备状态检修，加快老旧及不达标设备更新改造。加强设备全过程技术监督，构建贯通联动的技术监督体系，强化质量问题整改与供应商处置。建立健全电力设备质量管理体系，依托电力设备质量安全风险监测平台，加强质量信息共享与风险联合监测。
(七)提升电力建设工程安全质量管理水平
强化安全质量综合监管，规范危大工程作业全流程安全管理，严格设计变更和工期管理，强化施工班组与人员安全管控、勘察设计源头管控。加强安全质量问题常态化整治，加强监理单位弱化监管问题整治，严厉打击转包、违法分包等严重违法违规行为，加大工程质量问题整治力度。探索电力建设工程安全监管新模式，推动建立电力建设产业工人智能化协同创新服务平台，开展电力建设工程标准化和安全质量“阳光工程”专项行动。深化重点工程和新业态工程安全质量保障，重点加强雅鲁藏布江下游水电、“沙戈荒”新能源基地、大型海上风电基地、特高压交直流输电等重特大工程安全质量监督和施工安全保障，强化新技术新业态安全质量保障。
(八)加强电力应急体系和能力现代化建设
完善电力应急体系，推动省级停电事件应急预案修订，完善电力应急标准，加强国家电力应急指挥中心功能建设，健全完善大安全大应急框架下电力应急指挥机制，强化京津冀、长三角、粤港澳大湾区等区域应急协同。提高事前预防能力，推动电力企业完善直达基层的预警“叫应”和快速响应机制，编制完善电力灾害综合风险图和应急防御图，因地制宜开展电力设备设施主体与防灾抗灾配套设施同步规划、立项、建设、运行。夯实防灾减灾救灾基础，完成东北、西北国家级电力应急基地建设，优化完善“7+2+N”国家电力应急力量体系，强化基层应急力量和基础。提升应急救援水平，实施“人工智能+电力应急”创新工程，强化“小、快、轻、智”新型技术装备配置，提升极端应急场景下的处置和保障能力，加强专业技能教育培训。
(九)加快培育发展电力安全新质生产力
加强“人工智能+”安全治理，创新设备高精度故障预测及健康管理方法，推动人工智能技术嵌入智能安全工器具，研究基于人工智能大模型的电力安全生产辅助决策技术。加大关键电力装备自主研发，加强新型防护材料研发，设立电力装备核心部件技术攻关专项计划，推动电力芯片、特高压组部件等关键技术突破。推动电力建设工程安全质量管控技术创新，研究建设电力建设工程智能化监管体系，运用人工智能、大数据等手段加强重点电力工程非现场监管和质量监督工作。
(十)充分发挥可靠性管理支撑作用
完善可靠性管理顶层设计，加快制定《电力可靠性管理办法(暂行)》配套法规制度，健全多方参与的电力可靠性管理体系。加强电力可靠性监督管理，深化推广基于全量自动采集的电力系统可靠性管理和低压供电可靠性管理，完善电力可靠性数据标准规范与数据质量管理制度。健全覆盖全环节的可靠性标准体系，完善新要素与新场景可靠性标准，强化标准与业务场景的深度融合。深化可靠性技术创新应用，将可靠性管理贯穿设备全寿命周期，探索人工智能大模型在可靠性管理中的应用。
(十一)提高依法治理水平
完善政策法规体系，加快《电力安全事故应急处置和调查处理条例》《国家大面积停电事件应急预案》《电力安全生产监督管理办法》《电力建设工程施工安全监督管理办法》《电力建设工程质量监督管理办法》《水电站大坝运行安全监督管理规定》等法规规章制修订，健全安全管理规范性文件和质量监督大纲体系。完善标准体系建设，修订《电力安全工作规程》《电力安全设施配置技术规范》等国家标准，完善涉网安全技术标准体系，推动发布施工强制性标准，及时制修订安全生产标准化规范或指南。加强行刑衔接，紧盯违法的企业实际控制人、最终受益人、幕后操控人，严肃查处安全生产非法违法和弄虚作假等行为，完善线索移交机制，有力发挥震慑遏制效果。提升安全监管效能，完善执法程序规定，提升监管的专业性和穿透力，强化进场监管、全方位监管。加强监管人员能力建设，注重由“查问题”向“查体系”转变。规范科学开展事故事件调查，通过事故调查、问题整改、验收销号、追责问责形成整改闭环。完善电力安全信息报送和事故事件调查处理机制。提高隐患排查整治质效，健全把重大隐患当作事故实施责任倒查机制。构建科学量化安全评价体系，推进安全监管从定性向定量转变。深化电力安全国际交流合作。
(十二)深化电力安全文化建设
推进“和谐守规、安全共治”安全文化重点工程建设，完善电力安全文化建设基本规范，大力开展电力安全科普基地建设和科普宣传。完善安全生产教育培训体系，规范从业人员技能培训与鉴定，加强电力设施保护宣传。提升电力安全文化建设评估能力，试点开展企业班组及员工安全文化成效评估。提升员工安全文化素养，建立电力安全管理优良传统标准规范，构建员工安全心理健康评估体系。
建立健全国家能源局牵头组织、各派出机构协同省级电力管理部门督促指导，电力企业、电力调度机构、用户及各类并网主体细化落实的协同工作机制。电力企业要细化分解行动任务，科学有序推进。加大要素保障，加强跨行业协同，强化电力安全治理的人才、科技、文化、数据等支持力度。强化监督评估，完善行动计划实施监测与动态评估机制，定期开展执行监测分析、风险预警，确保落地见效。

title: 实时感知、全域可视！中核环保“SMARP2.0”引领核电辐射防护新范式
content:
实时感知、全域可视！中核环保“SMARP2.0”引领核电辐射防护新范式
在核电辐射作业场景中，若能预先掌握各区域辐射剂量水平，是无数核电从业人员长久以来的期盼。如今中核环保旗下中辐院研发的“SMARP2.0”系统将这一愿景照进现实。
近日，中核环保所属中国辐射防护研究院完成SMARP2.0数字化辐射防护技术支持系统迭代升级。该系统可预先测算核电作业各区域辐射剂量水平，有效解决长期以来核电一线从业人员难以提前掌握现场辐射工况的行业难题，为辐射作业方案优化、工作人员辐射安全防护提供有力技术支撑。
“SMARP2.0”新一代数字化辐射监测核心装备“SMARP2.0”聚焦数字化辐射监测硬件装备升级，深度融合多传感器采集、5G通信以及厂区高精度定位等先进技术，构建新一代数字化辐射监测装备体系。系统完整覆盖工作人员进入控制区、现场作业、离场退出全流程，可远程、实时、快速采集人员剂量、场所剂量率、表面污染等辐射信息数据，打通物理厂区与数字平台的数据交互通道，构建动态联动的辐射防护“数实空间”，有效破解传统辐射监测数据滞后、现场管控存在盲区等行业痛点，助力核电现场管理提质增效、节约人力成本、提高辐射安全的感知能力和管控水平。SMARP2.0将为核设施辐射防护现场管理提供辐射数据智能感知、数据挖掘分析与防护仿真、风险预警与决策支持的数字化解决方案，推动我国核电厂辐射防护与安全管控向更高水平的智能化迈进。

title: 广东省省委常委、宣传部部长胡劲军到惠州调研：向海图强加快推动海洋经济高质量发展
content:
广东省省委常委、宣传部部长胡劲军到惠州调研：向海图强加快推动海洋经济高质量发展
近日，广东省省委常委、宣传部部长胡劲军到惠州调研，强调要深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于推动海洋经济高质量发展重要论述，贯彻落实省委有关部署要求，有序推进强台风“红霞”灾后恢复，在复工复产中筑牢根基，坚持向海图强，加快推动海洋经济高质量发展。
胡劲军一行先后前往广东省鳇鲸海洋生物科技有限公司、好招楼湿地公园、中国科学院两大科学装置、中广核太平岭核电站、洲明科技惠州大亚湾科技园等地，了解黄唇鱼种源保护与南海大黄鱼种业创新、海洋生态保护、大科学装置成果转化、重大能源项目建设运营、文化装备研发制造等情况，对相关工作给予肯定。
胡劲军强调，惠州要高标准高水平推进稔平半岛开发建设，推动省海洋经济高质量发展改革创新实验区建设早见成效。要依托中国科学院两大科学装置加速科技成果产业化，前瞻布局核技术应用产业。要强化重大能源项目示范引领，保障太平岭核电站安全稳定运营，不断夯实清洁能源基础。要聚焦文化装备制造，支持企业技术攻关，推动文化与制造业深度融合，为全省海洋强省建设贡献力量。
省有关部门负责同志，惠州市有关领导参加调研。

title: 生态环境部华东核与辐射安全监督站启动民用核安全设备安装单位防造假专项检查
content:
2026-08-07 16:21 来源：生态环境部华东核与辐射安全监督站
为压实民用核安全设备安装单位主体责任，切实做好防造假工作，近日，生态环境部华东核与辐射安全监督站(以下简称华东监督站)正式启动民用核安全设备安装单位防造假专项检查。
华东监督站系统梳理防造假要求，精心编制检查方案，制定了涵盖辖区内相关核设施的检查计划，确定宁德核电厂作为检查第一站。检查注重深入民用核安全设备安装单位现场项目部一线，确认相关单位是否按照法律法规及核电厂质量保证要求，建立并有效运行防造假制度。检查坚持问题导向，聚焦制度建设和措施落实两大关键环节：在制度层面，重点检查安装单位是否建立涵盖风险识别、过程管控、经验反馈等要素的防造假体系，核查项目负责人防造假管理责任落实情况;在措施层面，重点检查现场管控、内部调查、举报处理等方面的工作实效，并对焊接、无损检验等重要工序记录的真实性开展现场复核。针对检查发现的问题，华东监督站督促相关单位深挖根源，从严落实整改要求。
核安全是核事业发展的生命线，从业单位的诚信与透明，是其履行核安全主体责任的基石。面对核电建设运行“双高峰”带来的新挑战，华东监督站将继续保持监管定力，强化各领域全链条监管，提升监管效能，依托防造假专项检查等工作，推动全行业牢固树立安全发展理念，以高水平核安全保障核事业高质量发展。

title: 自主研发“缔梦”引擎赋能大亚湾核电实景三维孪生平台试运行
content:
自主研发“缔梦”引擎赋能大亚湾核电实景三维孪生平台试运行
近日，由大亚湾核电、中广核数科下属智科/仿真公司共同建设的大亚湾核电实景三维孪生平台试运行上线。该平台依托仿真公司自主研发的“缔梦”国产三维引擎，实现大亚湾核电基地三维模型、高斯泼溅、正向数据、GIS等多源数据融合。
“缔梦”引擎是仿真公司针对核电行业设备密集、系统关联复杂、数据分散等特点自主研发的图形开发工具，提供模型渲染、空间交互、物理仿真、数据驱动等底层能力。在此基础上，仿真公司联合大亚湾核电搭建实景三维孪生平台，基于引擎构建“厂区级—厂房级—设备级”三层数据体系，贯通设计、运维、管理各环节数据接口，实现全域数据实时映射与物理厂区、虚拟厂区的联动管控。平台支持厂房“云核查”及设备一键定位等功能，运维人员通过热点标签，10秒内即可完成设备定位并关联主要数据，而传统方式需跨系统逐级检索，平均耗时约3分钟，在平台帮助下单次设备信息查询工作量大幅减少，效率显著提升。
该平台是数字孪生技术在集团核电运维领域的首次全域落地。后续仿真公司将在此基础上扩展应用场景，推动数字孪生从单个基地试点向规模化复制，支撑集团数字化转型。该平台的试运行，标志着自主三维引擎为“虚实共生”的智慧运维赋能迈出了坚实一步，后期项目组将继续深耕数字孪生应用，将已有经验全面推广至多机组，同时新增视频融合、系统孪生、危化品管控、管道三维可视化等功能，做好数字化转型底座平台。

title: 陆丰核电1号机组常规岛首台主行车B车第一根主梁吊装就位
content:
陆丰核电1号机组常规岛首台主行车B车第一根主梁吊装就位
陆丰核电1号机组常规岛首台主行车B车第一根主梁于2026年8月7日8点45分开始起钩，11点31分就位。
这标志着1号常规岛主行车吊装工作正式开始;A/B主行车全部吊装工作预计于8月10日完成。
陆丰核电1号机组1号常规岛主厂房布置2台主行车，分别为主行车A/B，采用同层布置，起重量均为240t/40t，是核电厂重要的起重设备，在核电厂建造期间主要用于汽轮机、发电机、凝汽器、汽水分离再热器及凝结水泵等常规岛主设备和管道阀门等其他安装工作的吊装，在核电厂运行阶段则用于大修期间的汽轮发电机组维修与厂房内其他物项维修的吊装。

title: ITER测试包层模块进入初步设计评审关键阶段
content:
ITER测试包层模块进入初步设计评审关键阶段
国际热核聚变实验堆 (ITER) 测试包层模块 (TBM) 项目正推进聚变能源领域一项关键技术验证。测试包层模块面向未来聚变电站的增殖包层需求，目标是在反应堆运行条件下验证氚增殖相关方案，为聚变燃料循环自给提供技术基础。
在ITER总部举行的欧洲TBM初步设计评审会议上的合影。F4E-ITER组织
在聚变反应中，氘与氚发生聚变并释放高能中子。高能中子进入含锂包层后，可与锂发生作用生成新的氚，随后重新进入燃料循环。由于天然氚资源稀缺，增殖包层被视为未来聚变电站实现长期运行的重要内部组件。
ITER为该技术提供了接近反应堆条件的测试平台。根据TBM项目安排，不同机构正在设计四种测试包层方案。其中，欧洲参与研发两种方案：由欧洲聚变能源组织 (F4E) 牵头的水冷锂铅包层 (WCLL)，以及与韩国合作开发的氦冷陶瓷球床包层 (HCCP)。这些原型包层计划在ITER运行期间安装并接受测试，使研究人员能够评估其在相关工况下的性能。
F4E近期围绕两项欧洲TBM方案召开初步设计评审 (PDR) 会议。为支撑评审，F4E及合作伙伴团队为每个方案准备了150多份技术文件，覆盖设计、安全、质量和工程分析等内容。这些文件吸收了与ITER组织长期技术交流的成果，也纳入了实验室和供应商提供的分析数据。
F4E测试包层模块项目经理弗朗切斯卡·范蒂尼 (Francesca Fantini) 表示，TBM集成了先进材料和多项关键技术，其设计必须满足严格的核安全和质量要求。她说，相关设计建立在欧洲聚变实验室长期研发工作的基础之上，实验室提供了多学科专业支撑，项目团队也将工程经验反馈给研究机构，用于后续增殖包层研发。
由于TBM系统涉及范围广、技术复杂度高，项目推进依赖多方协同。F4E、韩国方面和ITER组织的专家多年来持续协调技术方案，并在合作中形成了较稳定的工作机制。范蒂尼表示，各方在近期会议中讨论了仍需解决的问题及应对计划，并有信心在年底前完成初步设计评审。
初步设计评审完成后，F4E团队将转入最终设计阶段，并推进新的模型开发合同。该项工作将进一步推动测试包层模块从科研设计走向工程化验证，也有助于欧洲在增殖包层这一聚变关键技术领域积累并保持专业能力。

title: Nuclea与New Mining签署备忘录，评估模块化反应堆为数据中心供电
content:
Nuclea与New Mining签署备忘录，评估模块化反应堆为数据中心供电
先进核技术企业Nuclea能源公司 (Nuclea Energy Inc.) 近日宣布，已与总部位于美国迈阿密的数字基础设施提供商新矿业公司 (New Mining Co.) 签署一份不具约束力的谅解备忘录，双方将评估利用模块化反应堆技术满足数据中心用电需求的可行性。
根据备忘录，双方将建立评估框架，研究在New Mining数据中心设施内或附近部署先进模块化电力单元的技术和结构可行性。相关评估分为两个阶段：第一阶段重点分析New Mining现有约30兆瓦电力负荷的数据中心工程需求;第二阶段则评估未来扩展至累计最高100兆瓦容量的可能性。
Nuclea首席执行官约瑟夫·弗罗因多费尔 (Josef Freundorfer) 表示，高密度计算基础设施正是该公司技术面向的用户侧供电应用场景。New Mining首席执行官丹尼斯·斯拉巴科夫 (Denis Slabakov) 表示，随着公司基础设施规模扩大，探索可靠、无碳的用户侧电力方案，是其运营发展的自然延伸。
New Mining目前在美国北达科他州和明尼苏达州运营比特币挖矿基础设施，总容量约65兆瓦。此次谅解备忘录并不构成购电协议，也不代表任何供电承诺。Nuclea不会运营任何核设备，若项目后续推进，发电和供电将由另行确定并签约的合格第三方公用事业公司或核电运营企业负责。
根据协议安排，Nuclea将提供技术咨询服务，包括其模块化反应堆设计的工程规格和监管策略;New Mining则将提供场址和用电数据，用于支持可行性评估。
Nuclea正在开发Morpheus微型反应堆。这是一种铅冷、石墨慢化的微型模块化反应堆，设计目标为工厂化制造，并可按需求在约3.5兆瓦电功率至50兆瓦电功率范围内扩展。
此次消息发布前，Nuclea已于2026年7月30日披露与Mangoceuticals公司 (Mangoceuticals, Inc.) 达成最终业务合并协议，拟借此获得在纳斯达克 (Nasdaq) 公开上市的渠道。

title: Rostec旗下RosEl交付首批Vulkan磁性接触传感器
content:
Rostec旗下RosEl交付首批Vulkan磁性接触传感器
俄罗斯国家技术集团公司 (Rostec) 旗下RosEl控股公司 (RosEl) 已向客户交付首批Vulkan磁性接触传感器。该产品面向高压蒸汽管道应用场景，可用于包括核电站在内的自动化和信号系统。
据介绍，Vulkan传感器安装在蒸汽管道阀门内部，主要用于监测和控制阀门关闭过程。该装置可在最高350摄氏度环境下工作，能够承受150g机械冲击加速度，并达到一级抗震等级，可在强地震条件下保持运行能力。
该传感器采用不锈钢外壳，设计寿命最长可达12年。其核心簧片开关无需外部电源，体积小于传统霍尔效应传感器，可靠性较高，设计动作次数最高可达50亿次。
RosEl方面表示，俄罗斯企业对其研发成果的采用，体现了相关产品在战略性行业中的应用价值。Vulkan传感器已被俄罗斯一家主要管道阀门制造商用于天然气、石油和核能工业，同时也可服务于电力和铁路工程领域。
簧片开关是一类应用广泛的基础元件，可用于家用电器、汽车、医疗、电信和安防系统等领域。在终端设备中，这类元件通常作为各类开关的触点组件使用。

title: SHINE入选美国能源部两项AI核燃料回收项目
content:
SHINE入选美国能源部两项AI核燃料回收项目
美国聚变能源企业SHINE公司近日入选美国能源部“创世纪使命” (Genesis Mission) 相关项目，将参与两项面向核能领域的人工智能应用工作。其中，SHINE将牵头一项核燃料循环设施优化项目，并参与由国家实验室和产业界共同推进的普罗米修斯项目 (Prometheus)。
SHINE牵头的项目名为“AI引导的燃料循环设施优化”，属于第一阶段项目，技术合作方为阿贡国家实验室 (Argonne National Laboratory)。该项目计划开发一套人工智能辅助工作流程，用于帮助工程人员优化乏核燃料回收工艺设计。该流程将综合评估工艺性能、产品质量和废物产生等因素，并记录不同设计取舍的依据，以替代逐项单独评估的传统方式。
据SHINE介绍，美国目前约有9.5万公吨乏核燃料。该公司正在开发相关回收技术，目标是从既有乏燃料库存中回收更多可利用材料。此次项目将在阿贡国家实验室长期研发的两项工具基础上推进：AMUSE用于模拟乏燃料分离化学过程，ARTEMIS用于模拟完整回收设施的系统集成。双方将在项目期间共同加入新的人工智能层，使工程人员能够评估更多设计方案，并筛选出更优方案。
除牵头第一阶段项目外，SHINE还将加入由爱达荷国家实验室 (Idaho National Laboratory) 牵头的第二阶段“普罗米修斯”项目。该项目旨在汇集国家实验室和产业界力量，推动人工智能在核能领域的应用。SHINE将提供其核燃料回收工作中的相关数据，并可提前使用普罗米修斯项目开发的工具，用于自身回收项目。
SHINE表示，公司正推进乏核燃料回收商业示范项目，相关工艺化学基础已在其Chrysalis医疗同位素设施 (Chrysalis) 得到验证。该医疗同位素设施也已完成美国核管理委员会 (NRC) 的完整运行许可证审查。SHINE认为，这些化学、工程和监管经验将为人工智能工具进入核燃料回收工艺设计提供基础。
SHINE创始人兼首席执行官格雷格·皮弗 (Greg Piefer) 表示，人工智能技术有望与商业放射化学运行数据结合，用于加快核燃料回收技术进展。该项目将在未来数月内推进;如进展顺利，同类方法还可能扩展至更多回收工艺环节。

title: 中国核安全与核工业代表团访问俄罗斯浮动核热电站
content:
中国核安全与核工业代表团访问俄罗斯浮动核热电站
7月28日至30日，中国国家核安全局、中国核工业集团有限公司 (CNNC)、中国驻俄罗斯使馆代表，与俄罗斯联邦生态、技术与原子能监督局 (Rostechnadzor) 负责人共同访问位于楚科奇自治区佩韦克市的浮动核热电站。该站隶属于俄罗斯核电运营公司 (Rosenergoatom)，后者为俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 电力板块企业。
访问期间，代表团实地查看了浮动动力机组及岸上设施，并了解主要设备运行情况。中方专家重点关注乏燃料贮存、换料流程及相关设备配置，同时就反应堆装置、汽轮发电机组的运行模式和技术参数进行了交流。代表团还了解了“罗蒙诺索夫院士号”浮动动力机组一回路、二回路相关工艺流程。
实地访问结束后，双方在“罗蒙诺索夫院士号”会议区举行工作会议。浮动核热电站站长维克托·叶拉金 (Viktor Yelagin) 向中方代表和Rostechnadzor负责人介绍了电站生产指标、技术经济特性、安全水平、在极北地区运行的经验，以及小型核能发电的发展前景。
Rostechnadzor副局长阿列克谢·费拉蓬托夫 (Alexey Ferapontov) 与叶拉金还围绕浮动动力机组核安全保障与监管问题，同来访代表进行了问答交流。费拉蓬托夫表示，随着国际原子能机构 (IAEA) “ATLAS”倡议推进，海上核能应用正进入新的国际发展阶段，“罗蒙诺索夫院士号”作为目前全球唯一在役浮动核动力机组，其运行经验对类似项目具有参考价值。
“罗蒙诺索夫院士号”位于俄罗斯楚科奇自治区佩韦克市，是全球在役的浮动小型核电站之一，也是目前位置最北的核热电站。该机组在不向岸上供热的情况下，可向佩韦克岸上电网输出约70兆瓦电力;在最大供热模式下，电力输出约为44兆瓦。俄方资料称，该站可为佩韦克及周边工业项目提供能源保障。

title: 俄罗斯北方机械制造厂推进“斯大林格勒”号破冰船主推力轴承生产
content:
俄罗斯北方机械制造厂推进“斯大林格勒”号破冰船主推力轴承生产
俄罗斯联合造船集团 (USC) 旗下北方机械制造厂 (Sevmash) 正在继续为22220型第六艘量产通用破冰船“斯大林格勒”号生产主推力轴承。
用于该船的一套轴承包括3个轴承部件。目前，其中两个部件已送至16号车间，开展轴承座加工;轴承滚道也在该车间进行加工和组装。第三个部件的壳体正在工厂船体焊接车间组装。
与此同时，北方机械制造厂4号车间专用区域正在进行轴承内部填充作业，包括制造带防摩擦层的衬套和轴承座，并填充热巴氏合金。每个部件需安装24个轴承座。这一环节是轴承制造过程中劳动强度较高的工序之一。
按计划，完成加工后，“斯大林格勒”号破冰船两个推力轴承的壳体和滚道将进入最终组装阶段，随后运往波罗的海造船厂 (Baltiysky Zavod)。整套部件计划于2027年完成。
轴承设计文件由北方机械制造厂设计局根据客户技术要求编制。该型轴承高度为2.5米，总装配重量约25吨，约20个工厂部门参与相关制造工作。
据了解，22220型“斯大林格勒”号是俄罗斯第六艘量产的22220型通用核动力破冰船，由俄罗斯总统普京于2025年11月在圣彼得堡波罗的海造船厂亲自授权铺设龙骨，船名取自二战中斯大林格勒保卫战的英雄历史，仪式上还将带有马马耶夫岗战斗遗址土壤的纪念舱安置在船上，该船总长173.3米、宽34米、高15.2米，轴功率60兆瓦，开阔水域最大航速22节，目前北方机械制造厂正按计划推进其主推力轴承生产，整套轴承部件计划2027年全部交付，建成后将进一步强化俄罗斯在北极航道的核动力破冰保障能力。

title: 俄罗斯国家原子能公司代表团考察塞夫拉奥放射性废物管理设施
content:
俄罗斯国家原子能公司代表团考察塞夫拉奥放射性废物管理设施
俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 代表团近日考察了俄罗斯联邦国家单一制企业“拉东” (FSUE RADON) 下属西北中心——塞夫拉奥 (SevRAO) 的生产设施。代表团成员包括负责放射性废物、乏核燃料以及核与辐射安全国家政策相关工作的瓦西里·季宁，以及综合核潜艇退役项目办公室主任谢尔盖·马尔蒂年科。
接待方由FSUE RADON代理总经理伊戈尔·普龙、塞夫拉奥代理主任德米特里·德罗日尔金，以及赛达湾和安德烈耶夫湾分支机构负责人尤里·绍欣、亚历山大·德拉甘等组成。
此次考察从涅尔帕造船厂开始。双方围绕处置由国防部门移交的核废物相关合作项目进行了讨论。随后，代表团前往赛达湾基地，查看核潜艇反应堆舱段储存区域，并重点了解2026年相关重点任务安排，其中包括将TUK-143相关装备从格列米哈储存设施转运至赛达湾储存设施进行长期储存的准备工作。
在安德烈耶夫湾核设施，专家组检查了乏核燃料移除后续处理工作的准备进展。相关人员表示，现场工作正按既定安全要求推进，核与辐射安全管理保持在较高水平。
访问期间，各分支机构负责人还汇报了工业安全、职业健康与安全、维修进度以及财务经济指标完成情况。双方讨论了FSUE RADON与Rosatom在履行国家国防订单方面的协作进展。
此次考察结束时，相关方面对工作成果进行了总结，并形成一系列管理决策，旨在推进国家国防订单执行，提高塞夫拉奥相关设施运行和管理效率。

title: 俄罗斯国家原子能公司完成首批能源关键信息基础设施产品认证
content:
俄罗斯国家原子能公司
KII-Sert
关键信息基础设施
俄罗斯国家原子能公司(Rosatom)近日根据“KII-Sert”自愿认证体系，完成首批面向燃料能源行业关键信息基础设施的产品认证。该认证体系自2024年起在俄罗斯核能和航天工业领域运行，主要用于评估关键信息基础设施相关解决方案的可靠性、技术独立性和可持续性。
此次认证由俄罗斯国家原子能公司工程板块旗下原子能工程设计股份公司(Atomenergoproekt JSC)实施。该公司作为“KII-Sert”体系内可信产品和流程的授权认证机构，与工业测试实验室自动化服务公司(Avtomatika-Servis LLC)合作，对一套用于油气行业的软硬件系统进行了认证。
认证评估覆盖可靠性、兼容性、功能性、技术独立性和可持续性等指标。评估过程中，专家对产品及其组件的全生命周期进行了审查，并结合核工业经验和油气行业应用特点，对软件、硬件、软硬件组合及相关组件的性能开展分析和测试。同时，认证工作还单独评估了开发、生产和运行流程是否符合技术独立性要求。
俄罗斯联邦能源部副部长爱德华·谢列梅采夫表示，KII-Sert认证并非一次性工作，而是保障燃料能源行业技术独立性和可持续性的系统性措施之一。后续将对认证结果进行分析，以确定该体系在能源领域进一步应用的方向，并研究建立覆盖行业的合格评定机制。
俄罗斯国家原子能公司信息与数字技术总监叶夫根尼·阿巴库莫夫表示，此次工作标志着KII-Sert体系运行进入新阶段，也为该体系向其他关键信息基础设施领域扩展提供了条件。该体系可用于确认可信解决方案是否符合行业要求，并为非进口产品的选择和应用提供评估机制。
KII-Sert自愿认证体系由俄罗斯国家原子能公司注册建立，目标是对关键信息基础设施相关解决方案开展认证，并保障认证结果的客观性和可靠性。该体系重点确认相关产品和流程是否符合技术独立性标准，以提升关键信息基础设施的持续运行能力。

title: 国际原子能机构发布小型模块化反应堆应急计划区技术文件
content:
国际原子能机构发布小型模块化反应堆应急计划区技术文件
国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 发布 TECDOC 系列第2134号技术文件《小型模块化反应堆应急计划区技术基础》(Technical Basis for the Emergency Planning Zone for Small Modular Reactors)。该文件2026年在维也纳出版，全文132页，包含11幅插图，语言为英语。
该文件是IAEA首次以出版物形式发布有关小型模块化反应堆 (SMR) 部署应急计划区技术基础的协调研究项目 (CRP) 成果。相关研究项目于2018年至2021年开展，重点讨论在SMR部署场景下，如何确定场外应急准备与响应 (EPR) 安排的技术依据，特别是应急计划区 (EPZ) 的设置需求及范围。
文件指出，SMR通常指单个模块电功率不超过300兆瓦的反应堆，其设计、安全和厂址特征与传统大型核电机组存在差异。这些特点需要在制定应急安排时加以评估。按照IAEA安全标准，应急计划区主要包括预防行动区 (PAZ) 和紧急防护行动规划区 (UPZ)，分别用于在核或辐射应急情况下采取预防性、紧急性防护行动，以避免或降低厂址外严重确定性效应，并减少公众受照剂量。
该出版物介绍了确定SMR应急计划区技术基础的方法、方法论和判据，涉及事故情景选择、源项分析、大气扩散模拟、剂量预测、公众暴露途径、人口组别以及国家剂量准则等因素。文件还讨论了SMR设计中纵深防御的实施情况，以及较低热功率、较小放射性释放、更大安全裕量、工程安全系统和裂变产物释放较慢等特征，可能对厂址附近公众潜在辐射照射产生的影响。
IAEA在文件中强调，SMR并非单一反应堆设计，而是一类涵盖不同功率水平、冷却剂类型、燃料组成、安全系统和模块化方案的技术集合。因此，不同SMR设计在源项、事故进程和场外后果方面可能差异较大，不能简单套用统一的应急计划区范围。
研究项目参与机构开展了多项案例研究。文件总结称，相关机构估算的应急计划区范围均低于IAEA现行指南中针对热功率不低于100兆瓦轻水堆提出的15至30公里紧急防护行动规划区范围，多数估算值小于15公里，部分最小估算值仅为反应堆周围数百米，并位于参与机构所称的厂址边界内。
文件同时指出，上述关于应急计划区范围的初步结论主要反映参与机构观点，多数基于预测的放射性后果，并不总是建立在完整危害评估和应急准备类别预先判定基础上。IAEA认为，未来在SMR应急安排研究中，还需进一步关注非电力应用、城市或偏远厂址、地下或浮动式部署、多模块同址布置、运输场景、概率安全分析方法以及模型不确定性等问题。

title: 日本女川核电站2号机一放射线量检测器误动作，读数数百次异常波动
content:
日本女川核电站2号机一放射线量检测器误动作，读数数百次异常波动
日本东北电力公司8月6日发布消息称，位于宫城县女川町和石卷市的女川核电站2号机发生检测设备误动作。出现问题的是用于测量主蒸汽管放射线量的检测器，主蒸汽管负责将反应堆产生的蒸汽输送至汽轮机。在4台检测器中，有1台在中央控制室显示的数值出现急剧上升和下降，并反复发生数百次。
从已公开的信息看，此次事件被东北电力定性为检测器误动作，而非放射性物质异常释放或反应堆运行状态突变。公司方面称，该情况不构成保安规定上的问题，意味着从运营方判断看，事件未达到需要按重大安全违规处理的程度。不过，放射线监测设备本身承担着异常识别和预警功能，读数频繁剧烈波动仍容易引发外界对监测可靠性的关注。
女川核电站2号机位于2011年东日本大地震和福岛核事故影响深远的东北地区，任何与放射线监测相关的故障都具有较高敏感性。即便运营方说明没有保安规定问题，公众仍会关心误动作的原因、持续时间、是否影响其他监测系统判断，以及是否存在设备老化、维护不足或信号传输异常等技术因素。
此次事件的关键在于后续信息披露是否充分。运营方需要说明故障检测器的具体排查结果、替代监测措施是否正常、其他3台检测器是否稳定，以及是否向监管机构报告并采取再发防止措施。对于核电设施而言，安全不仅取决于反应堆本体运行，也取决于监测系统能否持续、准确地向控制室提供可信数据。

title: 日本陆奥市同意乏燃料临时储存设施研究接收其他企业燃料
content:
日本陆奥市同意乏燃料临时储存设施研究接收其他企业燃料
日本青森县陆奥市8月7日通知东京电力控股公司 (TEPCO Holdings) 和日本原子力发电公司 (JAPC)，同意两家公司研究在当地乏核燃料临时储存设施接收其他电力企业乏核燃料的方案。
该设施由两家公司相关主体推动建设，是日本唯一一座位于核电站厂址之外、用于临时储存乏核燃料的设施。按照现行安排，设施仅接收来自东京电力控股公司和日本原子力发电公司的乏核燃料，其他企业的乏核燃料不得运入。
当天，陆奥市市长山本智也在市政厅会见两家公司高管时表示，希望两家公司重新研究相关计划，包括通过企业间合作接收其他公司乏核燃料的可能性，并提交修订后的运输方案。
此前，两家公司已向青森县政府和陆奥市提出请求，希望地方政府允许其研究接收其他公司乏核燃料的安排。日本电气事业联合会 (FEPC) 的统计显示，日本全国核电站乏燃料池总体已约八成满，乏核燃料储存空间不足问题日益突出。

title: 福岛第一核电站退役新规划：3号机组核燃料碎片取出前将优先内部调查
content:
福岛第一核电站退役新规划：3号机组核燃料碎片取出前将优先内部调查
日本原子力损害赔偿和退役等支援机构8月6日公布了2026年版《退役战略计划》概要，围绕东京电力福岛第一核电站退役工作的技术路径提出建议。计划重点提到，针对3号机组预计在2037年度以后启动的大规模熔融核燃料碎片取出作业，现阶段应优先推进反应堆厂房内部调查，以便为后续工程方案提供更可靠依据。
该计划认为，东京电力正在研究的核燃料碎片取出工法仍需要进一步提高确定性，而关键前提是掌握反应堆内部实际状况。由于事故后机组内部辐射水平高、结构损伤复杂，外部推测难以满足大规模作业所需的精度，因此应根据内部调查取得的信息，重新确认整体战略方向和技术路线。
根据计划内容，调查方式之一是使用此前已有应用实绩的无人机，从反应堆安全壳侧面的贯通部进入，对反应堆压力容器及其下方支撑结构等部位进行重点确认。这些区域被认为与熔融核燃料碎片的分布、堆积状态以及未来取出路径密切相关，也是决定设备设计和作业安全条件的重要基础。
计划还提出，应提高从安全壳上方开展调查的优先级。这意味着福岛第一核电站3号机组的退役工作将从单纯推进取出准备，转向更加重视前期信息收集和风险评估。对于长期且高难度的退役工程而言，尽早厘清内部状况，有助于降低后续施工的不确定性，并为2037年度以后可能实施的大规模取出作业奠定技术基础。

title: 纽克莱奥启动美国MOX燃料设施监管协商，先进堆燃料供应链建设提速
content:
纽克莱奥启动美国MOX燃料设施监管协商，先进堆燃料供应链建设提速
先进反应堆与核燃料企业纽克莱奥已与美国核管理委员会(NRC)启动混合氧化物(MOX)燃料制造设施的监管协商程序，计划在南卡罗来纳州萨凡纳河场址推进相关建设。这一动作意味着企业不仅在推进先进反应堆本体许可，也试图同步建立配套燃料供应能力，以降低未来商业化部署中的燃料瓶颈。
此次提交的监管协作计划属于正式申请许可前的重要步骤，核心在于提前与监管机构沟通设施设计、安全标准、审查范围和关键技术问题。纽克莱奥此前已在7月向NRC提交其铅冷快堆LFR-AS-200的监管协作计划，如今又将MOX燃料设施纳入同一监管节奏，显示其正在围绕反应堆和燃料端构建一体化许可路径。
MOX燃料由铀氧化物与从乏燃料等来源提取的钚氧化物混合制成，具备再利用核材料、提高资源效率的特点。纽克莱奥研发的铅冷快堆以液态铅作为冷却剂，目标是与MOX燃料结合，形成闭式核燃料循环。若该路线实现商业化，不仅可减少对天然铀开采和浓缩能力的依赖，也有助于降低最终需要地质处置的高放废物规模和长期放射性负担。
不过，MOX燃料涉及乏燃料后处理和钚材料管理，天然伴随辐射安全、核材料保障监督和核不扩散等敏感议题。因此，相关设施在美国落地必须通过严格审查，燃料制造、运输、安保以及与反应堆运行之间的衔接都将成为监管重点。对纽克莱奥而言，燃料设施许可与铅冷快堆许可能否协调推进，将直接影响其2030年代商业部署计划的可行性。
这一案例也为韩国等面临乏燃料储存压力的核电国家提供了观察样本。韩国虽已推进高放射性废物管理相关制度建设，但临时储存设施趋于饱和，乏燃料长期处理仍是能源政策中的关键难题。美国及欧洲企业加快布局快堆、MOX燃料和闭式燃料循环，显示先进核能竞争已从单一堆型研发扩展到燃料供应链与废物减量技术体系的整体竞争。

title: 美国核管会将首次在先进反应堆许可审查中采用现代化听证程序
content:
美国核管会将首次在先进反应堆许可审查中采用现代化听证程序
美国核管理委员会 (NRC) 将于8月13日在田纳西州橡树岭举行公开听证会，审议田纳西河谷管理局 (TVA) 拟在克林奇河场址建设小型模块堆的申请。这将是NRC首次在先进反应堆许可审查中采用现代化强制性听证框架。
根据NRC介绍，新的听证程序旨在让公众更早了解该机构对项目安全性和环境影响的审查情况，同时提高许可审查的透明度、可预期性和效率。作为许可审查现代化工作的一部分，NRC目前的目标是在18个月内完成建设许可证相关决定。
TVA计划在田纳西州橡树岭附近的克林奇河场址建设一台BWRX-300小型模块堆。该反应堆装机容量约300兆瓦，可提供无碳电力，是美国目前处于审查阶段的主要先进反应堆项目之一。NRC预计将于今年晚些时候完成该项目建设许可证审查。
NRC先进反应堆办公室主任杰里米·鲍恩 (Jeremy Bowen) 表示，新的程序有助于公众更早参与许可流程，并提高安全审查的透明度，也有利于对新一代核电厂作出及时、可预期的决定。
此次听证会将于当地时间8月13日17时在田纳西州橡树岭波拉德中心举行。会议将简要介绍NRC对该项目的安全评价和补充环境影响报告书，随后安排较长时间的问答环节。
强制性听证会是NRC新反应堆许可程序的必要环节，与允许提出正式法律质疑的“争议性”听证程序相互独立。NRC已于2025年7月公布对克林奇河项目申请提出质疑的相关机会。即使NRC最终颁发建设许可证，TVA仍需另行提交运行许可证申请，反应堆获批后方可开始发电。

title: 美国田纳西河谷管理局加速谈判拟在阿拉巴马Bellefonte旧址部署小型模块化反应堆
content:
美国田纳西河谷管理局加速谈判拟在阿拉巴马Bellefonte旧址部署小型模块化反应堆
美国田纳西河谷管理局(TVA)确认，正与产业伙伴就北阿拉巴马州长期闲置的Bellefonte核电站旧址开发新核能发电项目展开积极谈判。TVA临时首席执行官Mike Skaggs在田纳西州诺克斯维尔一场核工业会议上表示，相关谈判正在“快节奏”推进，重点包括与GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy合作，在阿拉巴马州Bellefonte以及田纳西州橡树岭Clinch River核址建设小型模块化反应堆。
TVA在声明中强调，目前尚未作出最终投资或建设决定，但正在评估多个潜在地点和技术路线。小型模块化反应堆被列为候选方案之一，GE Vernova Hitachi则是其正在接触的重要合作方，双方讨论的方向包括在Bellefonte部署多台BWRX-300机组。TVA称，这些谈判涉及其历史上最复杂的能源协议之一，目标是在田纳西河谷地区布局新核能设施，同时满足包括数据中心在内的新兴用电需求。
Bellefonte核电站位于阿拉巴马州Jackson县Hollywood，距离Huntsville以东约45英里。该项目曾是TVA大规模核电建设计划的一部分，但在投入14年和数十亿美元后，于1988年停工。TVA当年规划的17座大型反应堆中，有10座最终未能完工，Bellefonte正是其中之一。如今，随着美国电力需求增长和核能政策回暖，这一闲置资产重新进入开发视野。
此次谈判也与美国推动先进核能产业链发展的大背景相呼应。报道提到，特朗普政府此前推动了一项涉及日本对美国先进反应堆投资的400亿美元贸易安排。TVA希望通过Bellefonte等项目支持美国核工业增长，并建立未来核能开发模式。Skaggs表示，相关项目推进的可能性“相当不错”，显示TVA对新核能部署持较积极态度。
除Bellefonte外，TVA还在与总部位于休斯敦的Entra1 Energy讨论，在田纳西州Hartsville一处未完工核电站附近建设小型模块化反应堆。这表明TVA并非只押注单一地点，而是在多个历史核电资产和新技术方案之间进行布局，以提升电力系统的安全性、可靠性和韧性。

title: 美国聚变公司新增六项Texatron聚变技术专利申请
content:
美国聚变公司新增六项Texatron聚变技术专利申请
8月6日，美国聚变公司 (American Fusion) 宣布，已在美国新提交六项专利申请，涉及其专有Texatron聚变引擎平台的多个技术环节。至此，该公司在美国提交的专利申请总数增至82项。
美国聚变公司表示，这批申请延续了其围绕Texatron平台构建知识产权组合的策略，覆盖反应堆架构、等离子体约束、电磁系统、燃料输送、反应堆控制、电源管理，以及支撑Texatron聚变引擎后续开发和未来商业化的相关工程技术。
公司首席法务官迈克尔·G·史密斯 (Michael G. Smith) 表示，新增六项申请体现了公司保护Texatron平台核心创新的系统性安排。每项申请均对应一项具体技术方向，共同构成其紧凑型聚变能源技术知识产权布局的一部分。
此次新提交的六项美国专利申请包括：申请号19/754,260，申请日为2026年7月26日，名称为“带膛线环形腔室和电子脉冲控制器的聚变约束装置”;申请号19/755,767，申请日为2026年7月27日，名称为“带膛线环形腔室的单体聚变约束装置”;申请号19/755,778，申请日为2026年7月27日，名称为“带膛线环形腔室的蛤壳式聚变约束装置”;申请号19/755,781，申请日为2026年7月27日，名称为“带电子脉冲控制的单体聚变约束装置”;申请号19/758,937，申请日为2026年7月30日，名称为“膛线环形聚变系统架构”;申请号19/760,554，申请日为2026年7月30日，名称为“单体膛线环形聚变系统架构”。
除知识产权布局外，美国聚变公司还披露了企业和工程项目进展。公司已就211表格申请收到的最后一轮意见作出回应，目前正在等待后续审批结果。该公司称，完成211表格流程是其获得OTCQB市场报价资格所需的最后一个监管步骤，但仍需满足OTC Markets适用要求。
在工程测试方面，美国聚变公司正继续为德克萨斯理工大学 (Texas Tech University) 开展的Texatron测试项目下一阶段做准备。根据早期测试阶段收集的工程和诊断信息，公司科研及工程团队将推进更多评估工作，重点包括子系统验证、控制系统、点火系统、燃料系统、等离子体与磁场控制系统、电子元件，以及专用测试设备的持续校准和验证。
公司表示，下一阶段测试将用于进一步优化系统性能，扩大工程数据收集范围，并以分阶段方式支持Texatron聚变引擎开发。与此前测试相同，公司将在发布技术更新前，对相关工程和诊断信息进行审查与分析。
美国聚变公司首席运营官德怀特·卡特赖特 (Dewight Cartwright) 表示，工程团队正在为下一阶段测试稳步推进准备工作，每一轮测试都有助于验证系统性能、加深对平台的理解，并改进设备和测试流程。
公司首席技术官约翰·E·勃兰登堡博士 (John E. Brandenburg) 表示，先进能源技术开发需要严谨、有序的工程流程，每个测试阶段获得的技术信息将用于指导后续开发。公司预计，在知识产权、工程进展、监管事项和测试计划取得重要节点后，将继续披露相关进展。

title: 英国MAST升级装置第五轮实验创下等离子体压力纪录
content:
英国MAST升级装置第五轮实验创下等离子体压力纪录
英国原子能管理局 (UKAEA) 已完成其旗舰聚变实验装置MAST升级装置 (MAST Upgrade) 的第五轮实验。该轮实验在2025年至2026年期间于英国牛津郡卡勒姆园区开展，共产生超过1100次等离子体放电，并在克服等离子体不稳定性问题的同时，实现该装置迄今最高等离子体压力。
在聚变装置中，氢同位素需要被加热、压缩并约束在极高温和高压环境下。等离子体密度和温度越高，聚变反应越强，高压等离子体也更接近未来商业聚变电站所需的运行条件。UKAEA表示，本轮实验成果是其2026—2030年战略中的重点进展之一，目标是为聚变成为可部署的低碳能源建立科学基础。
本轮实验的核心任务之一，是抑制“边缘局域模 (ELM)”不稳定性。ELM是等离子体边缘的突发爆发现象，可导致等离子体压力下降，并在单次事件中释放最高可达储存能量十分之一的能量，长期可能损伤装置内壁和排气部件。若无法有效控制，频繁的壁面损伤将显著增加未来聚变电站的维护难度和成本。
MAST升级团队在此前实验基础上，采用准连续排气模式 (QCE模式) 和共振磁扰动 (RMP) ELM抑制模式，通过线圈施加三维磁场，降低等离子体边缘压力并保持稳定。团队还实现了静止H模式 (QH模式) 和I模式两种稳定运行状态。这些改进约束模式能够在提高能量约束性能的同时，缓解大型ELM带来的冲击。
实验还开发出一种等离子体位置控制技术。研究人员通过测量装置上下外偏滤器中氘释放出的可见光，实时识别微小的位置不平衡，并据此进行控制。UKAEA认为，这类自动化、实时控制方法对未来聚变电站运行具有重要意义，因为电站需要在尽量减少人工持续干预的情况下维持稳定运行。
在热负荷控制方面，团队利用MAST升级装置的Super-X偏滤器研究强热量和粒子排出管理。实验显示，向等离子体边缘注入少量氮气，可使等离子体将大部分废气能量以光的形式释放，在热量到达内壁和偏滤器前进行体积耗散，从而降低峰值热通量并减少内表面磨损。该研究也是在球形托卡马克紧密挡板Super-X双零几何结构内，对此类相互作用开展的首次详细研究。
本轮实验还探索了“负三角性”等离子体形状。该构型可在不发生ELM的情况下支持高功率运行，目前正受到国际聚变研究界关注。
UKAEA的MAST升级科学负责人詹姆斯·哈里森 (James Harrison) 表示，团队实现了包括QH模式、QCE模式和I模式在内的多种稳定高性能等离子体状态，并采用了新的等离子体位置控制技术，相关成果将对未来聚变电站设计产生影响。
这些实验结果已在由UKAEA于爱丁堡主办的2026年欧洲物理学会 (EPS) 等离子体物理会议上展示，并正与国际聚变界共享，用于支持英国球形托卡马克能源生产计划 (STEP) 和国际热核聚变实验堆 (ITER) 的设计与运行。
MAST升级装置今年还将继续增强，包括新增两个中性束注入器，使中性束加热能力翻倍，并安装电子伯恩斯坦波 (EBW) 系统，新增1.6兆瓦加热功率。该增强计划预计于2027年结束，第六轮实验计划于2028年开展，重点研究与STEP相关的课题。

title: 韩国泰雄公司推进美国泰拉能源SMR二号机组订单，发力核电与燃机锻件新赛道
content:
韩国泰雄公司推进美国泰拉能源SMR二号机组订单，发力核电与燃机锻件新赛道
韩国自由锻造企业泰雄正在加快切入小型模块化反应堆(SMR)供应链。资料显示，泰雄已于今年6月首次获得美国泰拉能源SMR一号机组主设备旋转塞部件订单，并预计在9月推进同一项目二号机组相关部件的追加订单。旋转塞安装在反应堆上部，用于支持核燃料更换及堆内设备维护，对材料耐高温、耐辐照性能和大型锻造能力要求较高，因此该订单不仅具有收入意义，也体现了企业在高端核电锻件领域的技术验证价值。
泰拉能源由微软创始人比尔·盖茨创立，正在开发以液态钠为冷却剂的第四代“钠”反应堆。泰雄若能从首台套供应延伸至后续机组，将有助于形成连续交付业绩，并提高其在北美先进核能供应链中的存在感。此前，泰雄还曾向GE日立核能的3.5代SMR“BWRX-300”项目供应锻造部件，参与加拿大相关项目建设，这意味着其已在不同技术路线的SMR项目中积累交付经验。
从公司战略看，泰雄正把核电及SMR业务作为摆脱传统单一需求波动的重要增长方向。公司表示，正在围绕核电产品质量可靠性提升，推进炼钢、锻造、检测和质量管理等环节的技术积累与知识产权布局。对于大型自由锻企业而言，SMR市场虽然仍处于产业化初期，但其部件标准高、认证周期长、供应链门槛强，一旦进入合格供应体系，后续订单黏性和长期合作空间较大。
除核电外，泰雄也在扩大燃气轮机大型锻件业务。目前公司正与三菱重工合作开发燃气轮机核心部件转子轴，整个研发项目共8个阶段，去年已完成第2阶段，今年启动第3阶段，并在上半年获得阶段性开发物量，产生部分销售收入。泰雄计划在2028年完成转子轴研发、2030年实现商业化，并提出燃气轮机转子轴业务年销售额达到1200亿韩元的中长期目标。
在全球电力需求增长、AI数据中心扩张以及能源转型背景下，SMR和高效燃气轮机都被视为未来电力基础设施的重要组成部分。资料还提到，美国得克萨斯州Encinal LNG联合循环电站项目可能成为韩国企业参与燃气轮机及发电设备供应的中长期机会。泰雄若能同时在SMR核电锻件和燃机转子轴领域取得突破，其发电装备业务有望成为继风电之后的新核心板块。

title: 韩水原"综合核电站维修员资格制度"获政府正式认可
content:
韩水原"综合核电站维修员资格制度"获政府正式认可
8月7日，韩国水力原子力(韩水原)宣布其“统一核电维修人员资格制度”已正式获得韩国雇佣劳动部下属韩国人力资源开发服务机构的政府认可。该认可意味着企业内部用于提升员工岗位能力的资格制度，在评价标准、运行体系和管理机制等方面得到了官方确认，也为核电现场设备运行与维修能力建设提供了更具公信力的制度基础。
此次获认可的制度，核心在于将过去由各核电维修合作企业分别运营的资格体系整合为统一标准。这是韩国核电维修领域首次形成此类标准化模型。为建立更贴近现场需求的评价体系，韩水原与核电现场人才培养机构合作，过去三年持续推进标准操作程序制定、考试题库开发、资格管理信息系统建设等工作，试图解决不同企业之间评价尺度不一、人员能力难以横向比较的问题。
从首轮考试情况看，新制度明显提高了准入门槛。上月实施的第一次核电维修人员资格笔试，覆盖机械、电气、仪控三大维修领域的10个核心项目，共有来自水山E&S、金和PSC、斗山能源等12家主要合作公司的133名优秀维修人员参加。最终合格率仅为25%，远低于此前各合作企业自行认证时超过70%的合格水平，显示统一制度更强调评价的区分度和专业性。
合格率下降并不只是考试难度提高，也反映出核电维修岗位对标准化、规范化和高可靠性的要求正在加强。核电设施运行安全高度依赖一线维修人员的技术水平和操作一致性，如果资格认证缺乏统一标准，可能影响人员调配、外包管理和现场质量控制。韩水原计划依据首轮评价结果，结合现场实务能力分析和应试者满意度调查，继续补充和修正评价体系，以提高制度的成熟度和可信度。
与此同时，韩水原近期还在拓展海外核电合作。该公司已于上月31日在庆州总部与菲律宾能源企业Aboitiz Power签署核电业务合作谅解备忘录，双方将围绕核技术信息交流、新建核电项目预可行性研究、教育培训、研讨会和工作层级协商机制等展开合作。国内维修资格体系的标准化建设，也可能为其未来参与海外核电项目提供人才管理和运维能力方面的支撑。

title: 首尔大学NEXFO研讨会：探讨SMR·MMR可持续发展解决方案
content:
首尔大学NEXFO研讨会：探讨SMR·MMR可持续发展解决方案
8月7日，首尔大学原子力未来技术政策研究所原子力政策中心宣布，将于9月16日下午在首尔大学全球工程教育中心举办“核能可持续性NEXFO工作坊”。此次活动适逢该中心成立10周年，以“迎接SMR·MMR全面启动时代”为主题，围绕小型模块堆和微型模块堆商业化进程中的政策、产业与技术条件展开讨论。
本次工作坊首先将重新审视核能可持续性议题的公共讨论框架，并分析全球核燃料循环趋势及韩国面临的国内课题。随着SMR、MMR从技术示范逐步走向实际应用，核燃料供应、乏燃料管理以及长期政策稳定性成为影响项目落地的重要因素，也关系到核能在碳中和背景下能否被纳入更稳健的能源体系。
下午的分组议题将进一步聚焦核燃料循环与安全监管。与会研究人员将讨论乏燃料管理政策方向、韩国与美国核安全监管制度改进趋势，以及先进反应堆开发过程中监管支持和政策协作机制的作用。同时，核电设计、制造和供应链管理体系的完善也被纳入议程，显示韩国核电产业正从单一技术研发转向系统性产业能力建设。
另一组讨论则围绕能源政策、经济性和未来技术展开，包括不同发电来源的经济性评估、系统平准化度电成本、碳中和目标下的最优能源组合以及核电利用方案。美国核能对外政策、下一代核能技术开发趋势和出口产业化战略也将成为重点议题，这反映出韩国在推动SMR、MMR发展时，不仅关注国内能源安全，也希望将其塑造成具备国际竞争力的出口产业。
此次工作坊的意义在于把SMR、MMR商业化所需的核燃料循环、安全监管、经济性、供应链和出口政策放在同一框架下讨论。对于韩国核电产业而言，未来竞争力不仅取决于反应堆技术本身，还取决于监管体系能否同步调整、乏燃料问题能否形成可执行方案、制造供应链能否稳定扩展，以及海外市场战略能否与国际核能政策环境相衔接。

title: 二〇二六能源经济与碳达峰碳中和高质量发展论坛举行--中国能源新闻网
content:

二〇二六能源经济与碳达峰碳中和高质量发展论坛举行
《人民日报》陕西榆林8月6日电 （记者顾仲阳、张丹华）2026能源经济与碳达峰碳中和高质量发展论坛8月6日在陕西省榆林市举行。论坛以“向新  向绿  向未来”为主题，搭建对话交流平台，共享绿色转型经验，为加快经济社会发展全面绿色转型、能源经济高质量发展进一步凝聚共识、汇聚力量。
与会嘉宾表示，推动经济社会发展绿色化、低碳化是实现高质量发展的关键环节，要深入学习贯彻落实习近平生态文明思想和习近平总书记关于碳达峰碳中和的重要论述精神，坚持降碳、减污、扩绿、增长协同推进，深入推进能源革命，把促进新能源和清洁能源发展放在更加突出的位置，以能源绿色转型支撑经济社会发展全面绿色转型。
中央和国家机关有关部委负责同志，地方政府、企业负责人和专家学者等参加论坛。论坛还发布了《榆林能源革命创新示范区创新实践研究报告（2026）》等成果。

title: 哈萨克斯坦首个储能项目并网 国家电投集团助力中亚新能源高质量发展--中国能源新闻网
